Create `desktop/lib/ws/windows_pipe_kernel32.dart`:

```dart
import 'dart:ffi';
import 'dart:math' as math;
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:ffi/ffi.dart';

import 'windows_pipe.dart';

/// The real [PipeIo]: kernel32, on the isolate that calls it. Only Windows
/// has it; elsewhere nothing calls this, and kernel32 is never loaded.
PipeIo kernel32PipeIo() => _Kernel32PipeIo();

const _genericRead = 0x80000000;
const _genericWrite = 0x40000000;
const _openExisting = 3;
const _fileFlagOverlapped = 0x40000000;

/// The daemon's end may only identify this process, never act as it: a
/// squatter on a dead daemon's name gets nothing to impersonate.
const _securitySqosPresent = 0x00100000;
const _securityIdentification = 0x00010000;
const _infinite = 0xFFFFFFFF;
const _waitObject0 = 0;

// What a finished overlapped call leaves in OVERLAPPED.Internal (ntstatus.h).
const _statusSuccess = 0x00000000;
const _statusBufferOverflow = 0x80000005;
const _statusEndOfFile = 0xC0000011;
const _statusPipeDisconnected = 0xC00000B0;
const _statusPipeClosing = 0xC00000B1;
const _statusPipeBroken = 0xC000014B;
const _statusCancelled = 0xC0000120;

/// OVERLAPPED on a 64-bit Windows (x64 and arm64), 32 bytes.
final class _Overlapped extends Struct {
  @IntPtr()
  external int internal;
  @IntPtr()
  external int internalHigh;
  @Uint32()
  external int offset;
  @Uint32()
  external int offsetHigh;
  @IntPtr()
  external int hEvent;
}

final _kernel32 = DynamicLibrary.open('kernel32.dll');

// The calls that return at once are leaf calls, and so is GetLastError, made
// straight after: nothing the VM does can come between them and change the
// thread's last error. The waits block, so they are not leaf calls, and what a
// read or a write did is read from the OVERLAPPED the kernel filled in, never
// from GetLastError after a wait.
final _createFile = _kernel32
    .lookupFunction<
      IntPtr Function(
        Pointer<Utf16>,
        Uint32,
        Uint32,
        Pointer<Void>,
        Uint32,
        Uint32,
        IntPtr,
      ),
      int Function(Pointer<Utf16>, int, int, Pointer<Void>, int, int, int)
    >('CreateFileW', isLeaf: true);
final _readFile = _kernel32
    .lookupFunction<
      Int32 Function(
        IntPtr,
        Pointer<Uint8>,
        Uint32,
        Pointer<Uint32>,
        Pointer<_Overlapped>,
      ),
      int Function(
        int,
        Pointer<Uint8>,
        int,
        Pointer<Uint32>,
        Pointer<_Overlapped>,
      )
    >('ReadFile', isLeaf: true);
final _writeFile = _kernel32
    .lookupFunction<
      Int32 Function(
        IntPtr,
        Pointer<Uint8>,
        Uint32,
        Pointer<Uint32>,
        Pointer<_Overlapped>,
      ),
      int Function(
        int,
        Pointer<Uint8>,
        int,
        Pointer<Uint32>,
        Pointer<_Overlapped>,
      )
    >('WriteFile', isLeaf: true);
final _getLastError = _kernel32
    .lookupFunction<Uint32 Function(), int Function()>(
      'GetLastError',
      isLeaf: true,
    );
final _createEvent = _kernel32
    .lookupFunction<
      IntPtr Function(Pointer<Void>, Int32, Int32, Pointer<Utf16>),
      int Function(Pointer<Void>, int, int, Pointer<Utf16>)
    >('CreateEventW', isLeaf: true);
final _cancelIoEx = _kernel32
    .lookupFunction<
      Int32 Function(IntPtr, Pointer<_Overlapped>),
      int Function(int, Pointer<_Overlapped>)
    >('CancelIoEx', isLeaf: true);
final _closeHandle = _kernel32
    .lookupFunction<Int32 Function(IntPtr), int Function(int)>(
      'CloseHandle',
      isLeaf: true,
    );
final _waitNamedPipe = _kernel32
    .lookupFunction<
      Int32 Function(Pointer<Utf16>, Uint32),
      int Function(Pointer<Utf16>, int)
    >('WaitNamedPipeW');
final _waitForSingleObject = _kernel32
    .lookupFunction<Uint32 Function(IntPtr, Uint32), int Function(int, int)>(
      'WaitForSingleObject',
    );

final _nothing = Uint8List(0);

final class _Kernel32PipeIo implements PipeIo {
  _Operation? _reading;
  _Operation? _writing;

  @override
  ({int handle, int error}) create(String path) {
    final name = path.toNativeUtf16(allocator: calloc);
    try {
      final handle = _createFile(
        name,
        _genericRead | _genericWrite,
        0, // no sharing
        nullptr,
        _openExisting,
        _fileFlagOverlapped | _securitySqosPresent | _securityIdentification,
        0,
      );
      if (handle == invalidPipeHandle) {
        return (handle: invalidPipeHandle, error: _getLastError());
      }
      return (handle: handle, error: 0);
    } finally {
      calloc.free(name);
    }
  }

  @override
  bool waitFree(String path, int timeoutMs) {
    final name = path.toNativeUtf16(allocator: calloc);
    try {
      return _waitNamedPipe(name, timeoutMs) != 0;
    } finally {
      calloc.free(name);
    }
  }

  @override
  ({Uint8List bytes, int error}) read(int handle, int max) {
    final op = _reading ??= _Operation();
    op.arm();
    final ok = _readFile(
      handle,
      op.buffer,
      math.min(max, pipeChunkBytes),
      nullptr,
      op.overlapped,
    );
    if (ok == 0) {
      final error = _getLastError();
      if (error != errorIoPending && error != errorMoreData) {
        return (bytes: _nothing, error: error);
      }
    }
    final status = op.finish();
    return switch (status) {
      _statusSuccess || _statusBufferOverflow => (
        bytes: Uint8List.fromList(
          op.buffer.asTypedList(op.overlapped.ref.internalHigh),
        ),
        error: 0,
      ),
      _ => (bytes: _nothing, error: _errorOf(status)),
    };
  }

  @override
  ({int count, int error}) write(int handle, Uint8List bytes, int offset) {
    final op = _writing ??= _Operation();
    final length = math.min(bytes.length - offset, pipeChunkBytes);
    op.buffer.asTypedList(length).setRange(0, length, bytes, offset);
    op.arm();
    if (_writeFile(handle, op.buffer, length, nullptr, op.overlapped) == 0) {
      final error = _getLastError();
      if (error != errorIoPending) return (count: 0, error: error);
    }
    final status = op.finish();
    return status == _statusSuccess
        ? (count: op.overlapped.ref.internalHigh, error: 0)
        : (count: 0, error: _errorOf(status));
  }

  @override
  void cancel(int handle) => _cancelIoEx(handle, nullptr);

  @override
  void close(int handle) => _closeHandle(handle);

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _reading?.free();
    _writing?.free();
    _reading = null;
    _writing = null;
  }
}

/// The Windows error for an NTSTATUS a read or a write finished with.
int _errorOf(int status) => switch (status) {
  _statusPipeBroken ||
  _statusPipeDisconnected ||
  _statusPipeClosing ||
  _statusEndOfFile => errorBrokenPipe,
  _statusCancelled => errorOperationAborted,
  _ => status,
};

/// One overlapped read or write at a time: its buffer, its OVERLAPPED and the
/// event the kernel signals when it is done.
final class _Operation {
  _Operation()
    : buffer = calloc<Uint8>(pipeChunkBytes),
      overlapped = calloc<_Overlapped>(),
      event = _createEvent(nullptr, 1, 0, nullptr);

  final Pointer<Uint8> buffer;
  final Pointer<_Overlapped> overlapped;
  final int event;

  void arm() {
    overlapped.ref
      ..internal = 0
      ..internalHigh = 0
      ..offset = 0
      ..offsetHigh = 0
      ..hEvent = event;
  }

  /// Blocks this isolate until the call is done; its NTSTATUS, or -1 when the
  /// wait itself failed.
  int finish() => _waitForSingleObject(event, _infinite) == _waitObject0
      ? overlapped.ref.internal & 0xFFFFFFFF
      : -1;

  void free() {
    if (event != 0) _closeHandle(event);
    calloc.free(buffer);
    calloc.free(overlapped);
  }
}
```

### Task C2.3: Transport integration (REST and the trusted WebSocket)

**Files:**
- Create: `desktop/lib/ws/trusted_pipe.dart`. It holds `TrustedPipe`, the HTTP/1.1 reader and `PipeSocket`.
- Modify: `desktop/lib/ws/local_daemon_transport.dart` (the `trustedPipe` field, `detect`, and the adapter's trusted-route branch).
- Modify: `desktop/lib/api/api_client.dart` (the `phoneSignInUnavailable` getter, inserted above `phoneSignInCode`). Do not run `dart format` on this file, because it is not formatted today and its unrelated lines would change.
- Modify: `desktop/lib/ws/ws_conn.dart` (`trustedLocal`, the pipe dial, `trustedPipeMissing`, `moveToTrustedPipe`).
- Modify: `desktop/lib/ws/ws_pool.dart` (`connFor(trustedLocal:)` and its key).
- Modify: `desktop/lib/state/app_state.dart`, in `_conn` only. It passes `trustedLocal`. Do not reformat this file either.
- Modify: `desktop/lib/ws/daemon_pipe_record.dart` (`readDaemonTcpPort`), `desktop/lib/ws/local_cli_discovery.dart` (`probe`) and `desktop/lib/sharing/shared_harness_panel.dart` (`_start`): the recorded loopback port, Steps 7–9.
- Create: `desktop/test/support/pipe_daemon.dart`, a stand-in daemon with the pipe's rules, plus `dialStandIn` and `writeDaemonRecord`.
- Test: `desktop/test/trusted_pipe_test.dart`, `desktop/test/daemon_tcp_port_test.dart`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes everything that C2.1 and C2.2 produce.
- Produces the names the header leaves to C2, stated here once:
  - `LocalDaemonTransport({String? candidate, TrustedPipe? trustedPipe, int? Function()? recordedPort})`, with `final TrustedPipe? trustedPipe` and `final int? Function()? recordedPort` (both null off Windows and under `flutter test`), `bool get trustedRoutesUnavailable`, `Uri tcpBase(Uri daemonBase)` and `Uri? refreshTcpBase(Uri daemonBase)`;
  - `int? readDaemonTcpPort({required String dataDir, required int port})`, in `daemon_pipe_record.dart`;
  - `class TrustedPipe { TrustedPipe({required DaemonPipeRecord? Function() lookup, PipeDialer? dial, Random? random, Duration timeout}); factory TrustedPipe.forPort(int port, {Map<String, String>? environment}); bool get unavailable; Future<PipeHttpResponse> request(String method, String path, {Map<String, String> headers, List<int> body}); Future<WebSocket> webSocket(String path, {Duration timeout}); Future<bool> probe(); }`;
  - `const trustedDaemonRoutes = {'POST /api/auth/handoff'}` and `bool isTrustedDaemonRoute(String method, String path)`;
  - `class PipeSocket extends Stream<Uint8List> implements Socket`;
  - `WsConn({…, bool trustedLocal = false})`, with `bool get trustedPipeMissing`, `Future<void> moveToTrustedPipe()` and `static const trustedPipeRetry = Duration(seconds: 10)`;
  - `WsPool.connFor(…, {bool trustedLocal = false})`;
  - `ApiClient.phoneSignInUnavailable`.

Rulings for this task:
- **dart:io.** `WebSocket.fromUpgradedSocket(Socket, {serverSide, compression})` takes any `Socket`. Its implementation uses only the stream, `addStream` and `close`. `Socket` is an `abstract interface class`, so `PipeSocket` implements it over a `PipeStream`. Dart forwards the private `_detachRaw` to `noSuchMethod`, and nothing calls it on this path. A prototype WebSocket over such a wrapper exchanged frames with a `WebSocketTransformer` server. `web_socket_channel` needs no loopback adapter: `IOWebSocketChannel(ws)` wraps the result as `ws_conn.dart` already does.
- **The upgrade.** It is written by hand: `GET`, `upgrade`, `connection`, `sec-websocket-key`, `sec-websocket-version: 13` and `x-harness-auth`. It sends no `Origin`, because the daemon refuses one. The 101 is accepted only when its `x-harness-proof` proves the token for that nonce, its `sec-websocket-accept` matches, and `upgrade` is `websocket`. The proof is checked before anything else, the status included. Compression is off, and none is negotiated. Bytes already read after the head go first into the WebSocket's stream.
- **REST.** One pipe connection carries one exchange. The adapter writes `content-length` and `connection: close`, reads the head, checks the proof on every answer, the 401 included, and reads the body by length, chunked, or to EOF. Node answers chunked when `writeHead` comes before `end`. The body is capped at 4 MiB, the CLI's `maxBytes`. A missing or unproven pipe becomes `DioException.connectionError`, which `phoneSignInCode` already reads as "none". A trusted route never falls back to TCP, where the daemon would only refuse it.
- **WS routing: this computer's window connection rides the pipe, and nothing else does.** The trusted frames cannot ride a second WebSocket beside the TCP one:
  - The daemon takes `daemon_*` only from a window, not a tool, bound to its own machine and not relayed. It takes `product_observe` only from a connection in `windowSinks` (`localWsServer.ts`).
  - A second connection would therefore have to `machine_select` as a second window. The daemon would count a second presence (`registerLocalClient`), and it would push every event, notification, `dial_status` and open question twice.
  - So the connection that `AppNotifier.sendDaemonFrame` already uses, the one bound to this computer, dials the pipe first on Windows and falls back to TCP. Relayed machines' connections and every other REST call stay on TCP, as the header says.

  How this compares with macOS:
  - macOS puts everything on its Unix socket, because a socket is a plain `Socket` and costs nothing more.
  - On Windows a pipe connection costs two isolates. Keeping relayed connections on TCP, where they need no trust, keeps the new I/O code on one connection.
  - Latency: each pipe read of up to 64 KiB reaches the UI isolate as one `TransferableTypedData` message, and each keystroke is one `SendPort` message plus one `WriteFile`. Neither adds a copy beyond the read buffer.
  - C5's E2E should time a busy terminal on the pipe against TCP with `cli/scripts/benchmark-terminal-latency.mts`. This is assumed for reconciliation.
- **Re-lookup and the squatter.** `TrustedPipe` reads the record and the token on every request, so a restart's new name is found next time, and a name the record no longer gives is never dialled.
  - An answer without the proof is `PipeUnproven`, and `unavailable` turns true.
  - `WsConn` dials the pipe on every connect.
  - When it had to land on TCP (`trustedPipeMissing`), each trusted send calls `moveToTrustedPipe()`. That asks `probe()` at most once per 10 s, and it drops the TCP connection when the pipe proves itself. The 1 s reconnect then dials the pipe.
  - This covers a TCP reconnect that won the race against the new record after a restart.
- **No liveness check of the pid.** B's CLI checks the recorded pid before dialling. The app does not, because nothing it sends before the proof is checked is secret:
  - an auth bound to the dead pipe's id with a one-time nonce;
  - the handoff's `{}` body;
  - an upgrade request.

  Nothing in an unproven answer is used. A's pid-plus-start-marker proof lives in `harness-pty`, which Dart cannot ask cheaply.
- **`product_observe`.** The desktop app sends none. It is `hn`'s measurement: `grep -rn product_observe desktop/lib mobile/lib` finds nothing. If the app ever sends one, it would ride the same trusted window connection.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the stand-in daemon**

Create `desktop/test/support/pipe_daemon.dart`. It serves on a Unix socket named `harness-<id>`, under the rules of B's pipe: a 401 without a proof, a dropped upgrade without auth, and a proof on every answer, the 101 included. It also has a lying squatter and a loopback-port double, and its `daemon_act` answers as `localWsServer.ts` does.

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:math';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:harness/e2ee/primitives.dart' show hmacSha256;
import 'package:harness/ws/windows_pipe.dart';

String _hex(List<int> bytes) =>
    [for (final b in bytes) b.toRadixString(16).padLeft(2, '0')].join();

String _mac(Uint8List token, int separator, String nonce) =>
    _hex(hmacSha256(token, [separator, ...utf8.encode(nonce)]));

final _auth = RegExp(r'^([0-9a-f]{64})\.([0-9a-f]{64})$');

/// A stand-in daemon for the pipe tests, on a Unix socket off Windows, as the
/// CLI's own tests stand one in for its pipe.
///
/// [trusted] serves as the daemon's pipe does (CLI `localSocket.ts`
/// `listenAuthenticated`): a request without a valid `x-harness-auth` for its
/// id gets a 401 without a proof, an upgrade without one is dropped, and every
/// other answer, the 101 included, carries the proof. [lies] answers every
/// request with a proof that is not the token's: whatever took a dead daemon's
/// name. Neither is the loopback port, which takes no auth and refuses what
/// needs trust, as the CLI's does.
///
/// Its WebSocket answers `machine_select` with `connected`, and `daemon_act`
/// as `localWsServer.ts` does: `UNSUPPORTED` from a trusted connection,
/// `LOCAL_SOCKET_REQUIRED` from any other.
class PipeDaemon {
  PipeDaemon._(this.server, this.id, this.token, this.trusted, this.lies) {
    server.listen(_serve);
  }

  final HttpServer server;

  /// The 32 hex digits its name ends with; empty for the loopback port.
  final String id;
  final Uint8List token;
  final bool trusted;
  final bool lies;
  final hits = <String>[];
  final refused = <String>[];
  final _seen = <String>{};
  final _sockets = <WebSocket>[];
  var selects = 0;

  /// Where it listens, as the record names it.
  String get path => server.address.address;

  /// The daemon's pipe, named `harness-<id>` in [dir].
  static Future<PipeDaemon> pipe(
    Directory dir,
    Uint8List token, {
    String? id,
    bool lies = false,
  }) async {
    final pipeId = id ?? _newId();
    return PipeDaemon._(
      await HttpServer.bind(
        InternetAddress(
          '${dir.path}/harness-$pipeId',
          type: InternetAddressType.unix,
        ),
        0,
      ),
      pipeId,
      token,
      !lies,
      lies,
    );
  }

  /// The daemon's loopback port.
  static Future<PipeDaemon> tcp() async => PipeDaemon._(
    await HttpServer.bind(InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4, 0),
    '',
    Uint8List(32),
    false,
    false,
  );

  static String _newId() {
    final random = Random.secure();
    return _hex(List.generate(16, (_) => random.nextInt(256)));
  }

  /// The nonce of a valid auth for this pipe, seen for the first time; or null.
  String? _admit(HttpRequest request) {
    final match = _auth.firstMatch(
      request.headers.value('x-harness-auth') ?? '',
    );
    if (match == null) return null;
    final nonce = match.group(1)!;
    if (!nonce.startsWith(id) || match.group(2) != _mac(token, 0x01, nonce)) {
      return null;
    }
    return _seen.add(nonce) ? nonce : null;
  }

  Future<void> _serve(HttpRequest request) async {
    final route = '${request.method} ${request.uri.path}';
    hits.add(route);
    String? nonce;
    if (trusted) {
      nonce = _admit(request);
      if (nonce == null) {
        refused.add(route);
        if (WebSocketTransformer.isUpgradeRequest(request)) {
          (await request.response.detachSocket()).destroy();
          return;
        }
        request.response
          ..statusCode = 401
          ..headers.contentType = ContentType.json
          ..write(jsonEncode({'error': 'PIPE_AUTH_REQUIRED'}));
        await request.response.close();
        return;
      }
      request.response.headers.set('x-harness-proof', _mac(token, 0x00, nonce));
    } else if (lies) {
      request.response.headers.set('x-harness-proof', '0' * 64);
    }
    if (WebSocketTransformer.isUpgradeRequest(request)) {
      final ws = await WebSocketTransformer.upgrade(request);
      _sockets.add(ws);
      ws.listen((data) {
        final frame = jsonDecode(data as String) as Map<String, dynamic>;
        final payload = frame['payload'] as Map<String, dynamic>? ?? {};
        switch (frame['type']) {
          case 'machine_select':
            selects++;
            ws.add(jsonEncode({'type': 'connected', 'payload': payload}));
          case 'daemon_act':
            ws.add(
              jsonEncode({
                'type': 'daemon_act_result',
                'payload': {
                  'requestId': payload['requestId'],
                  'ok': false,
                  'error': trusted ? 'UNSUPPORTED' : 'LOCAL_SOCKET_REQUIRED',
                },
              }),
            );
        }
      });
      return;
    }
    await utf8.decodeStream(request);
    final response = request.response..headers.contentType = ContentType.json;
    switch (route) {
      case 'POST /api/auth/handoff' when !trusted && !lies:
        response.statusCode = 403;
        response.write(jsonEncode({'error': 'FORBIDDEN'}));
      case 'POST /api/auth/handoff':
        response.write(
          jsonEncode({
            'success': true,
            'data': {'code': lies ? 'squatted' : 'hnh_pipe', 'expiresIn': 90},
          }),
        );
      case 'GET /api/status':
        response.write(jsonEncode({'pid': pid}));
      default:
        response.statusCode = 404;
        response.write(jsonEncode({'error': 'NOT_FOUND'}));
    }
    await response.close();
  }

  /// Stops, as a daemon that exits does: its WebSockets end with it.
  Future<void> close() async {
    for (final ws in _sockets) {
      await ws.close();
    }
    await server.close(force: true);
  }
}

/// A stand-in pipe, dialled: the Unix socket at a recorded path, as a
/// [PipeStream]. Nothing listening is [PipeAbsent], as on Windows.
Future<PipeStream> dialStandIn(String path) async {
  try {
    return _SocketPipe(
      await Socket.connect(
        InternetAddress(path, type: InternetAddressType.unix),
        0,
      ),
    );
  } on SocketException {
    throw PipeAbsent(path);
  }
}

class _SocketPipe implements PipeStream {
  _SocketPipe(this._socket);
  final Socket _socket;

  @override
  Stream<Uint8List> get input => _socket;

  @override
  void add(List<int> bytes) => _socket.add(bytes);

  @override
  Future<void> close() async => _socket.destroy();
}

/// Writes the record and token a core writes, naming [pipe].
void writeDaemonRecord(Directory dir, int port, String pipe, Uint8List token) {
  File('${dir.path}/daemon-$port.json')
      .writeAsStringSync(jsonEncode({'port': port, 'pipe': pipe, 'pid': pid}));
  File('${dir.path}/daemon-token').writeAsStringSync('${_hex(token)}\n');
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing transport tests, Review Focus 2 included**

Create `desktop/test/trusted_pipe_test.dart`. The restart, squatter and missing-pipe cases pin Review Focus 2:
- `a daemon restarted under a new pipe name is found on the next request…`;
- `a squatter on the recorded name…`;
- `a missing pipe falls back to the port, says the trusted frames are unavailable…`;
- `a squatter is never trusted, and asking again is bounded`;
- `a daemon restart moves the connection to the new pipe…`;
- `with no proven pipe the code is unavailable and never sent to the port`.

One more case checks that a pipe which never answers is given up within the timeout, and that its connection is closed, so a hung squatter leaves no blocked isolate behind.

```dart
import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:harness/api/api_client.dart';
import 'package:harness/auth/auth_session.dart';
import 'package:harness/core/config.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/daemon_pipe_record.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/local_daemon_transport.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/trusted_pipe.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/windows_pipe.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/ws_conn.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/ws_pool.dart';

import 'support/pipe_daemon.dart';

const _port = 28473;
final _token = Uint8List.fromList(List.generate(32, (i) => 255 - i));

/// The trusted routes over the daemon's Windows pipe, with Unix sockets named
/// `harness-<id>` standing in for the pipe (the CLI's tests do the same) and
/// [dialStandIn] for kernel32. The real pipe is integration_test/windows_pipe_test.dart.
void main() {
  late Directory dir;
  final daemons = <PipeDaemon>[];

  setUp(() async {
    // Socket paths are capped near 104 bytes; the default temp dir is longer.
    dir = await Directory('/tmp').createTemp('hpipe-');
  });

  tearDown(() async {
    for (final daemon in daemons.reversed) {
      await daemon.close();
    }
    daemons.clear();
    await dir.delete(recursive: true);
  });

  Future<PipeDaemon> start(Future<PipeDaemon> daemon) async {
    final started = await daemon;
    daemons.add(started);
    return started;
  }

  TrustedPipe trustedPipe() => TrustedPipe(
    lookup: () =>
        readDaemonPipeRecord(dataDir: dir.path, port: _port, isWindows: false),
    dial: dialStandIn,
  );

  Future<void> until(bool Function() done) async {
    for (var i = 0; i < 200 && !done(); i++) {
      await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 10));
    }
  }

  group(
    'TrustedPipe',
    () {
      test('sends a fresh auth and takes the answer it proves', () async {
        final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
        final pipe = trustedPipe();

        final answer = await pipe.request(
          'POST',
          '/api/auth/handoff',
          headers: {'content-type': 'application/json', 'x-adapter-local': '1'},
          body: '{}'.codeUnits,
        );
        expect(answer.status, 200);
        expect(String.fromCharCodes(answer.body), contains('hnh_pipe'));
        // A second request is a second nonce: the daemon takes each auth once.
        expect((await pipe.request('GET', '/api/status')).status, 200);
        expect(daemon.refused, isEmpty);
        expect(pipe.unavailable, isFalse);
      });

      test(
        'takes a body by length, chunked, or to the end of the connection',
        () async {
          // dart:io's server answers chunked unless told the length; the CLI's Node does both.
          final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
          writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
          final answer = await trustedPipe().request('GET', '/api/status');
          expect(answer.headers['transfer-encoding'], ['chunked']);
          expect(String.fromCharCodes(answer.body), '{"pid":$pid}');
        },
      );

      test('a daemon restarted under a new pipe name is found on the next request, and the old name is never dialled again', () async {
        final before = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, before.path, _token);
        final pipe = trustedPipe();
        expect((await pipe.request('GET', '/api/status')).status, 200);

        // The restart: a new pipe, a new record. The old name still answers —
        // as whatever took it would — and must not be asked.
        final after = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, after.path, _token);
        expect((await pipe.request('GET', '/api/status')).status, 200);
        expect(before.hits, ['GET /api/status']);
        expect(after.hits, ['GET /api/status']);
      });

      test('a squatter on the recorded name, answering without the proof, is no pipe', () async {
        final squatter = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token, lies: true));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, squatter.path, _token);
        final pipe = trustedPipe();

        await expectLater(
          pipe.request('POST', '/api/auth/handoff'),
          throwsA(isA<PipeUnproven>()),
        );
        await expectLater(
          pipe.webSocket('/api/local-ws'),
          throwsA(isA<PipeUnproven>()),
        );
        expect(pipe.unavailable, isTrue);
        expect(await pipe.probe(), isFalse);

        // The daemon is back under a name of its own: trusted again at once.
        final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
        expect(await pipe.probe(), isTrue);
        expect(pipe.unavailable, isFalse);
      });

      test(
        'a daemon that refuses the auth (another token) counts as no pipe',
        () async {
          final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, Uint8List(32)));
          writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
          await expectLater(
            trustedPipe().request('GET', '/api/status'),
            throwsA(isA<PipeUnproven>()),
          );
          expect(daemon.refused, ['GET /api/status']);
        },
      );

      test('no record, or a pipe that is gone, is no pipe', () async {
        final pipe = trustedPipe();
        await expectLater(
          pipe.request('GET', '/api/status'),
          throwsA(isA<PipeRecordMissing>()),
        );
        expect(pipe.unavailable, isTrue);
        writeDaemonRecord(
          dir,
          _port,
          '${dir.path}/harness-${'0' * 32}',
          _token,
        );
        await expectLater(
          pipe.request('GET', '/api/status'),
          throwsA(isA<PipeAbsent>()),
        );
      });

      test('a pipe that never answers is given up in time, and its connection closed', () async {
        final path = '${dir.path}/harness-${'1' * 32}';
        final silent = await ServerSocket.bind(
          InternetAddress(path, type: InternetAddressType.unix),
          0,
        );
        addTearDown(silent.close);
        final closed = Completer<void>();
        silent.listen(
          (socket) => socket.listen((_) {}, onDone: closed.complete),
        );
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, path, _token);
        final pipe = TrustedPipe(
          lookup: () => readDaemonPipeRecord(
            dataDir: dir.path,
            port: _port,
            isWindows: false,
          ),
          dial: dialStandIn,
          timeout: const Duration(milliseconds: 200),
        );

        await expectLater(
          pipe.request('GET', '/api/status'),
          throwsA(isA<PipeProtocolError>()),
        );
        expect(pipe.unavailable, isTrue);
        await closed.future.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 2));
      });

      test(
        'opens a WebSocket over the pipe once its 101 proves the daemon',
        () async {
          final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
          writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
          final ws = await trustedPipe().webSocket('/api/local-ws');
          final replies = StreamIterator(ws);
          ws.add('{"type":"machine_select","payload":{"machineId":"m1"}}');
          expect(await replies.moveNext(), isTrue);
          expect(replies.current, contains('"connected"'));
          await ws.close();
          await replies.cancel();
          expect(daemon.selects, 1);
        },
      );
    },
    skip: Platform.isWindows
        ? 'Unix sockets stand in for the pipe off Windows; Windows runs the real one'
        : false,
  );

  group(
    'over LocalDaemonTransport',
    () {
      ApiClient api(PipeDaemon tcp, LocalDaemonTransport transport) =>
          ApiClient(
            config: AppConfig(
              apiBaseUrl: 'http://unused.invalid',
              localCliBaseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:${tcp.server.port}',
            ),
            session: AuthSession(),
            localTransport: transport,
          );

      WsConn connFor(PipeDaemon tcp, LocalDaemonTransport transport) => WsConn(
        wsBaseUrl: 'wss://unused.example',
        autonomousEnv: 'prod',
        machineId: 'm1',
        accessTokenProvider: (_, _) async => '',
        onAuthFailure: (_) {},
        onEvent: (_) {},
        onStatus: (_) {},
        transportKind: WsTransportKind.localPlaintext,
        localWsUri: Uri.parse('ws://127.0.0.1:${tcp.server.port}/api/local-ws'),
        localTransport: transport,
        trustedLocal: true,
        fixedReconnectDelay: const Duration(milliseconds: 50),
      );

      Future<String> actRefusal(WsConn conn) async {
        try {
          await conn.request(
            'daemon_act',
            payload: {'id': 'say:1', 'choice': 'y'},
          );
          return 'answered';
        } on WsRequestFailure catch (failure) {
          return failure.code;
        }
      }

      test('the Add Phone code goes over the pipe, and everything else over the port', () async {
        final tcp = await start(PipeDaemon.tcp());
        final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
        final client = api(
          tcp,
          LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe()),
        );

        expect((await client.phoneSignInCode())?.code, 'hnh_pipe');
        expect(client.phoneSignInUnavailable, isFalse);
        await client.me().catchError((_) => <String, dynamic>{});
        expect(daemon.hits, ['POST /api/auth/handoff']);
        expect(tcp.hits, ['GET /api/auth/me']);
      });

      test('with no proven pipe the code is unavailable and never sent to the port', () async {
        final tcp = await start(PipeDaemon.tcp());
        final squatter = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token, lies: true));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, squatter.path, _token);
        final client = api(
          tcp,
          LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe()),
        );

        expect(await client.phoneSignInCode(), isNull);
        expect(client.phoneSignInUnavailable, isTrue);
        expect(tcp.hits, isEmpty);
        // The next ask looks again, and finds the daemon's own pipe.
        final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
        expect((await client.phoneSignInCode())?.code, 'hnh_pipe');
        expect(client.phoneSignInUnavailable, isFalse);
      });

      test(
        'off Windows nothing changes: no pipe, and nothing is unavailable',
        () {
          final transport = LocalDaemonTransport();
          expect(transport.trustedPipe, isNull);
          expect(transport.trustedRoutesUnavailable, isFalse);
          expect(
            LocalDaemonTransport.detect(Uri.parse('http://127.0.0.1:18473'))
                .trustedPipe,
            isNull,
          );
        },
      );

      test('this computer\'s window connection rides the pipe, where the daemon trusts it', () async {
        final tcp = await start(PipeDaemon.tcp());
        final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
        final conn = connFor(
          tcp,
          LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe()),
        );
        addTearDown(conn.close);
        await conn.connect();
        await until(() => conn.isReady);

        expect(daemon.selects, 1);
        expect(tcp.selects, 0);
        expect(conn.trustedPipeMissing, isFalse);
        expect(await actRefusal(conn), 'UNSUPPORTED');
      });

      test('a relayed machine\'s connection stays on the port', () async {
        final tcp = await start(PipeDaemon.tcp());
        final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
        final conn = WsConn(
          wsBaseUrl: 'wss://unused.example',
          autonomousEnv: 'prod',
          machineId: 'm2',
          accessTokenProvider: (_, _) async => '',
          onAuthFailure: (_) {},
          onEvent: (_) {},
          onStatus: (_) {},
          transportKind: WsTransportKind.localPlaintext,
          localWsUri: Uri.parse(
            'ws://127.0.0.1:${tcp.server.port}/api/local-ws',
          ),
          localTransport: LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe()),
        );
        addTearDown(conn.close);
        await conn.connect();
        await until(() => conn.isReady);
        expect(tcp.selects, 1);
        expect(daemon.hits, isEmpty);
        expect(conn.trustedPipeMissing, isFalse);
      });

      test('a missing pipe falls back to the port, says the trusted frames are unavailable, and moves back once the pipe proves itself', () async {
        final tcp = await start(PipeDaemon.tcp());
        final transport = LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe());
        final conn = connFor(tcp, transport);
        addTearDown(conn.close);
        await conn.connect();
        await until(() => conn.isReady);

        expect(tcp.selects, 1);
        expect(conn.trustedPipeMissing, isTrue);
        expect(transport.trustedRoutesUnavailable, isTrue);
        expect(await actRefusal(conn), 'LOCAL_SOCKET_REQUIRED');

        // The daemon's pipe is there now: the next trusted ask moves the connection onto it.
        final daemon = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, daemon.path, _token);
        await conn.moveToTrustedPipe();
        await until(() => daemon.selects > 0 && conn.isReady);
        expect(conn.trustedPipeMissing, isFalse);
        expect(transport.trustedRoutesUnavailable, isFalse);
        expect(await actRefusal(conn), 'UNSUPPORTED');
      });

      test(
        'a squatter is never trusted, and asking again is bounded',
        () async {
          final tcp = await start(PipeDaemon.tcp());
          final squatter = await start(
            PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token, lies: true),
          );
          writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, squatter.path, _token);
          final conn = connFor(
            tcp,
            LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe()),
          );
          addTearDown(conn.close);
          await conn.connect();
          await until(() => conn.isReady);

          expect(conn.trustedPipeMissing, isTrue);
          expect(squatter.selects, 0);
          final asked = squatter.hits.length;
          await conn.moveToTrustedPipe();
          await conn.moveToTrustedPipe();
          // One probe, not two: the second ask came within WsConn.trustedPipeRetry.
          expect(squatter.hits.length, asked + 1);
          expect(conn.trustedPipeMissing, isTrue);
          expect(tcp.selects, 1);
        },
      );

      test('the pool keeps the trusted connection apart: same flag, same socket; another flag, a new one', () async {
        final tcp = await start(PipeDaemon.tcp());
        final pool = WsPool(
          localTransport: LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe()),
          wsBaseUrl: 'wss://unused.example',
          autonomousEnv: 'prod',
          accessTokenProvider: (_, _) async => '',
          onAuthFailure: (_) {},
          onEvent: (_, _) {},
          onStatus: (_, _) {},
        );
        addTearDown(pool.closeAll);
        final uri = Uri.parse('ws://127.0.0.1:${tcp.server.port}/api/local-ws');
        WsConn conn({required bool trusted}) => pool.connFor(
          'm1',
          transportKind: WsTransportKind.localPlaintext,
          localWsUri: uri,
          fixedReconnectDelay: const Duration(seconds: 1),
          trustedLocal: trusted,
        );
        final trusted = conn(trusted: true);
        expect(trusted.trustedLocal, isTrue);
        expect(identical(conn(trusted: true), trusted), isTrue);
        final plain = conn(trusted: false);
        expect(identical(plain, trusted), isFalse);
        expect(plain.trustedLocal, isFalse);
        expect(trusted.isClosed, isTrue);
      });

      test('a daemon restart moves the connection to the new pipe, never the old name', () async {
        final tcp = await start(PipeDaemon.tcp());
        final before = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, before.path, _token);
        final conn = connFor(
          tcp,
          LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe()),
        );
        addTearDown(conn.close);
        await conn.connect();
        await until(() => conn.isReady);
        expect(before.selects, 1);

        final after = await start(PipeDaemon.pipe(dir, _token));
        writeDaemonRecord(dir, _port, after.path, _token);
        await before.close();
        await until(() => after.selects > 0 && conn.isReady);
        expect(after.selects, 1);
        expect(conn.trustedPipeMissing, isFalse);
        expect(before.hits, ['GET /api/local-ws']);
      });
    },
    skip: Platform.isWindows
        ? 'Unix sockets stand in for the pipe off Windows; Windows runs the real one'
        : false,
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write `TrustedPipe`, the HTTP reader and `PipeSocket`**

Create `desktop/lib/ws/trusted_pipe.dart`:

```dart
import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:math';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:cryptography/dart.dart' show DartSha1;

import 'daemon_pipe_record.dart';
import 'windows_pipe.dart';
import 'windows_pipe_auth.dart';

/// The daemon's routes that need its trust (CLI `hookServer.ts`, `isTrustedLocal`): on
/// Windows they go over its pipe and nowhere else. Over the loopback port the daemon
/// refuses them, so they are never sent there.
const trustedDaemonRoutes = {'POST /api/auth/handoff'};

bool isTrustedDaemonRoute(String method, String path) =>
    trustedDaemonRoutes.contains('${method.toUpperCase()} $path');

/// The daemon's answer over its pipe, its proof checked.
class PipeHttpResponse {
  const PipeHttpResponse(this.status, this.headers, this.body);
  final int status;

  /// Lower-case names, as Dio's adapters hand them on.
  final Map<String, List<String>> headers;
  final Uint8List body;
}

/// The daemon's Windows pipe as the trusted callers use it (spec §1.6).
///
/// Every request looks the pipe up again ([lookup]): the record names a new pipe on
/// each daemon start, so a restart is found on the next request, and a name the record
/// no longer gives is never dialled. Every answer must prove the daemon's token; one
/// that does not is [PipeUnproven], and that pipe counts as no pipe. [unavailable] says
/// how the last request went, for the callers' fallback copy.
class TrustedPipe {
  TrustedPipe({
    required this.lookup,
    PipeDialer? dial,
    Random? random,
    this.timeout = const Duration(seconds: 15),
  }) : _dial = dial ?? WindowsPipeConnection.open,
       _random = random ?? Random.secure();

  /// The pipe of the daemon on [port], from its data folder
  /// ([defaultDaemonDataDir]).
  factory TrustedPipe.forPort(int port, {Map<String, String>? environment}) =>
      TrustedPipe(
        lookup: () {
          final dataDir = defaultDaemonDataDir(environment: environment);
          return dataDir == null
              ? null
              : readDaemonPipeRecord(dataDir: dataDir, port: port);
        },
      );

  /// The daemon's pipe and token as its data folder says now, or null.
  final DaemonPipeRecord? Function() lookup;

  /// How long one request may take, from the lookup to the last byte.
  final Duration timeout;
  final PipeDialer _dial;
  final Random _random;
  bool _unavailable = false;

  /// Whether the last request found no pipe that proved itself. False before any.
  bool get unavailable => _unavailable;

  /// One HTTP/1.1 request over its own pipe connection. Throws a [PipeFailure]
  /// when there is no proven pipe; any status the daemon answers is returned.
  Future<PipeHttpResponse> request(
    String method,
    String path, {
    Map<String, String> headers = const {},
    List<int> body = const [],
  }) => _attempt(timeout, (record, pipe) async {
    final auth = _auth(record);
    pipe.add(
      _head('${method.toUpperCase()} $path', {
        ...headers,
        'content-length': '${body.length}',
        'connection': 'close',
        pipeAuthHeader: auth,
      }),
    );
    if (body.isNotEmpty) pipe.add(body);
    final reader = _HttpReader(pipe.input);
    try {
      final head = await reader.head();
      _prove(record, auth, head);
      return PipeHttpResponse(
        head.status,
        head.headers,
        await reader.body(head),
      );
    } finally {
      await reader.cancel();
      await pipe.close();
    }
  });

  /// A WebSocket to [path] over its own pipe connection: an HTTP/1.1 upgrade
  /// written by hand, its 101 proven, then dart:io's WebSocket on the pipe's
  /// bytes ([WebSocket.fromUpgradedSocket] over [PipeSocket]).
  Future<WebSocket> webSocket(
    String path, {
    Duration timeout = const Duration(seconds: 5),
  }) => _attempt(timeout, (record, pipe) async {
    final auth = _auth(record);
    final key = base64.encode(_randomBytes(16));
    pipe.add(
      _head('GET $path', {
        'upgrade': 'websocket',
        'connection': 'Upgrade',
        'sec-websocket-key': key,
        'sec-websocket-version': '13',
        pipeAuthHeader: auth,
      }),
    );
    final reader = _HttpReader(pipe.input);
    try {
      final head = await reader.head();
      _prove(record, auth, head);
      if (head.status != 101 ||
          head.value('upgrade')?.toLowerCase() != 'websocket' ||
          head.value('sec-websocket-accept') != _acceptFor(key)) {
        throw PipeProtocolError(
          'The Harness daemon did not open its WebSocket (HTTP ${head.status}).',
        );
      }
      return WebSocket.fromUpgradedSocket(
        PipeSocket(reader.remaining(), pipe),
        serverSide: false,
        compression: CompressionOptions.compressionOff,
      );
    } catch (_) {
      await reader.cancel();
      await pipe.close();
      rethrow;
    }
  });

  /// Whether a pipe proves itself now: one `GET /api/status`. Never throws.
  Future<bool> probe() async {
    try {
      await request('GET', '/api/status');
      return true;
    } on PipeFailure {
      return false;
    }
  }

  /// Runs one [exchange] on a fresh pipe connection, within [limit]. A pipe that
  /// does not answer in time has its connection closed, so nothing is left
  /// blocked on it. Any failure marks the pipe [unavailable].
  Future<T> _attempt<T>(
    Duration limit,
    Future<T> Function(DaemonPipeRecord record, PipeStream pipe) exchange,
  ) async {
    PipeStream? opened;
    var late = false;
    try {
      final value =
          await () async {
            final record = lookup();
            if (record == null) throw const PipeRecordMissing();
            final pipe = opened = await _dial(record.pipePath);
            if (late) {
              await pipe.close();
              throw const PipeProtocolError(_tooLate);
            }
            return exchange(record, pipe);
          }().timeout(
            limit,
            onTimeout: () {
              late = true;
              final pipe = opened;
              if (pipe != null) unawaited(pipe.close());
              throw const PipeProtocolError(_tooLate);
            },
          );
      _unavailable = false;
      return value;
    } on PipeFailure {
      _unavailable = true;
      rethrow;
    } catch (_) {
      // Anything else that went wrong on the way (an isolate that would not
      // start, say) is still no pipe to trust.
      _unavailable = true;
      throw const PipeProtocolError(
        'The Harness daemon\'s private pipe could not be used.',
      );
    }
  }

  static const _tooLate =
      'The Harness daemon did not answer on its private pipe in time.';

  String _auth(DaemonPipeRecord record) =>
      pipeAuthHeaderValue(record.token, record.pipeId, _randomBytes(16));

  void _prove(DaemonPipeRecord record, String auth, _HttpHead head) {
    final proof = head.value(pipeProofHeader) ?? '';
    if (!pipeProofMatches(record.token, pipeNonceOf(auth), proof)) {
      throw PipeUnproven(record.pipePath);
    }
  }

  Uint8List _randomBytes(int length) =>
      Uint8List.fromList(List.generate(length, (_) => _random.nextInt(256)));
}

Uint8List _head(String requestLine, Map<String, String> headers) {
  final text = StringBuffer('$requestLine HTTP/1.1\r\nhost: localhost\r\n');
  headers.forEach((name, value) {
    if (name.toLowerCase() != 'host') text.write('$name: $value\r\n');
  });
  text.write('\r\n');
  return Uint8List.fromList(utf8.encode(text.toString()));
}

String _acceptFor(String key) => base64.encode(
  const DartSha1()
      .hashSync(ascii.encode('${key}258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11'))
      .bytes,
);

class _HttpHead {
  _HttpHead(this.status, this.headers);
  final int status;
  final Map<String, List<String>> headers;
  String? value(String name) => headers[name]?.join(', ');
}

/// Reads an HTTP/1.1 answer off the pipe's bytes: its head, then its body by
/// Content-Length, chunked, or to the end; for an upgrade, the bytes after it.
class _HttpReader {
  _HttpReader(Stream<Uint8List> input) : _chunks = StreamIterator(input);

  static const _maxHeadBytes = 64 * 1024;
  static const _maxBodyBytes = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
  final StreamIterator<Uint8List> _chunks;
  Uint8List _buffer = Uint8List(0);
  int _at = 0;
  bool _ended = false;

  int get _left => _buffer.length - _at;

  Future<bool> _more() async {
    if (_ended || !await _chunks.moveNext()) {
      _ended = true;
      return false;
    }
    _buffer = Uint8List.fromList([..._buffer.sublist(_at), ..._chunks.current]);
    _at = 0;
    return true;
  }

  Future<String> _line() async {
    for (;;) {
      for (var i = _at; i + 1 < _buffer.length; i++) {
        if (_buffer[i] == 13 && _buffer[i + 1] == 10) {
          final line = latin1.decode(_buffer.sublist(_at, i));
          _at = i + 2;
          return line;
        }
      }
      if (_left > _maxHeadBytes) {
        throw const PipeProtocolError(
          'The Harness daemon sent too long a line.',
        );
      }
      if (!await _more()) {
        throw const PipeBroken();
      }
    }
  }

  Future<Uint8List> _take(int count) async {
    while (_left < count) {
      if (!await _more()) throw const PipeBroken();
    }
    final bytes = _buffer.sublist(_at, _at + count);
    _at += count;
    return bytes;
  }

  Future<_HttpHead> head() async {
    final status = RegExp(r'^HTTP/1\.[01] (\d{3})').firstMatch(await _line());
    if (status == null) {
      throw const PipeProtocolError(
        'The Harness daemon did not answer in HTTP.',
      );
    }
    final headers = <String, List<String>>{};
    var size = 0;
    for (;;) {
      final line = await _line();
      if (line.isEmpty) break;
      size += line.length;
      final colon = line.indexOf(':');
      if (colon <= 0 || size > _maxHeadBytes) {
        throw const PipeProtocolError(
          'The Harness daemon sent a malformed answer.',
        );
      }
      headers
          .putIfAbsent(line.substring(0, colon).trim().toLowerCase(), () => [])
          .add(line.substring(colon + 1).trim());
    }
    return _HttpHead(int.parse(status.group(1)!), headers);
  }

  Future<Uint8List> body(_HttpHead head) async {
    if (head.status == 101 || head.status == 204 || head.status == 304) {
      return Uint8List(0);
    }
    final out = BytesBuilder(copy: false);
    void keep(Uint8List bytes) {
      out.add(bytes);
      if (out.length > _maxBodyBytes) {
        throw const PipeProtocolError(
          'The Harness daemon\'s answer is too large.',
        );
      }
    }

    if (head.value('transfer-encoding')?.toLowerCase().contains('chunked') ??
        false) {
      for (;;) {
        final size = int.tryParse(
          (await _line()).split(';').first.trim(),
          radix: 16,
        );
        if (size == null) {
          throw const PipeProtocolError(
            'The Harness daemon sent a malformed chunk.',
          );
        }
        if (size == 0) {
          while ((await _line()).isNotEmpty) {}
          return out.takeBytes();
        }
        keep(await _take(size));
        await _take(2);
      }
    }
    final length = int.tryParse(head.value('content-length') ?? '');
    if (length != null) {
      if (length > _maxBodyBytes) {
        throw const PipeProtocolError(
          'The Harness daemon\'s answer is too large.',
        );
      }
      return _take(length);
    }
    // Neither: the answer runs to the end of the connection.
    if (_left > 0) keep(_buffer.sublist(_at));
    _at = _buffer.length;
    while (await _chunks.moveNext()) {
      keep(_chunks.current);
    }
    _ended = true;
    return out.takeBytes();
  }

  /// Whatever follows the head: the start of a WebSocket's frames.
  Stream<Uint8List> remaining() async* {
    if (_left > 0) {
      final first = _buffer.sublist(_at);
      _at = _buffer.length;
      yield first;
    }
    try {
      while (!_ended && await _chunks.moveNext()) {
        yield _chunks.current;
      }
    } finally {
      _ended = true;
      await _chunks.cancel();
    }
  }

  Future<void> cancel() => _chunks.cancel();
}

/// A [PipeStream] as the [Socket] that [WebSocket.fromUpgradedSocket] takes. The
/// WebSocket reads the stream and writes and closes the sink; nothing else of a
/// Socket applies to a pipe.
class PipeSocket extends Stream<Uint8List> implements Socket {
  PipeSocket(this._input, this._pipe);

  final Stream<Uint8List> _input;
  final PipeStream _pipe;
  final _done = Completer<void>();

  @override
  Encoding encoding = utf8;

  @override
  StreamSubscription<Uint8List> listen(
    void Function(Uint8List event)? onData, {
    Function? onError,
    void Function()? onDone,
    bool? cancelOnError,
  }) => _input.listen(
    onData,
    onError: onError,
    onDone: onDone,
    cancelOnError: cancelOnError,
  );

  @override
  void add(List<int> data) => _pipe.add(data);

  @override
  void addError(Object error, [StackTrace? stackTrace]) {}

  @override
  Future<void> addStream(Stream<List<int>> stream) => stream.forEach(_pipe.add);

  @override
  Future<void> flush() async {}

  @override
  Future<void> close() async {
    await _pipe.close();
    if (!_done.isCompleted) _done.complete();
  }

  @override
  Future<void> get done => _done.future;

  @override
  void destroy() => unawaited(close());

  @override
  void write(Object? object) => add(encoding.encode('$object'));

  @override
  void writeAll(Iterable<Object?> objects, [String separator = '']) =>
      write(objects.join(separator));

  @override
  void writeln([Object? object = '']) => write('$object\n');

  @override
  void writeCharCode(int charCode) => write(String.fromCharCode(charCode));

  @override
  bool setOption(SocketOption option, bool enabled) => false;

  @override
  Uint8List getRawOption(RawSocketOption option) =>
      throw UnsupportedError('A pipe has no socket options.');

  @override
  void setRawOption(RawSocketOption option) =>
      throw UnsupportedError('A pipe has no socket options.');

  @override
  int get port => 0;

  @override
  int get remotePort => 0;

  @override
  InternetAddress get address => InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4;

  @override
  InternetAddress get remoteAddress => InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Write the failing test of the recorded loopback port**

On a PC shared by two people, the first user's daemon holds 18473. The second user's daemon then binds another port and records it in `daemon-18473.json` (CLI `hookServer.ts` `allowPortFallback`, `lib/daemonRecord.ts`). macOS and Linux reach their own daemon through the socket named for 18473 whatever port it bound; Windows has no socket, so the app must read the record's `port`, as the CLI's own clients do (`savedDaemonPort`). Without it, the second user's app asks the first user's daemon, reads "a daemon for a different computer", never starts its own, and stays on "Starting local service…".

Create `desktop/test/daemon_tcp_port_test.dart`:

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:harness/core/config.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/daemon_pipe_record.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/local_cli_discovery.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/local_daemon_transport.dart';

// Windows, a PC with two people on it: the other user's daemon took the configured port first, so this
// user's daemon bound another and recorded it in daemon-<configured port>.json (CLI lib/daemonRecord.ts).
// The app follows the record, as the CLI's own clients do (savedDaemonPort), and never takes the other
// daemon for its own.
const _ours = '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef';
const _theirs = 'fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210';

/// A daemon for [computerId]: `/api/status`, and any other path says [name]
/// and the query it got. [hits] collects every path asked.
Future<HttpServer> _daemon(
  String computerId,
  String name, [
  List<String>? hits,
]) async {
  final server = await HttpServer.bind(InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4, 0);
  server.listen((request) async {
    hits?.add(request.uri.path);
    request.response.headers.contentType = ContentType.json;
    request.response.write(
      jsonEncode(
        request.uri.path == '/api/status'
            ? {
                'computerId': computerId,
                'localWs': {
                  'path': '/api/local-ws',
                  'protocolVersion': 1,
                  'terminalProtocolVersion': 3,
                  'e2ee': false,
                },
              }
            : {'via': name, 'query': request.uri.query},
      ),
    );
    await request.response.close();
  });
  return server;
}

void main() {
  late Directory scratch;
  late File identity;

  setUp(() {
    scratch = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('daemon-tcp-port-');
    identity = File('${scratch.path}/computer-id')..writeAsStringSync(_ours);
  });
  tearDown(() => scratch.deleteSync(recursive: true));

  LocalCliDiscovery discovery(int configuredPort, LocalDaemonTransport transport) =>
      LocalCliDiscovery(
        config: AppConfig(
          apiBaseUrl: 'https://harness-api.autonomous.ai',
          localCliBaseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:$configuredPort',
        ),
        identity: LocalMachineIdentity(computerIdFile: identity),
        transport: transport,
      );

  group('readDaemonTcpPort', () {
    void record(String text) =>
        File('${scratch.path}/daemon-18473.json').writeAsStringSync(text);

    test('is the port the daemon bound, from the record named for the configured one', () {
      record(jsonEncode({'port': 51234, 'pipe': r'\\.\pipe\harness-' + _ours, 'pid': 4242}));
      expect(readDaemonTcpPort(dataDir: scratch.path, port: 18473), 51234);
      expect(readDaemonTcpPort(dataDir: scratch.path, port: 18474), isNull);
    });

    test('is null with no record, or with a record that names no port', () {
      expect(readDaemonTcpPort(dataDir: scratch.path, port: 18473), isNull);
      for (final text in ['{"port":0}', '{"port":70000}', '{"port":"51234"}', '{}', '[]', 'not json']) {
        record(text);
        expect(readDaemonTcpPort(dataDir: scratch.path, port: 18473), isNull, reason: text);
      }
    });
  });

  test("discovery follows the recorded port past another user's daemon on the configured one, and so does REST", () async {
    final theirs = await _daemon(_theirs, 'theirs');
    final ours = await _daemon(_ours, 'ours');
    addTearDown(() => theirs.close(force: true));
    addTearDown(() => ours.close(force: true));
    final transport = LocalDaemonTransport(recordedPort: () => ours.port);

    final endpoint = await discovery(theirs.port, transport).discover();
    expect(endpoint?.computerId, _ours);
    expect(endpoint?.wsUri.toString(), 'ws://127.0.0.1:${ours.port}/api/local-ws');

    final daemonBase = Uri.parse('http://127.0.0.1:${theirs.port}');
    final dio = Dio(BaseOptions(baseUrl: daemonBase.toString()))
      ..httpClientAdapter = LocalDaemonHttpAdapter(transport, daemonBase: daemonBase);
    addTearDown(() => dio.close(force: true));
    final answer = await dio.get<Map<String, dynamic>>('/api/auth/me', queryParameters: {'a': '1'});
    expect(answer.data, {'via': 'ours', 'query': 'a=1'});
  });

  test('before the daemon has recorded a port, the configured one is not asked', () async {
    final hits = <String>[];
    final theirs = await _daemon(_theirs, 'theirs', hits);
    addTearDown(() => theirs.close(force: true));
    final probe = await discovery(theirs.port, LocalDaemonTransport(recordedPort: () => null)).probe();
    expect(probe.state, LocalCliProbeState.down);
    expect(probe.reason, 'the daemon has not recorded its port yet');
    expect(hits, isEmpty);
  });

  test('off Windows there is no record to read: the configured port is the port', () {
    final base = Uri.parse('http://127.0.0.1:18473');
    final transport = LocalDaemonTransport();
    expect(transport.refreshTcpBase(base), base);
    expect(transport.tcpBase(base), base);
  });
}
```

In `desktop/lib/ws/daemon_pipe_record.dart`, add after `readDaemonPipeRecord`:

```dart
/// The loopback port the daemon on [port] actually bound, from its record in
/// [dataDir] (`daemon-<port>.json`'s `port`; CLI `savedDaemonPort`), or null
/// when there is no record or it names no port.
///
/// It differs from [port] when another OS user's daemon held [port] at start
/// (CLI `hookServer.ts`, `allowPortFallback`): [port] then leads to that
/// user's daemon, never to this one.
int? readDaemonTcpPort({required String dataDir, required int port}) {
  try {
    final record = _regularFile(p.join(dataDir, 'daemon-$port.json'));
    if (record == null || record.lengthSync() > _maxRecordBytes) return null;
    final value = jsonDecode(record.readAsStringSync());
    final bound = value is Map ? value['port'] : null;
    return bound is int && bound > 0 && bound <= 65535 ? bound : null;
  } on FileSystemException {
    return null;
  } on FormatException {
    return null;
  }
}
```

4. After the `trustedRoutesUnavailable` getter, add:

```dart
  /// Windows: reads the loopback port the daemon actually bound from its
  /// record ([readDaemonTcpPort]). Null elsewhere, where the socket named for
  /// the configured port leads to this user's daemon whatever port it bound.
  /// Another OS user's daemon may hold the configured port; this user's daemon
  /// then binds another and records it (CLI `hookServer.ts`,
  /// `allowPortFallback`), and the CLI's own clients read it the same way
  /// (`savedDaemonPort`).
  final int? Function()? recordedPort;

  int? _tcpPort;

  /// [daemonBase] on the port discovery last read from the daemon's record
  /// ([refreshTcpBase]), or [daemonBase] itself.
  Uri tcpBase(Uri daemonBase) {
    final port = _tcpPort;
    return port == null || port == daemonBase.port
        ? daemonBase
        : daemonBase.replace(port: port);
  }

  /// Reads the daemon's record again and returns the loopback address to ask,
  /// as [tcpBase] then gives it. Discovery calls it before each loopback
  /// probe, so a daemon that restarted on another port is followed. Null on
  /// Windows while the daemon has recorded no port: the configured port may be
  /// another user's daemon then, so nothing is asked there.
  Uri? refreshTcpBase(Uri daemonBase) {
    final read = recordedPort;
    if (read == null) return daemonBase;
    final port = read();
    if (port == null) return null;
    _tcpPort = port;
    return tcpBase(daemonBase);
  }
```

```dart
  /// [options] aimed at the loopback port the daemon recorded, when that is
  /// not [daemonBase]'s ([LocalDaemonTransport.tcpBase]; Windows only).
  RequestOptions _onTcpPort(RequestOptions options) {
    final port = transport.tcpBase(daemonBase).port;
    final uri = options.uri;
    if (port == uri.port) return options;
    // The whole address goes in the path: Dio then ignores baseUrl, and the
    // query is already part of it.
    return options.copyWith(
      path: uri.replace(port: port).toString(),
      queryParameters: <String, dynamic>{},
    );
  }
```

```dart
    // Windows: the port the daemon recorded. Another user's daemon on the

      socketPath: null,
```

A `down` probe lets the supervisor start `harness start` after two quiet ticks, as for a daemon that is not running. A daemon writes its record as soon as it has bound (CLI `core/main.ts`), so a running daemon is never missed for long.

with:

```dart
    final base = Uri.parse(widget.notifier.config.localCliBaseUrl);
    // Windows: the port this user's daemon recorded (LocalDaemonTransport.tcpBase).
    final uri = (viewer == null
            ? widget.notifier.localDaemonTransport.tcpBase(base)
            : base)
        .replace(scheme: 'ws', path: '/api/local-ws');
```

### Task C2.4: Callers' fallback copy, and the real pipe on Windows CI

**Files:**
- Modify: `desktop/lib/daemons/daemon_brain.dart` (`trustedConnectionMissing`, `unreachableWords`, `privateConnectionWords`).
- Modify: `desktop/lib/screens/swarm_screen.dart` (the `_brain` wiring).
- Modify: `desktop/lib/state/app_state.dart`, in `sendDaemonFrame` and the new `daemonTrustedConnectionMissing`. Do not reformat the file.
- Modify: `desktop/lib/widgets/add_phone_dialog.dart` (`signInUnavailable` and the sentence under the QR).
- Test:
  - Modify `desktop/test/daemons/daemon_brain_test.dart`. Append one test, and do not reformat the file.
  - Create `desktop/test/daemon_trusted_pipe_test.dart`.
  - Modify `desktop/test/add_phone_dialog_test.dart` (`_open` gains `signInUnavailable`, plus one test).
- Create: `cli/scripts/windows-pipe-test-server.ts`.
- Create: `desktop/integration_test/windows_pipe_test.dart`.
- Modify: `.github/workflows/windows-desktop.yml` (C1.4's `build-test` job gains steps).
- Modify: `desktop/CLAUDE.md` (one paragraph in "Native desktop talks to the local `harness` CLI").

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes `WsConn.trustedPipeMissing`, `WsConn.moveToTrustedPipe()`, `ApiClient.phoneSignInUnavailable`, `TrustedPipe` and `WindowsPipeConnection`.
- Produces:
  - `DaemonBrain({…, bool Function()? trustedConnectionMissing})`, `static const unreachableWords` and `static const privateConnectionWords`;
  - `AppNotifier.daemonTrustedConnectionMissing`;
  - `showAddPhoneDialog(…, {bool Function()? signInUnavailable})` and `AddPhoneDialog.signInUnavailable`;
  - the CI step "Trusted pipe against a real daemon pipe".

Rulings for this task:
- **Add Phone.** With no proven pipe the dialog shows its QR as it does for an older CLI, with `e`, `m` and `c` but no `h`. Under "Scan with the Harness app." it shows one sentence: "Your phone will ask for a code from your email." It shows nothing more, so there is no transport jargon. The next renewal (60 s) asks again. When the pipe has come back, the code goes into the QR and the sentence goes away. On macOS and Linux `signInUnavailable` is always false, so nothing changes there.
- **The daemon's features.**
  - On Windows, `sendDaemonFrame` sends no `daemon_*` frame over TCP, where the daemon would answer `LOCAL_SOCKET_REQUIRED`. It returns false and calls `moveToTrustedPipe()`.
  - `DaemonBrain` then says `privateConnectionWords` where it said "harnessd is not reachable.":
    > keys and talk need harnessd's private connection, which is not open on this PC yet. the next one asks again.

    That is lowercase, as the surrounding brain copy is. It names `harnessd`, as every other line there does.
  - Presence frames are dropped quietly, as they are today when there is no socket. `DaemonPlateClient` keeps the species plate and asks again a minute later, as it does today.
- **The real-pipe test runs inside the app**, with `flutter test -d windows integration_test/windows_pipe_test.dart`.
  - `flutter test` treats any file under `integration_test/` as a device test (`_shouldRunAsIntegrationTests`), so it cannot run in the VM.
  - On a desktop device `flutter_tools` starts the app without a working folder, and with the parent environment merged in (`desktop_device.dart`). So `Directory.current` is `desktop/`, and `node` from `setup-node` is on the app's `PATH`.
  - The server is the daemon's own code, `listenLocalSocket` with a token, `attachLocalWsServer`, `ensureDaemonToken` and `saveDaemonPort`, run from the checkout with `node --import tsx`. It runs under `Directory.systemTemp`, which is in the profile as `secureState` requires, and on a random port in 28000–28999.
- **Which errors are proven.** `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` is proven on the real pipe, through a name nobody serves. So is a broken pipe as end of stream, through every 401 and the dropped upgrade. `ERROR_PIPE_BUSY` is proven through the fake handle layer only, since provoking busy instances on a runner is not reliable.

```dart
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/local_cli_discovery.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/ws_conn.dart';

import 'swarm_state_test.dart' show createApp;

/// This computer's socket, ready, and on the loopback port or its private pipe
/// as [missing] says ([WsConn.trustedPipeMissing]).
class _Conn extends WsConn {
  _Conn({required this.missing})
    : super(
        wsBaseUrl: 'ws://fixture.invalid',
        autonomousEnv: 'test',
        machineId: 'm',
        accessTokenProvider: (_, _) async => '',
        onAuthFailure: (_) {},
        onEvent: (_) {},
        onStatus: (_) {},
        transportKind: WsTransportKind.localPlaintext,
        localWsUri: Uri.parse('ws://127.0.0.1:1/ws'),
        trustedLocal: true,
      );

  bool missing;
  final sent = <String>[];
  var moves = 0;

  @override
  bool get isReady => true;

  @override
  bool get trustedPipeMissing => missing;

  @override
  Future<void> moveToTrustedPipe() async => moves++;

  @override
  Future<bool> sendTerminalFrame(
    String type,
    Map<String, dynamic> payload,
  ) async {
    sent.add(type);
    return true;
  }
}

void main() {
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  test('the daemon_* frames go only on harnessd\'s private connection; without it none is sent and the pipe is asked again', () async {
    final conn = _Conn(missing: true);
    final app = createApp(connectionForTest: (_) => conn, connected: true);
    addTearDown(app.dispose);
    app.machineStates['m']!.localEndpoint = LocalCliEndpoint(
      computerId: '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef',
      wsUri: Uri.parse('ws://127.0.0.1:1/ws'),
      protocolVersion: 1,
      terminalProtocolVersion: 3,
    );
    app.adoptPoolConnectionForTest('m', conn);

    expect(app.daemonTrustedConnectionMissing, isTrue);
    expect(
      app.sendDaemonFrame('daemon_act', {'id': 's1', 'choice': 'y'}),
      isFalse,
    );
    await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);
    expect(conn.sent, isEmpty);
    expect(conn.moves, 1);

    conn.missing = false;
    expect(app.daemonTrustedConnectionMissing, isFalse);
    expect(
      app.sendDaemonFrame('daemon_act', {'id': 's1', 'choice': 'y'}),
      isTrue,
    );
    await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);
    expect(conn.sent, ['daemon_act']);
    expect(conn.moves, 1);
  });
}
```

```diff
--- a/desktop/lib/state/app_state.dart
+++ b/desktop/lib/state/app_state.dart
@@ -788,10 +788,29 @@
       if (!machine.usesLocalTransport) continue;
       final connection = _pool?[machine.machine.machineId];
       if (connection == null || !connection.isReady) return false;
+      // Windows: harnessd takes these only over its pipe, and this socket rides the loopback port.
+      // There they would only be refused, so none is sent; the pipe is asked again instead, and the
+      // caller says why ([daemonTrustedConnectionMissing]).
+      if (connection.trustedPipeMissing) {
+        unawaited(connection.moveToTrustedPipe());

+  /// Whether the socket to this computer's harnessd is up but is not its private one, so the
+  /// `daemon_*` frames cannot go: on Windows, its pipe was missing or did not prove itself when the
+  /// socket connected ([WsConn.trustedPipeMissing]). Never true on macOS or Linux.
+  bool get daemonTrustedConnectionMissing {
+    for (final machine in machineStates.values) {
+      if (!machine.usesLocalTransport) continue;
+      final connection = _pool?[machine.machine.machineId];
+      return connection != null && connection.isReady && connection.trustedPipeMissing;
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Write the stand-in server from the daemon's own pipe code**

Create `cli/scripts/windows-pipe-test-server.ts`. Off Windows it listens on Unix sockets named like pipes, so it can be checked on a Mac.

```ts
/**
 * A stand-in daemon on the daemon's own pipe code, for the desktop app's real-pipe test
 * (desktop/integration_test/windows_pipe_test.dart). Built from the daemon's pieces, as daemonPipe.real.spec.ts is:
 * lib/localSocket.ts's authenticated pipe, localWsServer.ts's local WebSocket on it, and the token and record the
 * core writes (pipeAuth.ts `ensureDaemonToken`, daemonEndpoint.ts `saveDaemonPort`). Beside it, a squatter: a plain
 * HTTP server on another harness-<id> pipe that answers everything, its 101 included, with a proof that is not the
 * token's — whatever took a dead daemon's name.
 *
 * On Windows both are named pipes. Elsewhere they are Unix sockets named like one in the data folder, as the CLI's
 * own tests stand a pipe in, so the script can be tried on a Mac.
 *
 * Run from cli/: node --import tsx scripts/windows-pipe-test-server.ts <throwaway data folder> <port>
 * It prints one JSON line once everything listens — { pipe, squatter, tcpPort, machineId } — and stops when its stdin
 * closes. It refuses port 18473: the real daemon's.
 */
import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'
import http from 'node:http'
import type { AddressInfo } from 'node:net'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { WebSocketServer } from 'ws'
import { attachLocalWsServer, type LocalWsBackend } from '../src/localWsServer.js'
import { saveDaemonPort } from '../src/lib/daemonEndpoint.js'
import { listenLocalSocket } from '../src/lib/localSocket.js'
import { ensureDaemonToken, newPipePath, PIPE_PROOF_HEADER } from '../src/lib/windows/pipeAuth.js'

const [dataDir, portText] = process.argv.slice(2)
const port = Number(portText)
if (!dataDir || !Number.isInteger(port) || port <= 0 || port > 65535 || port === 18473) {
  console.error('usage: windows-pipe-test-server.ts <throwaway data folder> <port, not 18473>')
  process.exit(2)
}

const machineId = 'pipe-test-machine'
const pipeName = (): string => process.platform === 'win32' ? newPipePath() : join(dataDir, `harness-${randomBytes(16).toString('hex')}`)
const json = (res: http.ServerResponse, status: number, body: unknown): void => {
  res.writeHead(status, { 'content-type': 'application/json' })
  res.end(JSON.stringify(body))
}

const token = ensureDaemonToken(dataDir)
const pipePath = pipeName()
const pipe = await listenLocalSocket((req, res) => {
  const route = `${req.method} ${(req.url ?? '').split('?')[0]}`
  if (route === 'POST /api/auth/handoff') json(res, 200, { success: true, data: { code: 'hnh_pipe_test', expiresIn: 90 } })
  else if (route === 'GET /api/status') json(res, 200, { pid: process.pid })
  else json(res, 404, { error: 'NOT_FOUND' })
}, pipePath, { token })

// The loopback port, with the same local WebSocket: the app's fallback.
const backend: LocalWsBackend = { registerLocalClient: () => true, unregisterLocalClient: async () => {}, handleLocalFrame: () => {}, handleLocalBinary: async () => {} }
const tcp = http.createServer((_req, res) => json(res, 404, { error: 'NOT_FOUND' }))
await new Promise<void>((resolve) => tcp.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve))
const local = attachLocalWsServer(tcp, { machineId, backend, localSocketServer: pipe.server })
const tcpPort = (tcp.address() as AddressInfo).port
saveDaemonPort(dataDir, port, tcpPort, { pipe: pipePath, pid: process.pid })

const wrongProof = '0'.repeat(64)
const squatterPath = pipeName()
const squatter = http.createServer((_req, res) => {
  res.setHeader(PIPE_PROOF_HEADER, wrongProof)
  json(res, 200, { success: true, data: { code: 'squatted', expiresIn: 90 } })
})
const squatterWs = new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })
squatterWs.on('headers', (headers) => headers.push(`${PIPE_PROOF_HEADER}: ${wrongProof}`))
squatter.on('upgrade', (req, socket, head) => squatterWs.handleUpgrade(req, socket, head, (ws) => {
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'connected', payload: { machineId } }))
}))
await new Promise<void>((resolve) => squatter.listen(squatterPath, resolve))

console.log(JSON.stringify({ pipe: pipePath, squatter: squatterPath, tcpPort, machineId }))

process.stdin.resume()
process.stdin.on('end', () => {
  squatterWs.close()
  squatter.close()
  local.close()
  tcp.close()
  void pipe.close().then(() => process.exit(0))
})
```

Check it on the Mac. It needs `npm ci` in `cli/`.
