- [ ] **Step 7: Write the real-pipe integration test**

Create `desktop/integration_test/windows_pipe_test.dart`:

```dart
// The trusted pipe against the daemon's own pipe code, on a real Windows named pipe, from inside the
// app: cli/scripts/windows-pipe-test-server.ts serves lib/localSocket.ts's authenticated pipe and
// localWsServer.ts's WebSocket from this checkout, under a throwaway data folder and port, never the
// real %USERPROFILE%\.harness or 18473, and the app dials it with its kernel32 client
// (lib/ws/windows_pipe.dart). Windows only; the Windows desktop workflow's build-test job runs it:
//
//   cd cli && npm ci && cd ../desktop && flutter test -d windows integration_test/windows_pipe_test.dart
import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:math';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:harness/api/api_client.dart';
import 'package:harness/auth/auth_session.dart';
import 'package:harness/core/config.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/daemon_pipe_record.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/local_daemon_transport.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/trusted_pipe.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/windows_pipe.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/windows_pipe_auth.dart';
import 'package:harness/ws/ws_conn.dart';
import 'package:integration_test/integration_test.dart';
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;

void main() {
  IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  group(
    'on a real Windows pipe',
    () {
      late Directory dataDir;
      late Process server;
      late String pipePath;
      late String squatterPath;
      late int tcpPort;
      late String machineId;
      // A throwaway port: the record is named for it. Never the real daemon's 18473.
      final port = 28000 + Random().nextInt(1000);

      setUpAll(() async {
        // %TEMP% is in the profile, where the daemon's token may live (secureState.ts).
        dataDir = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('hpipe-');
        server = await Process.start(
          'node',
          [
            '--import',
            'tsx',
            'scripts/windows-pipe-test-server.ts',
            dataDir.path,
            '$port',
          ],
          workingDirectory: p.normalize(
            p.join(Directory.current.path, '..', 'cli'),
          ),
        );
        unawaited(server.stderr.transform(utf8.decoder).forEach(stderr.write));
        final ready = jsonDecode(
          await server.stdout
              .transform(utf8.decoder)
              .transform(const LineSplitter())
              .first
              .timeout(const Duration(seconds: 60)),
        ) as Map<String, dynamic>;
        pipePath = ready['pipe'] as String;
        squatterPath = ready['squatter'] as String;
        tcpPort = ready['tcpPort'] as int;
        machineId = ready['machineId'] as String;
      });

      tearDownAll(() async {
        await server.stdin.close();
        await server.exitCode.timeout(
          const Duration(seconds: 10),
          onTimeout: () {
            server.kill();
            return -1;
          },
        );
        dataDir.deleteSync(recursive: true);
      });

      /// Points the record at [pipe], as a restart, or a stale record a squatter took over, would.
      void recordNames(String pipe) =>
          File(p.join(dataDir.path, 'daemon-$port.json')).writeAsStringSync(
            jsonEncode({'port': tcpPort, 'pipe': pipe, 'pid': server.pid}),
          );

      TrustedPipe trustedPipe() => TrustedPipe(
        lookup: () => readDaemonPipeRecord(dataDir: dataDir.path, port: port),
      );

      ApiClient api(LocalDaemonTransport transport) => ApiClient(
        config: AppConfig(
          apiBaseUrl: 'http://unused.invalid',
          localCliBaseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:$tcpPort',
        ),
        session: AuthSession(),
        localTransport: transport,
      );

      WsConn conn(LocalDaemonTransport transport, {bool trusted = true}) =>
          WsConn(
            wsBaseUrl: 'wss://unused.example',
            autonomousEnv: 'prod',
            machineId: machineId,
            accessTokenProvider: (_, _) async => '',
            onAuthFailure: (_) {},
            onEvent: (_) {},
            onStatus: (_) {},
            transportKind: WsTransportKind.localPlaintext,
            localWsUri: Uri.parse('ws://127.0.0.1:$tcpPort/api/local-ws'),
            localTransport: transport,
            trustedLocal: trusted,
            fixedReconnectDelay: const Duration(milliseconds: 200),
          );

      Future<void> ready(WsConn connection) =>
          connection.waitUntilReady(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 20));

      /// What the daemon says to a key from [connection]: `UNSUPPORTED` from a trusted window,
      /// `LOCAL_SOCKET_REQUIRED` from any other (localWsServer.ts).
      Future<String> actRefusal(WsConn connection) async {
        try {
          await connection.request(
            'daemon_act',
            payload: {'id': 'say:1', 'choice': 'y'},
          );
          return 'answered';
        } on WsRequestFailure catch (failure) {
          return failure.code;
        }
      }

      /// One raw exchange on the pipe: what came back before the daemon closed its end.
      Future<String> raw(String request) async {
        final connection = await WindowsPipeConnection.open(pipePath);
        try {
          connection.add(utf8.encode(request));
          final bytes = BytesBuilder();
          await connection.input
              .forEach(bytes.add)
              .timeout(const Duration(seconds: 10));
          return latin1.decode(bytes.takeBytes());
        } finally {
          await connection.close();
        }
      }

      setUp(() => recordNames(pipePath));

      test('REST: the Add Phone code comes over the pipe, with the daemon\'s proof', () async {
        final client = api(LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe()));
        expect((await client.phoneSignInCode())?.code, 'hnh_pipe_test');
        expect(client.phoneSignInUnavailable, isFalse);
      });

      test('WebSocket: this computer\'s window connection over the pipe is one the daemon trusts', () async {
        final trusted = conn(LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: trustedPipe()));
        addTearDown(trusted.close);
        unawaited(trusted.connect());
        await ready(trusted);
        expect(trusted.trustedPipeMissing, isFalse);
        expect(await actRefusal(trusted), 'UNSUPPORTED');

        // The same daemon over its loopback port: refused, which is why the pipe is needed.
        final plain = conn(LocalDaemonTransport(), trusted: false);
        addTearDown(plain.close);
        unawaited(plain.connect());
        await ready(plain);
        expect(await actRefusal(plain), 'LOCAL_SOCKET_REQUIRED');
      });

      test('the daemon refuses a request without an auth, and with a wrong one, and drops such an upgrade', () async {
        final noAuth = await raw(
          'GET /api/status HTTP/1.1\r\nhost: localhost\r\nconnection: close\r\n\r\n',
        );
        expect(noAuth, startsWith('HTTP/1.1 401'));
        expect(noAuth.toLowerCase(), isNot(contains(pipeProofHeader)));

        final record = readDaemonPipeRecord(dataDir: dataDir.path, port: port)!;
        final wrong = pipeAuthHeaderValue(
          Uint8List(32),
          record.pipeId,
          Uint8List(16),
        );
        final wrongAuth = await raw(
          'GET /api/status HTTP/1.1\r\nhost: localhost\r\nconnection: close\r\n$pipeAuthHeader: $wrong\r\n\r\n',
        );
        expect(wrongAuth, startsWith('HTTP/1.1 401'));
        expect(wrongAuth.toLowerCase(), isNot(contains(pipeProofHeader)));

        final upgrade = await raw(
          'GET /api/local-ws HTTP/1.1\r\nhost: localhost\r\nupgrade: websocket\r\nconnection: Upgrade\r\n'
          'sec-websocket-key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==\r\nsec-websocket-version: 13\r\n\r\n',
        );
        expect(upgrade, isEmpty);
      });

      test('a pipe that answers with a bad proof is not trusted, and the daemon\'s own is found again', () async {
        recordNames(squatterPath);
        final pipe = trustedPipe();
        final transport = LocalDaemonTransport(trustedPipe: pipe);
        final client = api(transport);
        await expectLater(
          pipe.request('GET', '/api/status'),
          throwsA(isA<PipeUnproven>()),
        );
        await expectLater(
          pipe.webSocket('/api/local-ws'),
          throwsA(isA<PipeUnproven>()),
        );
        expect(await client.phoneSignInCode(), isNull);
        expect(client.phoneSignInUnavailable, isTrue);

        final fallback = conn(transport);
        addTearDown(fallback.close);
        unawaited(fallback.connect());
        await ready(fallback);
        expect(fallback.trustedPipeMissing, isTrue);

        recordNames(pipePath);
        expect(await pipe.probe(), isTrue);
        expect((await client.phoneSignInCode())?.code, 'hnh_pipe_test');
        expect(client.phoneSignInUnavailable, isFalse);
      });

      test('a pipe that is gone is absent', () async {
        const gone = r'\\.\pipe\harness-00000000000000000000000000000000';
        await expectLater(
          WindowsPipeConnection.open(gone),
          throwsA(isA<PipeAbsent>()),
        );
        recordNames(gone);
        await expectLater(
          trustedPipe().request('GET', '/api/status'),
          throwsA(isA<PipeAbsent>()),
        );
      });
    },
    skip: Platform.isWindows ? false : 'the real pipe is Windows only; test/trusted_pipe_test.dart covers the rest',
  );
}
```

Run on the Mac: `cd desktop && flutter analyze integration_test/windows_pipe_test.dart`
Expected: `No issues found!` Its group is skipped off Windows. Its protocol logic is the same as `trusted_pipe_test.dart`'s and was run against this server over Unix sockets. Only the kernel32 dial differs.

- [ ] **Step 9: Document the transport**

In `desktop/CLAUDE.md`, under "Native desktop talks to the local `harness` CLI", add the new bullet after the one about the Unix socket:

```diff
--- a/desktop/CLAUDE.md
+++ b/desktop/CLAUDE.md
@@ -265,6 +265,19 @@
   socket file exists, so a daemon restart does not strand the app on TCP. Windows and paths over 96
   bytes have no socket. The CLI, engine hooks and the dashboard stay on TCP. Under `flutter test`
   `LocalDaemonTransport.detect` finds no socket, so tests never reach a real daemon.
+- **On Windows the trusted routes go over the daemon's pipe** (`ws/trusted_pipe.dart`, B's §2):
+  `POST /api/auth/handoff`, and this computer's window connection (`WsConn.trustedLocal`), where
+  the daemon takes its `daemon_*` frames. Everything else stays on loopback TCP, relayed machines'
+  connections included. Reaching a Windows pipe is no trust: the app reads the pipe's name from
+  `daemon-<port>.json` and the token from `daemon-token` for every request (`ws/daemon_pipe_record.dart`),
+  each request carries `x-harness-auth`, and an answer counts only when its `x-harness-proof` proves the
+  token (`ws/windows_pipe_auth.dart`, held to the CLI's `__fixtures__/pipe-auth-vectors.json`). An
+  unproven pipe is no pipe: Add Phone shows its QR without the sign-in code, and the daemon's keys
+  and talk say harnessd's private connection is missing. The pipe client is kernel32 over FFI on two
+  background isolates (`ws/windows_pipe.dart`); its real-pipe test is
+  `integration_test/windows_pipe_test.dart`, on Windows CI. With no socket, the loopback port on
+  Windows is the one the daemon recorded in `daemon-<port>.json` (`LocalDaemonTransport.refreshTcpBase`):
+  another user's daemon may hold the configured one.
 - Besides viewer builds, a direct-to-backend test path is `LocalManualFixture` (`lib/main_local_manual.dart`), a
   compile-time-gated dev entrypoint fed by `scripts/start-terminal-local-manual.sh`. It fails closed
   unless every `--dart-define` is present.
```

### Phase C2 rulings

- **Home.** `defaultDaemonDataDir` uses C1.1's `maybeHomeDir`, which returns null when nothing names a home. `homeDir` throws then, and never returns `''`.
- **HMAC** reuses `hmacSha256` from `lib/e2ee/primitives.dart` (synchronous, pure Dart, no new dependency). The proof is compared in constant time over 64 hex characters.
- **CI reach.** The fixture `pipe-auth-vectors.json` also selects the desktop suite (`ALSO` in `scripts/ci-plan.py`), since `desktop/test/windows_pipe_auth_test.dart` reads it from `cli/`.
- **The token file** is 64 lowercase hex digits and an optional `\n` (`pipeAuth.ts` `TOKEN_TEXT`), decoding to 32 bytes. Anything else, or a link where a file should be, is refused.
- **Pipe names.** On Windows only `^\\\\\.\\pipe\\harness-[0-9a-f]{32}$`. Off Windows, in tests, a socket whose last part is `harness-<32 hex>`, mirroring `isPipePath`.
- **I/O.** An overlapped handle with a reader isolate and a writer isolate, so a WebSocket never waits behind a blocked read. `CreateFileW` adds `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION`. `GetLastError` is read only after leaf calls; a wait's result is the NTSTATUS in `OVERLAPPED`. No `dart:io` file API on the pipe.
- **WS routing.** Only this computer's window connection rides the pipe. A second trusted connection would be a second presence, and every push would arrive twice. Relayed connections stay on TCP.
- **`product_observe`** is not sent by the app today. If it ever is, it rides the same trusted connection.
- **No pid liveness check before dialling.** Nothing sent before the proof is secret, and nothing unproven is used.
- **A trusted route never falls back to TCP**, where the daemon refuses it and an answer would prove nothing.
- **Asking a missing pipe again** for the WebSocket happens at most once per 10 s, triggered by the trusted sends themselves, not by a timer.
- **The recorded loopback port (reconciliation).** Real issue, fixed in C2.3 Steps 7–9. On a shared PC another user's daemon may hold 18473, and this user's daemon then binds another port and records it in `daemon-18473.json` (`hookServer.ts` `allowPortFallback`). On Windows the app reads that port for discovery, REST and the local WebSocket, as the CLI's own clients do (`savedDaemonPort`). With no record, discovery reports the daemon down and asks nothing on 18473.
- **The real-pipe test** runs inside the app (`flutter test -d windows`) with `FLUTTER_TEST=1`, because `flutter test` runs `integration_test/` files on a device only. It uses C1.4's `setup-node` step and adds only `npm ci` in `cli/`.
- **Fallback copy.** Add Phone shows its QR without `h`, plus "Your phone will ask for a code from your email." The daemon brain says `privateConnectionWords`, lowercase like the rest of its copy.

---

## Phase C3: Native runner

The stock Flutter runner in `desktop/windows/runner` becomes the Harness runner. After this phase:

- one Harness runs per user, and a later launch hands it its `harness://` link;
- links reach Dart on the channel macOS and Linux already use;
- agents' news shows as Windows toasts, and a click on a toast opens that agent;
- Harness has a tray icon with the macOS status menu's rows, and the close button hides the window to the tray;
- image paste, copied files and the font list answer on their existing channels;
- the in-window menu bar is shared by Linux and Windows;
- the keys follow a Windows rule that never takes a chord a terminal program answers.

Each feature is one `.h/.cpp` pair registered from `flutter_window.cpp`. Every channel uses Flutter's C++ client wrapper,
`flutter::MethodChannel<flutter::EncodableValue>` with `flutter::StandardMethodCodec::GetInstance()`. That is the codec
the Dart side already uses: every one of these channels is a plain `MethodChannel('<name>')`, and a plain
`MethodChannel` defaults to `StandardMethodCodec`. Every handler answers on the platform thread. The font list is
enumerated on a worker thread, and its answer is posted back to the window.

**How C++ is verified here.** The runner cannot be built or run on the Mac that implements these tasks, so each C++
task is checked in three ways:

1. A Dart contract test, `desktop/test/windows_runner_contract_test.dart`, reads the C++ source, as
   `nativeIconLoaderOpens` in `test/swarm_screen_test.dart` reads `SwarmTitlebar.swift`. It pins the names that Dart and
   the launcher (C4) depend on, and it checks that CMake compiles every `.cpp`.
2. The Windows CI build of `windows-desktop.yml` (C1.4, job `build-test`, x64 and arm64) compiles the runner with the
   stock `/W4 /WX`.
3. C3.7's integration test runs the runner's channels and its single instance on Windows CI.

Commands run from the repository root unless a step says `cd desktop`.

### Task C3.1: Single instance

**Files:**
- Create: `desktop/windows/runner/single_instance.h`, `desktop/windows/runner/single_instance.cpp`
- Modify: `desktop/windows/runner/main.cpp` (whole file), `desktop/windows/runner/flutter_window.h` (whole file),
  `desktop/windows/runner/flutter_window.cpp` (whole file), `desktop/windows/runner/CMakeLists.txt` (whole file)
- Test: `desktop/test/windows_runner_contract_test.dart` (create)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces, in `single_instance.h`:
  - `constexpr wchar_t kHarnessQuitMessageName[] = L"Autonomous.Harness.Quit";`, with `UINT HarnessQuitMessage()` (the
    registered `WM_HARNESS_QUIT`, 0 if it could not be registered) and `bool IsHarnessQuitMessage(UINT message)`;
  - `constexpr ULONG_PTR kHarnessCopyDataCommandLine = 0x48524E53;` ("HRNS");
  - `class HarnessSingleInstance`, with these members:
    - `enum class Role { kPrimary, kForwarded, kGaveUp }`;
    - `Role Acquire(DWORD wait_ms = 15000)`;
    - `bool Listen(HWND main_window, CommandLineHandler on_command_line, std::function<void()> on_quit)`, where
      `CommandLineHandler` is `std::function<bool(const std::wstring&)>`;
    - `static bool NotifyQuit(DWORD wait_ms = 10000)`;
    - `static std::wstring InstanceName()`;
    - `static void BringToFront(HWND window)`;
    - `static constexpr wchar_t kWindowClass[] = L"HarnessSingleInstance"`.
- Produces, for C4 and C3.7:
  - **`harness-desktop.exe --quit`.** It calls `NotifyQuit()`. Exit code 0 means no Harness is left running for this
    user; 1 means one is still running after 10 s.
  - **The instance name.** It is `Local\Harness-<SID>`. A debug build appends `-debug`, so a `flutter run` never
    forwards to the installed app. When `HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTANCE` is set (tests), `-<value>` follows.
- Produces, on `FlutterWindow`: `void RequestQuit()`, `bool quitting() const` and
  `bool AcceptCommandLine(const std::wstring& command_line)`.
- Refinement: the header names `Local\Harness-<user SID>`. This plan adds two suffixes, `-debug` and
  `-<HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTANCE>`, and a new test-only environment variable, `HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTANCE`.

**The quit contract (`WM_HARNESS_QUIT`), shared with C4.3 word for word.**
- `WM_HARNESS_QUIT` is the registered window message `RegisterWindowMessageW(L"Autonomous.Harness.Quit")`. It is not a
  `WM_APP` value, so it means the same in every process and no other program's private message can be read as it.
- The app quits on it as the tray's Quit does (`FlutterWindow::RequestQuit`), hidden to the tray or not. It answers it
  on two windows: its main window, of the Flutter runner's class `FLUTTER_RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW`, and its single-instance
  window (class `HarnessSingleInstance`, message-only, titled with the instance name).
- `Harness.exe` (`--uninstall`, and `--install` over a running different version) posts it to the main window of each
  process whose image is `<install>\app\<one folder>\harness-desktop.exe` (`pty/src/desktop/win.rs`, `QUIT_MESSAGE`,
  `quit_app`), waits up to 10 s, and ends a process that is still there. It never uses the instance name or `--quit`.
- `harness-desktop.exe --quit` posts it to this user's single-instance window and waits up to 10 s. C3.7's race test
  uses it.

**Review Focus 4.** Two launches can race: a second launch can start while the first is still starting, when the first
has its mutex but no window yet. The second then looks for the window every 100 ms, for up to 15 s, and waits on the
mutex in between:

- if the first exits meanwhile, the second takes the mutex and becomes the app;
- a command line is sent again only when the first refused it (it is quitting) or its window was gone;
- a `SendMessageTimeoutW` that timed out is never retried, so a link is delivered at most once;
- a launch never creates a window before `Acquire()` returns `kPrimary`, so no second window can appear.

C3.7 runs this race on Windows CI.

```dart
// contracts are with Dart and with the launcher (`Harness.exe`, C4), which
// read none of it. This reads the source, as `nativeIconLoaderOpens` reads
// SwarmTitlebar.swift, so a renamed constant or a source file left out of the
// build fails here first. Windows CI then compiles the runner, and
// integration_test/windows_runner_test.dart runs it.

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';

String runner(String name) => File('windows/runner/$name').readAsStringSync();

void main() {
  test('every runner source is in the build', () {
    final cmake = runner('CMakeLists.txt');
    final sources = Directory('windows/runner')
        .listSync()

        .where((name) => name.endsWith('.cpp'));

      expect(
        header,

          'constexpr wchar_t kHarnessQuitMessageName[] = '
```

Create `desktop/windows/runner/single_instance.h`:

```cpp
#ifndef RUNNER_SINGLE_INSTANCE_H_
#define RUNNER_SINGLE_INSTANCE_H_

#include <windows.h>

#include <functional>
#include <string>

// WM_HARNESS_QUIT: the registered message that makes the running app quit,
// as the tray's Quit does, hidden to the tray or not. Registered, not a WM_APP
// value, so it means the same in every process and no other program's private
// message can be read as it. `Harness.exe` (pty/src/desktop/win.rs,
// QUIT_MESSAGE) posts it to the main window (class FLUTTER_RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW)
// of each process running from `<install>\app\*\harness-desktop.exe`;
// `harness-desktop.exe --quit` posts it to the single-instance window. Part of
// the launcher's contract: the name never changes.
constexpr wchar_t kHarnessQuitMessageName[] = L"Autonomous.Harness.Quit";

// The registered WM_HARNESS_QUIT, or 0 when it could not be registered.
UINT HarnessQuitMessage();

// Whether |message| is WM_HARNESS_QUIT. Never true when it is not registered,
// so WM_NULL is never read as a quit.
bool IsHarnessQuitMessage(UINT message);

// COPYDATASTRUCT::dwData of a forwarded command line: "HRNS".
constexpr ULONG_PTR kHarnessCopyDataCommandLine = 0x48524E53;

// One Harness per user and session.
//
// The first launch takes the mutex `Local\Harness-<user SID>` and, once its
// main window exists, creates a message-only window titled with the same name.
// A later launch finds that window, hands it its whole command line with
// WM_COPYDATA and exits. A launch that finds the mutex held but no window yet
// (the first is still starting) looks again every 100 ms, up to a bound. If
// the first exits meanwhile, it takes the mutex and becomes the app itself.
//
// Delivery is at most once. A command line is sent again only when the
// running app refused it (it is quitting) or its window had gone.
class HarnessSingleInstance {
 public:
  enum class Role {
    kPrimary,    // This process is the app.
    kForwarded,  // The running app has this launch's command line: exit.
    kGaveUp,     // The running app never showed its window: exit.
  };

  // Runs on the platform thread for each later launch's command line. False
  // refuses it, and that launch waits to become the app itself.
  using CommandLineHandler = std::function<bool(const std::wstring&)>;

  static constexpr wchar_t kWindowClass[] = L"HarnessSingleInstance";

  HarnessSingleInstance() = default;
  ~HarnessSingleInstance();

  HarnessSingleInstance(const HarnessSingleInstance&) = delete;
  HarnessSingleInstance& operator=(const HarnessSingleInstance&) = delete;

  // Takes the instance, or forwards this launch to the one that has it,
  // waiting up to |wait_ms| for that one to create its window.
  Role Acquire(DWORD wait_ms = 15000);

  // Creates the window later launches find. Call once |main_window| exists.
  bool Listen(HWND main_window, CommandLineHandler on_command_line,
              std::function<void()> on_quit);

  // Asks the running app to quit and waits up to |wait_ms| for it to exit.
  // True when no Harness is left running for this user.
  static bool NotifyQuit(DWORD wait_ms = 10000);

  // `Local\Harness-<SID>`, then `-debug` in a debug build (so `flutter run`
  // never forwards to the installed app), then `-<HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTANCE>`
  // when that variable is set (tests).
  static std::wstring InstanceName();

  // Shows |window| (restored if minimised, shown if hidden to the tray) and
  // puts it in front.
  static void BringToFront(HWND window);

 private:
  enum class Delivery { kAccepted, kRefused, kUnknown };

  static Delivery Forward(HWND target);
  static LRESULT CALLBACK WndProc(HWND window, UINT message, WPARAM wparam,
                                  LPARAM lparam) noexcept;
  LRESULT HandleMessage(UINT message, WPARAM wparam, LPARAM lparam);

  HANDLE mutex_ = nullptr;
  bool owns_mutex_ = false;
  HWND message_window_ = nullptr;
  HWND main_window_ = nullptr;
  CommandLineHandler on_command_line_;
  std::function<void()> on_quit_;
};

#endif  // RUNNER_SINGLE_INSTANCE_H_
```

Create `desktop/windows/runner/single_instance.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "single_instance.h"

#include <sddl.h>

#include <cwchar>
#include <memory>

namespace {

// The largest command line Windows passes, in bytes, with its terminator.
constexpr DWORD kMaxCommandLineBytes = 32768 * sizeof(wchar_t);

// The user's SID as text ("S-1-5-21-..."), or empty when the token cannot be
// read.
std::wstring CurrentUserSid() {
  HANDLE token = nullptr;
  if (!::OpenProcessToken(::GetCurrentProcess(), TOKEN_QUERY, &token)) {
    return std::wstring();
  }
  std::wstring sid;
  DWORD size = 0;
  ::GetTokenInformation(token, TokenUser, nullptr, 0, &size);
  if (size > 0) {
    auto buffer = std::make_unique<BYTE[]>(size);
    if (::GetTokenInformation(token, TokenUser, buffer.get(), size, &size)) {
      auto* user = reinterpret_cast<TOKEN_USER*>(buffer.get());
      wchar_t* text = nullptr;
      if (::ConvertSidToStringSidW(user->User.Sid, &text)) {
        sid = text;
        ::LocalFree(text);
      }
    }
  }
  ::CloseHandle(token);
  return sid;
}

}  // namespace

UINT HarnessQuitMessage() {
  static const UINT message =
      ::RegisterWindowMessageW(kHarnessQuitMessageName);
  return message;
}

bool IsHarnessQuitMessage(UINT message) {
  const UINT quit = HarnessQuitMessage();
  return quit != 0 && message == quit;
}

HarnessSingleInstance::~HarnessSingleInstance() {
  if (message_window_ != nullptr) {
    ::DestroyWindow(message_window_);
  }
  if (mutex_ != nullptr) {
    if (owns_mutex_) {
      ::ReleaseMutex(mutex_);
    }
    ::CloseHandle(mutex_);
  }
}

std::wstring HarnessSingleInstance::InstanceName() {
  const std::wstring sid = CurrentUserSid();
  std::wstring name =
      L"Local\\Harness-" + (sid.empty() ? std::wstring(L"user") : sid);
#ifdef _DEBUG
  name += L"-debug";
#endif
  wchar_t suffix[64] = {};
  const DWORD length =
      ::GetEnvironmentVariableW(L"HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTANCE", suffix, 64);
  if (length > 0 && length < 64) {
    name += L"-";
    name += suffix;
  }
  return name;
}

HarnessSingleInstance::Role HarnessSingleInstance::Acquire(DWORD wait_ms) {
  const std::wstring name = InstanceName();
  mutex_ = ::CreateMutexW(nullptr, TRUE, name.c_str());
  if (mutex_ == nullptr) {
    // No mutex at all (a broken session): running beats refusing to start.
    return Role::kPrimary;
  }
  if (::GetLastError() != ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS) {
    owns_mutex_ = true;
    return Role::kPrimary;
  }
  const ULONGLONG deadline = ::GetTickCount64() + wait_ms;
  for (;;) {
    HWND target =
        ::FindWindowExW(HWND_MESSAGE, nullptr, kWindowClass, name.c_str());
    if (target != nullptr && Forward(target) != Delivery::kRefused) {
      return Role::kForwarded;
    }
    // Still starting, or quitting. If it exits, its mutex is this launch's.
    const DWORD wait = ::WaitForSingleObject(mutex_, 100);
    if (wait == WAIT_OBJECT_0 || wait == WAIT_ABANDONED) {
      owns_mutex_ = true;
      return Role::kPrimary;
    }
    if (::GetTickCount64() >= deadline) {
      return Role::kGaveUp;
    }
  }
}

HarnessSingleInstance::Delivery HarnessSingleInstance::Forward(HWND target) {
  DWORD process_id = 0;
  ::GetWindowThreadProcessId(target, &process_id);
  // This launch came from a click, so it may hand the foreground on.
  if (process_id != 0) {
    ::AllowSetForegroundWindow(process_id);
  }
  const wchar_t* command_line = ::GetCommandLineW();
  const size_t length = wcsnlen(command_line, 32767);
  COPYDATASTRUCT data = {};
  data.dwData = kHarnessCopyDataCommandLine;
  data.cbData = static_cast<DWORD>((length + 1) * sizeof(wchar_t));
  data.lpData = const_cast<wchar_t*>(command_line);
  DWORD_PTR answer = FALSE;
  if (::SendMessageTimeoutW(target, WM_COPYDATA, 0,
                            reinterpret_cast<LPARAM>(&data), SMTO_NORMAL,
                            10000, &answer) == 0) {
    // A send that timed out may still be read later, so it is never sent
    // again. Any other failure means the window went away unread.
    return ::GetLastError() == ERROR_TIMEOUT ? Delivery::kUnknown
                                             : Delivery::kRefused;
  }
  return answer == TRUE ? Delivery::kAccepted : Delivery::kRefused;
}

bool HarnessSingleInstance::Listen(HWND main_window,
                                   CommandLineHandler on_command_line,
                                   std::function<void()> on_quit) {
  main_window_ = main_window;
  on_command_line_ = std::move(on_command_line);
  on_quit_ = std::move(on_quit);
  WNDCLASSW window_class = {};
  window_class.lpfnWndProc = WndProc;
  window_class.hInstance = ::GetModuleHandleW(nullptr);
  window_class.lpszClassName = kWindowClass;
  // Fails harmlessly when the class is already registered.
  ::RegisterClassW(&window_class);
  const std::wstring name = InstanceName();
  message_window_ = ::CreateWindowExW(0, kWindowClass, name.c_str(), 0, 0, 0,
                                      0, 0, HWND_MESSAGE, nullptr,
                                      window_class.hInstance, this);
  return message_window_ != nullptr;
}

LRESULT CALLBACK HarnessSingleInstance::WndProc(HWND window, UINT message,
                                                WPARAM wparam,
                                                LPARAM lparam) noexcept {
  if (message == WM_NCCREATE) {
    auto* create = reinterpret_cast<CREATESTRUCTW*>(lparam);
    ::SetWindowLongPtrW(window, GWLP_USERDATA,
                        reinterpret_cast<LONG_PTR>(create->lpCreateParams));
  } else if (auto* that = reinterpret_cast<HarnessSingleInstance*>(
                 ::GetWindowLongPtrW(window, GWLP_USERDATA))) {
    if (message == WM_COPYDATA || IsHarnessQuitMessage(message)) {
      return that->HandleMessage(message, wparam, lparam);
    }
  }
  return ::DefWindowProcW(window, message, wparam, lparam);
}

LRESULT HarnessSingleInstance::HandleMessage(UINT message, WPARAM,
                                             LPARAM lparam) {
  if (IsHarnessQuitMessage(message)) {
    if (on_quit_) {
      on_quit_();
    }
    return 0;
  }
  const auto* data = reinterpret_cast<const COPYDATASTRUCT*>(lparam);
  if (data == nullptr || data->dwData != kHarnessCopyDataCommandLine ||
      data->lpData == nullptr || data->cbData < sizeof(wchar_t) ||
      data->cbData > kMaxCommandLineBytes ||
      data->cbData % sizeof(wchar_t) != 0) {
    return FALSE;
  }
  const auto* text = static_cast<const wchar_t*>(data->lpData);
  const std::wstring command_line(
      text, wcsnlen(text, data->cbData / sizeof(wchar_t)));
  if (!on_command_line_ || !on_command_line_(command_line)) {
    return FALSE;
  }
  BringToFront(main_window_);
  return TRUE;
}

void HarnessSingleInstance::BringToFront(HWND window) {
  if (window == nullptr) {
    return;
  }
  ::ShowWindow(window, ::IsIconic(window) ? SW_RESTORE : SW_SHOW);
  ::SetForegroundWindow(window);
}

bool HarnessSingleInstance::NotifyQuit(DWORD wait_ms) {
  const std::wstring name = InstanceName();
  HWND target =
      ::FindWindowExW(HWND_MESSAGE, nullptr, kWindowClass, name.c_str());
  if (target == nullptr) {
    return true;
  }
  DWORD process_id = 0;
  ::GetWindowThreadProcessId(target, &process_id);
  const UINT quit = HarnessQuitMessage();
  if (quit == 0) {
    return false;
  }
  HANDLE process = process_id == 0
                       ? nullptr
                       : ::OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE, FALSE, process_id);
  if (!::PostMessageW(target, quit, 0, 0)) {
    if (process != nullptr) {
      ::CloseHandle(process);
    }
    // The window went away between finding it and posting to it.
    return ::FindWindowExW(HWND_MESSAGE, nullptr, kWindowClass,
                           name.c_str()) == nullptr;
  }
  if (process == nullptr) {
    return false;
  }
  const bool exited = ::WaitForSingleObject(process, wait_ms) == WAIT_OBJECT_0;
  ::CloseHandle(process);
  return exited;
}
```

```cpp
#include <flutter/dart_project.h>
#include <flutter/flutter_view_controller.h>
#include <windows.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "flutter_window.h"
#include "single_instance.h"
#include "utils.h"

int APIENTRY wWinMain(_In_ HINSTANCE instance, _In_opt_ HINSTANCE prev,
                      _In_ wchar_t *command_line, _In_ int show_command) {
  std::vector<std::string> command_line_arguments =
      GetCommandLineArguments();

  // `Harness.exe --uninstall` asks the running app to quit through this.
  if (std::find(command_line_arguments.begin(), command_line_arguments.end(),
                "--quit") != command_line_arguments.end()) {
    return HarnessSingleInstance::NotifyQuit() ? EXIT_SUCCESS : EXIT_FAILURE;
  }

  // One Harness per user: a later launch hands its command line over and
  // exits here, before it has a window of its own.
  HarnessSingleInstance single_instance;
  switch (single_instance.Acquire()) {
    case HarnessSingleInstance::Role::kPrimary:
      break;
    case HarnessSingleInstance::Role::kForwarded:
      return EXIT_SUCCESS;
    case HarnessSingleInstance::Role::kGaveUp:
      return EXIT_FAILURE;
  }

  // Attach to console when present (e.g., 'flutter run') or create a
  // new console when running with a debugger.
  if (!::AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) && ::IsDebuggerPresent()) {
    CreateAndAttachConsole();
  }

  // Initialize COM, so that it is available for use in the library and/or
  // plugins.
  ::CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED);

  flutter::DartProject project(L"data");

  project.set_dart_entrypoint_arguments(std::move(command_line_arguments));

  FlutterWindow window(project);
  Win32Window::Point origin(10, 10);
  Win32Window::Size size(1280, 720);
  if (!window.Create(L"Harness", origin, size)) {
    return EXIT_FAILURE;
  }
  window.SetQuitOnClose(true);

  single_instance.Listen(
      window.GetHandle(),
      [&window](const std::wstring& line) {
        return window.AcceptCommandLine(line);
      },
      [&window]() { window.RequestQuit(); });

  ::MSG msg;
  while (::GetMessage(&msg, nullptr, 0, 0)) {
    ::TranslateMessage(&msg);
    ::DispatchMessage(&msg);
  }

  ::CoUninitialize();
  return EXIT_SUCCESS;
}
```

```cpp
#ifndef RUNNER_FLUTTER_WINDOW_H_
#define RUNNER_FLUTTER_WINDOW_H_

#include <flutter/dart_project.h>
#include <flutter/flutter_view_controller.h>

#include <memory>
#include <string>

#include "win32_window.h"

// A window that hosts a Flutter view, and the Harness features the runner
// adds. Each feature's channel is registered in OnCreate.
class FlutterWindow : public Win32Window {
 public:
  // Creates a new FlutterWindow hosting a Flutter view running |project|.
  explicit FlutterWindow(const flutter::DartProject& project);
  virtual ~FlutterWindow();

  // Quits for real: past the close button's hide-to-tray, through Flutter's
  // own exit request (so `didRequestAppExit` saves the layout), and after 5 s
  // without it if Dart never answers.
  void RequestQuit();

  // Whether a quit has begun.
  bool quitting() const { return quitting_; }

  // A later launch's command line, handed over by the single instance. False
  // once quitting, so that launch waits and starts the app afresh.
  bool AcceptCommandLine(const std::wstring& command_line);

 protected:
  // Win32Window:
  bool OnCreate() override;
  void OnDestroy() override;
  LRESULT MessageHandler(HWND window, UINT const message, WPARAM const wparam,
                         LPARAM const lparam) noexcept override;

 private:
  // The project to run.
  flutter::DartProject project_;

  // The Flutter instance hosted by this window.
  std::unique_ptr<flutter::FlutterViewController> flutter_controller_;

  bool quitting_ = false;
};

#endif  // RUNNER_FLUTTER_WINDOW_H_
```

Replace `desktop/windows/runner/flutter_window.cpp` with:

```cpp
#include "flutter_window.h"

#include <optional>

#include "flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.h"
#include "single_instance.h"

namespace {

// RequestQuit's deadline for Flutter's exit request.
constexpr UINT_PTR kQuitTimer = 0x4851;
constexpr UINT kQuitTimeoutMs = 5000;

}  // namespace

FlutterWindow::FlutterWindow(const flutter::DartProject& project)
    : project_(project) {}

FlutterWindow::~FlutterWindow() {}

void FlutterWindow::RequestQuit() {
  if (quitting_) {
    return;
  }
  quitting_ = true;
  HWND window = GetHandle();
  if (window == nullptr) {
    ::PostQuitMessage(0);
    return;
  }
  ::SetTimer(window, kQuitTimer, kQuitTimeoutMs, nullptr);
  ::PostMessageW(window, WM_CLOSE, 0, 0);
}

bool FlutterWindow::AcceptCommandLine(const std::wstring& command_line) {
  return !quitting_;
}

bool FlutterWindow::OnCreate() {
  if (!Win32Window::OnCreate()) {
    return false;
  }

  RECT frame = GetClientArea();

  // The size here must match the window dimensions to avoid unnecessary surface
  // creation / destruction in the startup path.
  flutter_controller_ = std::make_unique<flutter::FlutterViewController>(
      frame.right - frame.left, frame.bottom - frame.top, project_);
  // Ensure that basic setup of the controller was successful.
  if (!flutter_controller_->engine() || !flutter_controller_->view()) {
    return false;
  }
  RegisterPlugins(flutter_controller_->engine());
  SetChildContent(flutter_controller_->view()->GetNativeWindow());

  flutter_controller_->engine()->SetNextFrameCallback([&]() {
    this->Show();
  });

  // Flutter can complete the first frame before the "show window" callback is
  // registered. The following call ensures a frame is pending to ensure the
  // window is shown. It is a no-op if the first frame hasn't completed yet.
  flutter_controller_->ForceRedraw();

  return true;
}

void FlutterWindow::OnDestroy() {
  if (flutter_controller_) {
    flutter_controller_ = nullptr;
  }

  Win32Window::OnDestroy();
}

LRESULT
FlutterWindow::MessageHandler(HWND hwnd, UINT const message,
                              WPARAM const wparam,
                              LPARAM const lparam) noexcept {
  // WM_HARNESS_QUIT (single_instance.h): Harness.exe asks the app to quit
  // through its main window, before an uninstall or an install over it.
  if (IsHarnessQuitMessage(message)) {
    RequestQuit();
    return 0;
  }

  if (message == WM_TIMER && wparam == kQuitTimer) {
    // Flutter did not finish its exit in time: leave without it.
    ::KillTimer(hwnd, kQuitTimer);
    ::DestroyWindow(hwnd);
    return 0;
  }

  // Give Flutter, including plugins, an opportunity to handle window messages.
  if (flutter_controller_) {
    std::optional<LRESULT> result =
        flutter_controller_->HandleTopLevelWindowProc(hwnd, message, wparam,
                                                      lparam);
    if (result) {
      return *result;
    }
  }

  switch (message) {
    case WM_FONTCHANGE:
      flutter_controller_->engine()->ReloadSystemFonts();
      break;
  }

  return Win32Window::MessageHandler(hwnd, message, wparam, lparam);
}
```

**Files:**
- Create: `desktop/windows/runner/community_links.h`, `desktop/windows/runner/community_links.cpp`
- Modify:
  - `desktop/windows/runner/main.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `HarnessSingleInstance` and `FlutterWindow::AcceptCommandLine` (C3.1).
- Produces, native side:
  - `harness/community_links` answers Dart's `ready` with the links that came before it, and later sends
    `open(<url>)`. These are the same two calls `AppDelegate.swift` and `my_application.cc` use.
  - A link starts with `harness://` (case-insensitive) and is at most 240 bytes. At most 20 wait for `ready`.
  - `HarnessCommunityLinks` has `Instance()`, `Attach(messenger)`, `Detach()`, `Deliver(url)`,
    `DeliverArguments(args)`, `DeliverCommandLine(line)` and `IsHarnessLink(value)`.
- Produces, Dart side:
  - `class NotificationLink` with `machineId`, `agentId`, `static const bare = 'harness://notification'`,
    `static String build(String machineId, String agentId)` and `static NotificationLink? parse(String value)`.
  - `bool SystemNotifications.openLink(String url)`.
  - `ForkInbox(store, {channel, bool Function(String url)? claimLink})`.
- Consumed by C3.3: `NotificationLink.build` gives a toast its launch link.

**Routing.**
- **A click while Harness runs.** `Harness.exe` starts `harness-desktop.exe` with the link. That process is a later
  launch, so it forwards the link over WM_COPYDATA. The running app's `DeliverCommandLine` sends `open`.
  `ForkInbox.accept` offers the link to `claimLink`, which is `systemNotifications.openLink`. That calls the handler
  `swarm_screen.dart` installs as `app.systemNotifications.onTap`, the same one a macOS notification click calls.
- **A click while Harness is closed.** The link arrives in argv and waits for `ready`. No workspace is listening yet, so
  the click only opens Harness. That is what `HarnessNotifications.swift` does for a click that launches the app.

In `desktop/lib/notify/system_notifications.dart`, add this class after `enum NotificationPermission { … }`:

```dart
/// What a Windows toast opens when it is clicked:
/// `harness://notification/<machineId>/<agentId>`, each part
/// percent-encoded. The toast launches it like any other link (single
/// instance, then `harness/community_links`), and
/// [SystemNotifications.openLink] sends it where a macOS click goes. The bare
/// link names no agent: it only brings Harness forward, which the runner has
/// already done by the time Dart reads it.
class NotificationLink {
  const NotificationLink(this.machineId, this.agentId);

  final String machineId;
  final String agentId;

  static const bare = 'harness://notification';

  /// The runner hands Dart at most this many bytes of a link (the macOS and
  /// Linux limit too).
  static const maxLength = 240;

  static String build(String machineId, String agentId) {
    if (machineId.isEmpty || agentId.isEmpty) return bare;
    final url =
        '$bare/${Uri.encodeComponent(machineId)}/${Uri.encodeComponent(agentId)}';
    return url.length > maxLength ? bare : url;
  }

  static NotificationLink? parse(String value) {
    if (value.length > maxLength) return null;
    final uri = Uri.tryParse(value);
    if (uri == null ||
        uri.scheme != 'harness' ||
        uri.host != 'notification' ||
        uri.hasPort ||
        uri.userInfo.isNotEmpty ||
        uri.hasQuery ||
        uri.hasFragment) {
      return null;
    }
    final segments = uri.pathSegments;
    if (segments.isEmpty) return const NotificationLink('', '');
    if (segments.length != 2 || segments.any((segment) => segment.isEmpty)) {
      return null;
    }
    return NotificationLink(segments[0], segments[1]);
  }
}
```

```dart
      _onTap?.call(link.machineId, link.agentId);
```

Create `desktop/windows/runner/community_links.h`:

```cpp
#ifndef RUNNER_COMMUNITY_LINKS_H_
#define RUNNER_COMMUNITY_LINKS_H_

#include <flutter/binary_messenger.h>
#include <flutter/encodable_value.h>
#include <flutter/method_channel.h>

#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

// `harness://` links for Dart, on `harness/community_links`: the channel and
// the two calls AppDelegate.swift and my_application.cc use.
//  - Dart -> native `ready` answers the links that arrived before it, and
//    every later link goes straight to Dart.
//  - Native -> Dart `open(<url>)`.
// A link starts with `harness://` and is at most 240 bytes. At most 20 wait
// for `ready`. They come from this launch's arguments and from later
// launches' command lines, which the single instance forwards.
class HarnessCommunityLinks {
 public:
  static HarnessCommunityLinks& Instance();

  void Attach(flutter::BinaryMessenger* messenger);
  void Detach();

  // One candidate link. Anything that is not a Harness link is ignored.
  void Deliver(const std::string& url);

  // This launch's own arguments (UTF-8, without the program).
  void DeliverArguments(const std::vector<std::string>& arguments);

  // A later launch's whole command line, as WM_COPYDATA carried it.
  void DeliverCommandLine(const std::wstring& command_line);

  static bool IsHarnessLink(const std::string& value);

 private:
  HarnessCommunityLinks() = default;

  std::unique_ptr<flutter::MethodChannel<flutter::EncodableValue>> channel_;
  std::vector<std::string> pending_;
  bool ready_ = false;
};

#endif  // RUNNER_COMMUNITY_LINKS_H_
```

```cpp
#include "community_links.h"

#include <flutter/standard_method_codec.h>
#include <windows.h>
#include <shellapi.h>

#include <string.h>

#include "utils.h"

namespace {

constexpr size_t kMaxLinkLength = 240;
constexpr size_t kMaxPending = 20;
constexpr char kScheme[] = "harness://";

}  // namespace

HarnessCommunityLinks& HarnessCommunityLinks::Instance() {
  static HarnessCommunityLinks links;
  return links;
}

bool HarnessCommunityLinks::IsHarnessLink(const std::string& value) {
  const size_t scheme = sizeof(kScheme) - 1;
  return value.size() > scheme && value.size() <= kMaxLinkLength &&
         _strnicmp(value.c_str(), kScheme, scheme) == 0;
}

void HarnessCommunityLinks::Attach(flutter::BinaryMessenger* messenger) {
  channel_ = std::make_unique<flutter::MethodChannel<flutter::EncodableValue>>(
      messenger, "harness/community_links",
      &flutter::StandardMethodCodec::GetInstance());
  channel_->SetMethodCallHandler([this](const auto& call, auto result) {
    if (call.method_name() != "ready") {
      result->NotImplemented();
      return;
    }
    ready_ = true;
    flutter::EncodableList links;
    for (const auto& link : pending_) {
      links.emplace_back(link);
    }
    pending_.clear();
    result->Success(flutter::EncodableValue(std::move(links)));
  });
}

void HarnessCommunityLinks::Detach() {
  if (channel_) {
    channel_->SetMethodCallHandler(nullptr);
  }
  channel_.reset();
  ready_ = false;
}

void HarnessCommunityLinks::Deliver(const std::string& url) {
  if (!IsHarnessLink(url)) {
    return;
  }
  if (ready_ && channel_) {
    channel_->InvokeMethod("open", std::make_unique<flutter::EncodableValue>(url));
  } else if (pending_.size() < kMaxPending) {
    pending_.push_back(url);
  }
}

void HarnessCommunityLinks::DeliverArguments(
    const std::vector<std::string>& arguments) {
  for (const auto& argument : arguments) {
    Deliver(argument);
  }
}

void HarnessCommunityLinks::DeliverCommandLine(
    const std::wstring& command_line) {
  int count = 0;
  wchar_t** argv = ::CommandLineToArgvW(command_line.c_str(), &count);
  if (argv == nullptr) {
    return;
  }
  // argv[0] is the program.
  for (int i = 1; i < count; i++) {
    Deliver(Utf8FromUtf16(argv[i]));
  }
  ::LocalFree(argv);
}
```

### Task C3.3: Notifications

**Files:**
- Create: `desktop/windows/runner/notifications.h`, `desktop/windows/runner/notifications.cpp`
- Modify:
  - `desktop/windows/runner/utils.h`, `desktop/windows/runner/utils.cpp` (add `Utf16FromUtf8`)
  - `desktop/windows/runner/main.cpp` (the AUMID)
  - `desktop/windows/runner/flutter_window.h`, `desktop/windows/runner/flutter_window.cpp`
  - `desktop/windows/runner/CMakeLists.txt`
  - `desktop/lib/notify/system_notifications.dart`
- Test: `desktop/test/windows_system_notifier_test.dart` (create), `desktop/test/windows_runner_contract_test.dart`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `NotificationLink.build` (C3.2) and the Start Menu shortcut with `System.AppUserModel.ID = Autonomous.Harness`
  (C4.2).
- Produces, on `harness/notifications`, the macOS calls and answers:
  - `authorize` → `granted | denied | unavailable`;
  - `show({id, title, body, machineId, agentId, tag, launch})` → `granted | denied | unavailable | unknown`;
  - `withdraw({id, tag})`.
- Refinement: `show` and `withdraw` carry two Windows-only keys, `tag` and `launch`, which Dart computes:
  - `tag` is `windowsToastTag(id)`: `harness-` followed by the FNV-1a 32-bit hex of the id's UTF-8. Windows caps a tag
    at 64 characters, and an id can be longer.
  - `launch` is `NotificationLink.build(machineId, agentId)`.
- Produces, Dart:
  - `class WindowsSystemNotifier implements SystemNotifier`;
  - `String windowsToastTag(String id)`;
  - `SystemNotifier platformSystemNotifier({String? operatingSystem})`.
- Produces, runner: `std::wstring Utf16FromUtf8(const std::string& utf8_string)` in `utils.h`.

**How CMake enables C++/WinRT.** The stock runner does not use C++/WinRT. Its headers ship with the Windows SDK in
`Include\<version>\cppwinrt`, which is on the include path of every Visual Studio project, so no include line is needed.
The exact lines are:

```cmake
target_link_libraries(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE "windowsapp.lib")
set_source_files_properties("notifications.cpp" PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "/bigobj;/permissive-")
```

- `windowsapp.lib` is the WinRT umbrella library, present for x64 and arm64.
- `/bigobj` covers the large `Windows.UI.Notifications` projection.
- `/permissive-` is C++/WinRT's recommended conformance mode. It applies to that one file only.
- The stock `/EHsc` already enables C++ exceptions. The stock `_HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0` trims only the STL's own throws.
  Every WinRT call is inside `try { … } catch (...)`.
- The headers sit inside `#pragma warning(push, 3)`, so the projection's own code never meets `/W4 /WX`.

```dart
/// One call on `harness/notifications`, answered as the macOS and Windows
/// runners answer: a missing runner is [NotificationPermission.unavailable],
/// any other failure [NotificationPermission.unknown].
Future<NotificationPermission> _askNotifications(
  MethodChannel channel,
  String method,
  Object? args,
) async {
  try {
    return NotificationPermission.parse(
      await channel.invokeMethod<String>(method, args),
    );
  } on MissingPluginException {
    return NotificationPermission.unavailable;
  } catch (_) {
    return NotificationPermission.unknown;
  }
}

/// The toast's tag for notification [id]: `harness-` and the FNV-1a 32-bit
/// hash of its UTF-8, in hex. A toast posted under a tag replaces the one
/// already there, as the Mac's identifier does, and Windows caps a tag at 64
/// characters, which an agent's id can pass.
String windowsToastTag(String id) {
  var hash = 0x811c9dc5;
  for (final byte in utf8.encode(id)) {
    hash ^= byte;
    hash = (hash * 0x01000193) & 0xffffffff;
  }
  return 'harness-${hash.toRadixString(16).padLeft(8, '0')}';
}

/// Windows: toasts through WinRT's `ToastNotificationManager`, in
/// `windows/runner/notifications.cpp`.
///
/// They post under the AUMID `Autonomous.Harness`, which only the installed
/// app's Start Menu shortcut carries. A copy run straight from the zip
/// answers [NotificationPermission.unavailable], and the banner keeps doing
/// the job. Windows has no permission prompt: [authorize] reports the switch
/// in Settings ▸ System ▸ Notifications.
///
/// A click is not a channel call. The toast launches its
/// `harness://notification/…` link ([NotificationLink]), which reaches the
/// running app through the single instance and `harness/community_links`, and
/// [SystemNotifications.openLink] sends it where a macOS click goes.
class WindowsSystemNotifier implements SystemNotifier {
  WindowsSystemNotifier({MethodChannel? channel})
    : _channel = channel ?? const MethodChannel('harness/notifications');

  final MethodChannel _channel;

  @override
  bool get supported => true;

  @override
  bool get clickOpensAgent => true;

  @override
  String get deniedAdvice =>
      'Allow it in Windows Settings ▸ System ▸ Notifications ▸ Harness.';

  @override
  Future<NotificationPermission> authorize() =>
      _askNotifications(_channel, 'authorize', null);

  @override
  Future<NotificationPermission> show({
    required String id,
    required String title,
    required String body,
    required String machineId,
    required String agentId,
  }) => _askNotifications(_channel, 'show', {
    'id': id,
    'title': title,
    'body': body,
    'machineId': machineId,
    'agentId': agentId,
    'tag': windowsToastTag(id),
    'launch': NotificationLink.build(machineId, agentId),
  });

  @override
  Future<void> withdraw(String id) async {
    try {
      await _channel.invokeMethod<void>('withdraw', {
        'id': id,
        'tag': windowsToastTag(id),
      });
    } catch (_) {}
  }

  /// Clicks come back as links ([SystemNotifications.openLink]), not here.
  @override
  set onTap(void Function(String machineId, String agentId)? handler) {}
}
```

```dart
/// The notifier for the platform this build runs on ([operatingSystem] is
/// `Platform.operatingSystem` unless a test names one).
SystemNotifier platformSystemNotifier({String? operatingSystem}) {
  if (kIsWeb) return browserSystemNotifier();
  return switch (operatingSystem ?? Platform.operatingSystem) {
    'macos' => MacSystemNotifier(),
    'linux' => LinuxSystemNotifier(),
    'windows' => WindowsSystemNotifier(),
    _ => const NoSystemNotifier(),
  };
}
```

```cpp
std::wstring Utf16FromUtf8(const std::string& utf8_string);
```

In `desktop/windows/runner/utils.cpp`, append:

```cpp
std::wstring Utf16FromUtf8(const std::string& utf8_string) {
  if (utf8_string.empty()) {
    return std::wstring();
  }
  const int input_length = static_cast<int>(utf8_string.size());
  const int target_length =
      ::MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, MB_ERR_INVALID_CHARS, utf8_string.data(),
                            input_length, nullptr, 0);
  if (target_length <= 0) {
    return std::wstring();
  }
  std::wstring utf16_string(static_cast<size_t>(target_length), L'\0');
  if (::MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, MB_ERR_INVALID_CHARS, utf8_string.data(),
                            input_length, utf16_string.data(),
                            target_length) == 0) {
    return std::wstring();
  }
  return utf16_string;
}
```

Create `desktop/windows/runner/notifications.h`:

```cpp
#ifndef RUNNER_NOTIFICATIONS_H_
#define RUNNER_NOTIFICATIONS_H_

#include <flutter/binary_messenger.h>
#include <flutter/encodable_value.h>
#include <flutter/method_channel.h>

#include <memory>
#include <string>

// An agent's news as a Windows toast, on `harness/notifications`: the calls
// HarnessNotifications.swift answers (`authorize`, `show`, `withdraw`), with
// its answers (`granted`, `denied`, `unavailable`, `unknown`).
//
// Dart decides whether and when to post. Toasts post under the AUMID
// `Autonomous.Harness`, which the Start Menu shortcut carries (C4). Without
// it Windows refuses, and `authorize` says `unavailable`. A toast's click is
// its `harness://notification/...` link (activationType="protocol"). It
// arrives through the single instance and `harness/community_links` like any
// other link, so no COM activator is needed.
class HarnessNotifications {
 public:
  explicit HarnessNotifications(flutter::BinaryMessenger* messenger);
  ~HarnessNotifications();

 private:
  static std::string Authorize();
  static std::string Show(const std::wstring& tag, const std::wstring& title,
                          const std::wstring& body,
                          const std::wstring& launch);
  static void Withdraw(const std::wstring& tag);

  std::unique_ptr<flutter::MethodChannel<flutter::EncodableValue>> channel_;
};

#endif  // RUNNER_NOTIFICATIONS_H_
```

Create `desktop/windows/runner/notifications.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "notifications.h"

#include <flutter/standard_method_codec.h>
#include <windows.h>

#pragma warning(push, 3)
#include <winrt/Windows.Data.Xml.Dom.h>
#include <winrt/Windows.Foundation.h>
#include <winrt/Windows.UI.Notifications.h>
#pragma warning(pop)

#include "utils.h"

namespace {

using winrt::Windows::Data::Xml::Dom::XmlDocument;
using winrt::Windows::UI::Notifications::NotificationSetting;
using winrt::Windows::UI::Notifications::ToastNotification;
using winrt::Windows::UI::Notifications::ToastNotificationManager;

constexpr wchar_t kAppUserModelId[] = L"Autonomous.Harness";
constexpr wchar_t kGroup[] = L"harness";
constexpr wchar_t kBareLink[] = L"harness://notification";
constexpr char kLinkPrefix[] = "harness://notification";

const std::string* StringArgument(const flutter::EncodableMap* arguments,
                                  const char* key) {
  if (arguments == nullptr) {
    return nullptr;
  }
  auto entry = arguments->find(flutter::EncodableValue(key));
  if (entry == arguments->end()) {
    return nullptr;
  }
  return std::get_if<std::string>(&entry->second);
}

// Text for the toast's XML. Control characters an agent's message may carry
// are dropped, because XML 1.0 cannot hold them.
std::wstring EscapeXml(const std::wstring& text) {
  std::wstring escaped;
  escaped.reserve(text.size());
  for (wchar_t c : text) {
    switch (c) {
      case L'&':
        escaped += L"&amp;";
        break;
      case L'<':
        escaped += L"&lt;";
        break;
      case L'>':
        escaped += L"&gt;";
        break;
      case L'"':
        escaped += L"&quot;";
        break;
      case L'\'':
        escaped += L"&apos;";
        break;
      default:
        if (c >= 0x20 || c == L'\t' || c == L'\n' || c == L'\r') {
          escaped += c;
        }
    }
  }
  return escaped;
}

// The click's link as Dart built it, or the bare one, which only opens Harness.
std::wstring LaunchLink(const std::string* launch) {
  const std::string prefix = kLinkPrefix;
  if (launch == nullptr || launch->size() > 240 ||
      launch->compare(0, prefix.size(), prefix) != 0) {
    return kBareLink;
  }
  return Utf16FromUtf8(*launch);
}

}  // namespace

HarnessNotifications::HarnessNotifications(flutter::BinaryMessenger* messenger)
    : channel_(std::make_unique<flutter::MethodChannel<flutter::EncodableValue>>(
          messenger, "harness/notifications",
          &flutter::StandardMethodCodec::GetInstance())) {
  channel_->SetMethodCallHandler([](const auto& call, auto result) {
    const std::string& method = call.method_name();
    const auto* arguments = std::get_if<flutter::EncodableMap>(call.arguments());
    if (method == "authorize") {
      result->Success(flutter::EncodableValue(Authorize()));
      return;
    }
    const std::string* tag = StringArgument(arguments, "tag");
    const bool tag_ok = tag != nullptr && !tag->empty() && tag->size() <= 64;
    if (method == "show") {
      const std::string* title = StringArgument(arguments, "title");
      const std::string* body = StringArgument(arguments, "body");
      if (!tag_ok || title == nullptr || body == nullptr) {
        result->Error("INVALID_NOTIFICATION", "Missing tag, title or body");
        return;
      }
      result->Success(flutter::EncodableValue(
          Show(Utf16FromUtf8(*tag), Utf16FromUtf8(*title),
               Utf16FromUtf8(*body),
               LaunchLink(StringArgument(arguments, "launch")))));
      return;
    }
    if (method == "withdraw") {
      if (tag_ok) {
        Withdraw(Utf16FromUtf8(*tag));
      }
      result->Success();
      return;
    }
    result->NotImplemented();
  });
}

HarnessNotifications::~HarnessNotifications() {
  channel_->SetMethodCallHandler(nullptr);
}

std::string HarnessNotifications::Authorize() {
  try {
    switch (ToastNotificationManager::CreateToastNotifier(kAppUserModelId)
                .Setting()) {
      case NotificationSetting::Enabled:
        return "granted";
      case NotificationSetting::DisabledForApplication:
      case NotificationSetting::DisabledForUser:
      case NotificationSetting::DisabledByGroupPolicy:
        return "denied";
      default:
        return "unavailable";
    }
  } catch (...) {
    // No shortcut carries the AUMID (a copy run straight from the zip), or
    // no notification platform at all.
    return "unavailable";
  }
}

std::string HarnessNotifications::Show(const std::wstring& tag,
                                       const std::wstring& title,
                                       const std::wstring& body,
                                       const std::wstring& launch) {
  const std::string answer = Authorize();
  if (answer != "granted") {
    return answer;
  }
  try {
    XmlDocument document;
    document.LoadXml(
        L"<toast activationType=\"protocol\" launch=\"" + EscapeXml(launch) +
        L"\"><visual><binding template=\"ToastGeneric\">"
        L"<text hint-maxLines=\"1\">" +
        EscapeXml(title) + L"</text><text>" + EscapeXml(body) +
        L"</text></binding></visual></toast>");
    ToastNotification toast(document);
    // The same tag replaces what is already there: one entry per agent.
    toast.Tag(tag);
    toast.Group(kGroup);
    ToastNotificationManager::CreateToastNotifier(kAppUserModelId).Show(toast);
    return "granted";
  } catch (...) {
    // This one toast, not the channel: "unknown" keeps the next alert trying.
    return "unknown";
  }
}

void HarnessNotifications::Withdraw(const std::wstring& tag) {
  try {
    ToastNotificationManager::History().Remove(tag, kGroup, kAppUserModelId);
  } catch (...) {
    // Already gone, or never shown.
  }
}
```

**Files:**
- Create: `desktop/windows/runner/tray.h`, `desktop/windows/runner/tray.cpp`, `desktop/lib/core/windows_status_tray.dart`
- Modify:
  - `desktop/windows/runner/flutter_window.h`, `desktop/windows/runner/flutter_window.cpp`
  - `desktop/windows/runner/CMakeLists.txt`
  - `desktop/lib/screens/swarm_screen.dart`
  - `desktop/lib/app_shell.dart`
- Test: `desktop/test/windows_status_tray_test.dart` (create), `desktop/test/swarm_screen_test.dart` (the `mount` helper),
  `desktop/test/windows_runner_contract_test.dart`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - `statusMenuEntries`, `statusMenuWorkingEntries` and `statusMenuReceiptIsCurrent` (`lib/state/status_menu.dart`);
  - `_SwarmScreenState._onNative` and its `'openStatusHarness'` case, which calls `_openStatusHarness`;
  - `revealWindow()` (`lib/core/desktop_window.dart`);
  - `systemNotifications.notifier` (C3.3);
  - `FlutterWindow::RequestQuit` and `HarnessSingleInstance::BringToFront` (C3.1).
- Produces, on `harness/status_menu`:
  - Dart → native `update({entries, workingEntries, workspaceAvailable})`, as the header says. `entries` and
    `workingEntries` are the very maps `statusMenuEntries`/`statusMenuWorkingEntries` return.
  - Dart → native `quit`.
  - Native → Dart `selected(<row>)` (the receipt), `openApp` and `hidden`.
- Why `quit` travels Dart → native, not native → Dart: the native side owns the hide-to-tray
  flag, so the in-window menu's Quit (C3.6) asks the runner. The tray's own Quit row calls `RequestQuit` natively,
  without a round trip. `hidden` is added, native → Dart, for the one-time notice.
- Produces, Dart:
  - `class WindowsStatusTray`, with `install()`, `update({…})`, `clear()`, `quit()`,
    `Future<void> Function(Map receipt)? onSelected`, `static const channelName = 'harness/status_menu'`,
    `noticeId` and `noticeBody`;
  - `class TrayNoticeStore extends OnOffPreference`, with key `app_tray_notice_shown`;
  - `final windowsStatusTray`;
  - `Future<void> quitHarness()`;
  - `SwarmScreen({…, WindowsStatusTray? statusTray})`.

**Hide to tray: the runner's WM_CLOSE, not `window_manager.setPreventClose`.** `FlutterWindow::MessageHandler`
decides on WM_CLOSE before `HandleTopLevelWindowProc`. That keeps it ahead of both the plugin's close delegate and
Flutter's exit request.

- While the tray icon is installed and no quit has begun, the close button hides the window.
- A quit sets `quitting_` and posts WM_CLOSE again. That WM_CLOSE goes on to Flutter, so `didRequestAppExit` saves the
  layout as it does on macOS. If Flutter never finishes, C3.1's 5 s timer ends the app anyway.
- If Explorer is not running and the icon could not be added, the close button quits. A window must never vanish with
  no way back.

The first hide shows the toast "Harness is still running in the tray." once (spec Risks). It is counted only after
Windows has actually shown it.

**The menu**, mirroring `HarnessStatusMenu.swift`:

```
Ready (N)                        (heading, unread rows only; none when empty)
<title>                    now   (at most 5 unread rows; greyed when the row is unavailable)
N more                           (greyed, past 5)
All caught up | Open Harness to get started   (greyed, when there is no unread row)
───────
Working (N)                      (heading, when the workspace is up and something works)
<title>                    42s
───────
Open Harness                     (bold default: shows the window)
Quit
```

The tray leaves out these macOS rows, which the spec does not list and the header's channel cannot carry:

- Mark all read;
- View all N notifications…;
- New Harness…;
- Open Harness… (which on macOS opens the session picker).

A left click on the icon shows the window.

```dart
// The Windows tray (`windows/runner/tray.cpp`): the rows the workspace hands
// it, what comes back when one is chosen, and the one-time notice when the
// close button hides Harness instead of quitting it.
import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:harness/core/windows_status_tray.dart';
import 'package:harness/notify/alert_sounds.dart';
import 'package:harness/notify/system_notifications.dart';

import 'support/memory_key_value_store.dart';
import 'swarm_screen_test.dart' show mount, terminal;
import 'swarm_state_test.dart' show createApp;

class _Notifier implements SystemNotifier {
  NotificationPermission answer = NotificationPermission.granted;
  final shown = <String>[];

  @override
  bool get supported => true;

  @override
  bool get clickOpensAgent => true;

  @override
  String get deniedAdvice => '';

  @override
  Future<NotificationPermission> authorize() async => answer;

  @override
  Future<NotificationPermission> show({
    required String id,
    required String title,
    required String body,
    required String machineId,
    required String agentId,
  }) async {
    shown.add('$id|$title|$body');
    return answer;
  }

  @override
  Future<void> withdraw(String id) async {}

  @override
  set onTap(void Function(String machineId, String agentId)? handler) {}
}

void main() {
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  const channel = MethodChannel('test/status_menu');
  final messenger =
      TestDefaultBinaryMessengerBinding.instance.defaultBinaryMessenger;
  late List<MethodCall> calls;

  setUp(() {
    calls = [];
    messenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(channel, (call) async {
      calls.add(call);
      return null;
    });
  });

  tearDown(() {
    messenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(channel, null);
    channel.setMethodCallHandler(null);
  });

  Future<void> fromNative(String method, [Object? arguments]) {
    final done = Completer<void>();
    messenger.handlePlatformMessage(
      channel.name,
      const StandardMethodCodec().encodeMethodCall(MethodCall(method, arguments)),
      (_) => done.complete(),
    );
    return done.future;
  }

  TrayNoticeStore notice() => TrayNoticeStore(storage: MemoryKeyValueStore());

  test('the tray is the runner\'s status menu channel', () {
    expect(WindowsStatusTray.channelName, 'harness/status_menu');
  });

  test('sends the rows once per change, and an empty tray when the workspace '
      'leaves', () async {
    final tray = WindowsStatusTray(channel: channel, notice: notice());
    final row = <String, Object?>{
      'machineId': 'm',
      'agentId': 'a',
      'unread': true,
      'title': 'Fix login',
    };
    await tray.update(
      entries: [row],
      workingEntries: const [],
      workspaceAvailable: true,
    );
    await tray.update(
      entries: [Map.of(row)],
      workingEntries: const [],
      workspaceAvailable: true,
    );
    await tray.clear();
    expect(calls.map((call) => call.method), ['update', 'update']);
    expect(calls.first.arguments, {
      'entries': [row],
      'workingEntries': [],
      'workspaceAvailable': true,
    });
    expect(calls.last.arguments, {
      'entries': [],
      'workingEntries': [],
      'workspaceAvailable': false,
    });
  });

  test('a chosen row reaches the workspace, and the icon reveals the window',
      () async {
    var reveals = 0;
    final chosen = <Map>[];
    final tray = WindowsStatusTray(
      channel: channel,
      notice: notice(),
      reveal: () async => reveals++,
    )..install();
    // No workspace on screen: nothing to open.
    await fromNative('selected', {'machineId': 'm', 'agentId': 'a'});
    tray.onSelected = (receipt) async => chosen.add(receipt);
    await fromNative('selected', {
      'machineId': 'm',
      'agentId': 'a',
      'readToken': 't',
    });
    await fromNative('openApp');
    await fromNative('somethingElse');
    expect(chosen, [
      {'machineId': 'm', 'agentId': 'a', 'readToken': 't'},
    ]);
    expect(reveals, 1);
  });

  test('hiding to the tray says so once, counted once Windows has shown it',
      () async {
    final store = MemoryKeyValueStore();
    final notifier = _Notifier()..answer = NotificationPermission.unavailable;
    WindowsStatusTray(
      channel: channel,
      notice: TrayNoticeStore(storage: store),
      notifier: () => notifier,
    ).install();
    await fromNative('hidden');
    notifier.answer = NotificationPermission.granted;
    await fromNative('hidden');
    await fromNative('hidden');
    const shown =
        '${WindowsStatusTray.noticeId}|Harness|Harness is still running in the tray.';
    expect(notifier.shown, [shown, shown]);
    // The next start remembers.
    WindowsStatusTray(
      channel: channel,
      notice: TrayNoticeStore(storage: store),
      notifier: () => notifier,
    ).install();
    await fromNative('hidden');
    expect(notifier.shown, hasLength(2));
  });

  test('Quit asks the runner to quit for real', () async {
    await WindowsStatusTray(channel: channel, notice: notice()).quit();
    expect(calls.single.method, 'quit');
  });

  testWidgets('the workspace feeds the tray and opens the row chosen there', (
    tester,
  ) async {
    const windowChannel = MethodChannel('window_manager');
    final windowActions = <String>[];
    tester.binding.defaultBinaryMessenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(
      windowChannel,
      (call) async {
        windowActions.add(call.method);
        return call.method == 'isMinimized' ? false : null;
      },
    );
    addTearDown(
      () => tester.binding.defaultBinaryMessenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(
        windowChannel,
        null,
      ),
    );
    final updates = <Map>[];
    tester.binding.defaultBinaryMessenger.setMockMethodCallHandler(channel, (
      call,
    ) async {
      if (call.method == 'update') updates.add(call.arguments as Map);
      return null;
    });
    final app = createApp(connected: true)..watchedAgents = () => const [];
    final resultTab = app.activeSwarmId;
    app.adoptSessionForTest(terminal('a8', []));
    app.newSwarm(name: 'Desktop');
    app.adoptSessionForTest(terminal('a0', []));
    final originalTab = app.activeSwarmId;
    app.agentUnread.mark('m', 'a8', AlertKind.done);
    final tray = WindowsStatusTray(channel: channel, notice: notice())..install();
    await mount(tester, app, statusTray: tray);
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(updates.last['workspaceAvailable'], isTrue);
    final row = (updates.last['entries'] as List).cast<Map>().single;
    expect(row['agentId'], 'a8');
    expect(app.activeSwarmId, originalTab);

    final done = Completer<void>();
    tester.binding.defaultBinaryMessenger.handlePlatformMessage(
      channel.name,
      const StandardMethodCodec().encodeMethodCall(MethodCall('selected', row)),
      (_) => done.complete(),
    );
    // The workspace replies after the destination's next frame.
    for (var i = 0; i < 8 && !done.isCompleted; i++) {
      await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));
    }
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();
    expect(done.isCompleted, isTrue);
    expect(app.activeSwarmId, resultTab);
    expect(app.agentUnread.kindFor('m', 'a8'), isNull);
    expect(windowActions, contains('show'));

    await tester.pumpWidget(const SizedBox());
    expect(updates.last, {
      'entries': [],
      'workingEntries': [],
      'workspaceAvailable': false,
    });
    app.dispose();
  });
}
```

Create `desktop/lib/core/windows_status_tray.dart`:

```dart
import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

import '../notify/alert_sounds.dart';
import '../notify/system_notifications.dart';
import 'desktop_window.dart';

/// Whether Windows has said "Harness is still running in the tray." once.
///
/// On Windows the close button hides Harness to the tray instead of quitting
/// it, which is not what it means on a Mac. The first time, a toast says
/// where the window went.
class TrayNoticeStore extends OnOffPreference {
  TrayNoticeStore({super.storage}) : super('app_tray_notice_shown');
}

/// Harness in the Windows notification area (`windows/runner/tray.cpp`), on
/// `harness/status_menu`.
///
/// Dart → native:
/// - `update({entries, workingEntries, workspaceAvailable})`: the rows the
///   macOS status menu draws, straight from `statusMenuEntries` and
///   `statusMenuWorkingEntries`. The workspace sends them while it is on
///   screen, and [clear]s them when it leaves.
/// - `quit`: leave for real ([quitHarness]). The window's close button only
///   hides it.
///
/// Native → Dart:
/// - `selected(<row>)`: a notification or working row was chosen, and the
///   workspace opens it as a macOS menu click does ([onSelected]);
/// - `openApp`: the icon, or Open Harness, brought the window forward;
/// - `hidden`: the close button hid the window to the tray.
class WindowsStatusTray {
  WindowsStatusTray({
    MethodChannel? channel,
    TrayNoticeStore? notice,
    SystemNotifier Function()? notifier,
    Future<void> Function()? reveal,
  }) : _channel = channel ?? const MethodChannel(channelName),
       _notice = notice ?? TrayNoticeStore(),
       _notifier = notifier ?? (() => systemNotifications.notifier),
       _reveal = reveal ?? revealWindow;

  static const channelName = 'harness/status_menu';
  static const noticeId = 'harness-tray-notice';
  static const noticeBody = 'Harness is still running in the tray.';

  final MethodChannel _channel;
  final TrayNoticeStore _notice;
  final SystemNotifier Function() _notifier;
  final Future<void> Function() _reveal;
  String? _sent;
  bool _installed = false;

  /// Where a chosen row goes: the workspace's `_openStatusHarness`. Null while
  /// no workspace is on screen, which is when the tray has no rows.
  Future<void> Function(Map receipt)? onSelected;

  /// Starts listening to the runner. Once, at start-up, on Windows only.
  void install() {
    if (_installed) return;
    _installed = true;
    _channel.setMethodCallHandler(_receive);
  }

  /// The tray's rows. Sent only when they changed.
  Future<void> update({
    required List<Map<String, Object?>> entries,
    required List<Map<String, Object?>> workingEntries,
    required bool workspaceAvailable,
  }) async {
    final state = <String, Object?>{
      'entries': entries,
      'workingEntries': workingEntries,
      'workspaceAvailable': workspaceAvailable,
    };
    final encoded = jsonEncode(state);
    if (encoded == _sent) return;
    _sent = encoded;
    try {
      await _channel.invokeMethod<void>('update', state);
    } on MissingPluginException {
      // No runner answers: a test, or a build without the tray.
    }
  }

  /// No workspace: "Open Harness to get started", and no rows to choose.
  Future<void> clear() => update(
    entries: const [],
    workingEntries: const [],
    workspaceAvailable: false,
  );

  /// Leaves Harness for real, through Flutter's exit request.
  Future<void> quit() async {
    try {
      await _channel.invokeMethod<void>('quit');
    } on MissingPluginException {
      // Nothing to ask.
    }
  }

  Future<void> _receive(MethodCall call) async {
    switch (call.method) {
      case 'selected':
        if (call.arguments case final Map receipt) {
          await onSelected?.call(receipt);
        }
      case 'openApp':
        await _reveal();
      case 'hidden':
        await _noticeOnce();
    }
  }

  /// Once, and counted only after Windows has shown it: a copy run straight
  /// from the zip cannot post a toast, and says so the next time instead.
  Future<void> _noticeOnce() async {
    await _notice.load();
    if (_notice.value) return;
    final answer = await _notifier().show(
      id: noticeId,
      title: 'Harness',
      body: noticeBody,
      machineId: '',
      agentId: '',
    );
    if (answer == NotificationPermission.granted) await _notice.set(true);
  }
}

/// The app's one tray.
final windowsStatusTray = WindowsStatusTray();

/// Quits Harness for real on Windows, where the close button only hides it.
Future<void> quitHarness() => windowsStatusTray.quit();
```
