  Create `pty/src/desktop/mod.rs` (the `Install` and `Uninstall` arms are filled in by C4.2 and C4.3):

````rust
//! `Harness.exe`, the Harness desktop app's launcher on Windows (desktop spec section 3). It is the one program the
//! Start Menu shortcut, the `harness://` key and the uninstall entry name, so an update, which swaps the app's
//! version folder, never breaks any of them:
//!
//! ```text
//! %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Harness\
//!   Harness.exe   Harness.ico   current   previous   app\<ver>\   launch.log   launch-state.json
//! ```
//!
//! - no arguments, or a `harness://` link: start `app\<current>\harness-desktop.exe` with the same arguments, then
//!   exit (`launch`). `--wait-pid <pid>` first waits for that process to end: the updater and the self-install pass
//!   the app they are replacing, which still holds the single-instance mutex.
//! - `--install [--wait-pid <pid>]`, run from an extracted zip: install that zip's version (`install`).
//! - `--uninstall`, from Settings ▸ Apps (`uninstall`).
//! - `--version`.
//!
//! It is a GUI-subsystem program, so nothing it does opens a console window, and it says what went wrong in a message
//! box and in `launch.log`. It builds and runs on Unix too, where the launch path starts the app with `Command` and
//! the Windows-only steps (registry, Start Menu, windows) are absent, so `cargo test` covers the rest everywhere.

use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

pub mod launch;
pub mod pointer;
pub mod system;
#[cfg(windows)]
pub mod win;

/// The Flutter app in each version folder (`BINARY_NAME`, desktop/windows/CMakeLists.txt).
pub const APP_EXE: &str = "harness-desktop.exe";
/// This program, as the zip and the install name it.
pub const LAUNCHER_EXE: &str = "Harness.exe";
/// The icon the shortcut and the uninstall entry show, beside the launcher (the launcher has no icon resource).
pub const ICON: &str = "Harness.ico";
/// The version folders.
pub const APP_DIR: &str = "app";
/// What the app writes in its version folder once its first frame is drawn (desktop/lib/update/started_marker.dart).
pub const STARTED_MARKER: &str = ".started";
pub const AUMID: &str = "Autonomous.Harness";
pub const DISPLAY_NAME: &str = "Harness";
pub const PUBLISHER: &str = "Autonomous";

pub const INSTALL_ROOT_ENV: &str = "HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT";
pub const PROGRAMS_DIR_ENV: &str = "HARNESS_DESKTOP_PROGRAMS_DIR";
pub const REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV: &str = "HARNESS_DESKTOP_REGISTRY_ROOT";

pub const EXIT_OK: i32 = 0;
pub const EXIT_FAILED: i32 = 1;
pub const EXIT_USAGE: i32 = 2;
pub const EXIT_BROKEN: i32 = 3;
pub const EXIT_SPAWN: i32 = 4;

pub const USAGE: &str = "usage: Harness.exe [--wait-pid <pid>] [<harness:// link>...] | --install [--wait-pid <pid>] | --uninstall | --version";

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Command {
    Launch { wait_pid: Option<u32>, args: Vec<OsString> },
    Install { wait_pid: Option<u32> },
    Uninstall,
    Version,
}

fn pid_after(args: &[OsString], at: usize) -> Result<u32, String> {
    args.get(at)
        .and_then(|value| value.to_str())
        .and_then(|value| value.parse::<u32>().ok())
        .filter(|&pid| pid > 0)
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("--wait-pid needs a process id\n{USAGE}"))
}

/// Only the first word can be one of this program's own options. A `harness://` link is whatever the shell passes
/// as `%1` and always begins with the scheme, so no link reads as `--uninstall`.
pub fn parse(args: &[OsString]) -> Result<Command, String> {
    match args.first().and_then(|first| first.to_str()) {
        Some("--version") if args.len() == 1 => Ok(Command::Version),
        Some("--uninstall") if args.len() == 1 => Ok(Command::Uninstall),
        Some("--install") => match args.len() {
            1 => Ok(Command::Install { wait_pid: None }),
            3 if args[1] == "--wait-pid" => Ok(Command::Install { wait_pid: Some(pid_after(args, 2)?) }),
            _ => Err(format!("unexpected arguments after --install\n{USAGE}")),
        },
        Some("--version" | "--uninstall") => Err(format!("unexpected arguments after {:?}\n{USAGE}", args[0])),
        Some("--wait-pid") => Ok(Command::Launch { wait_pid: Some(pid_after(args, 1)?), args: args[2..].to_vec() }),
        _ => Ok(Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: args.to_vec() }),
    }
}

/// The folder this program runs from: the root it launches from, unless [INSTALL_ROOT_ENV] names another (tests).
pub fn launch_root(own_exe: &Path, env: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<OsString>) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    if let Some(root) = env(INSTALL_ROOT_ENV).filter(|root| !root.is_empty()) {
        return Some(PathBuf::from(root));
    }
    own_exe.parent().filter(|dir| !dir.as_os_str().is_empty()).map(Path::to_path_buf)
}

/// The program: see the module comment.
pub fn run(args: Vec<OsString>) -> i32 {
    let command = match parse(&args) {
        Ok(command) => command,
        Err(err) => {
            system::say(&err);
            return EXIT_USAGE;
        }
    };
    match command {
        Command::Version => {
            println!("{}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
            EXIT_OK
        }
        Command::Launch { wait_pid, args } => {
            let Some(root) = std::env::current_exe().ok().and_then(|exe| launch_root(&exe, |key| std::env::var_os(key))) else {
                system::say("Harness.exe does not know its own folder.");
                return EXIT_BROKEN;
            };
            launch::run(&root, wait_pid, &args, &mut system::Real::default())
        }
        // C4.2 and C4.3.
        Command::Install { .. } | Command::Uninstall => {
            system::say("This Harness.exe does not install or uninstall yet.");
            EXIT_USAGE
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn os(args: &[&str]) -> Vec<OsString> {
        args.iter().map(OsString::from).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_each_form_and_passes_a_link_through() {
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&[])).unwrap(), Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: vec![] });
        assert_eq!(
            parse(&os(&["harness://notification/m/a"])).unwrap(),
            Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: os(&["harness://notification/m/a"]) }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse(&os(&["--wait-pid", "42", "harness://x"])).unwrap(),
            Command::Launch { wait_pid: Some(42), args: os(&["harness://x"]) }
        );
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&["--install"])).unwrap(), Command::Install { wait_pid: None });
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&["--install", "--wait-pid", "7"])).unwrap(), Command::Install { wait_pid: Some(7) });
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&["--uninstall"])).unwrap(), Command::Uninstall);
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&["--version"])).unwrap(), Command::Version);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_option_counts_only_as_the_first_word() {
        // What a link to `harness:--uninstall` would hand over: one argument, the whole link.
        assert_eq!(
            parse(&os(&["harness:--uninstall"])).unwrap(),
            Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: os(&["harness:--uninstall"]) }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse(&os(&["harness://x", "--uninstall"])).unwrap(),
            Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: os(&["harness://x", "--uninstall"]) }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_a_malformed_option() {
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--wait-pid"])).unwrap_err().contains("needs a process id"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--wait-pid", "0"])).unwrap_err().contains("needs a process id"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--wait-pid", "x"])).unwrap_err().contains("needs a process id"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--install", "--wait-pid"])).unwrap_err().contains("unexpected arguments"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--install", "extra"])).unwrap_err().contains("unexpected arguments"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--uninstall", "now"])).unwrap_err().contains("unexpected arguments"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_launch_root_is_the_programs_folder_unless_the_tests_name_one() {
        let exe = Path::new("/R/Harness.exe");
        assert_eq!(launch_root(exe, |_| None), Some(PathBuf::from("/R")));
        let env = |key: &str| (key == INSTALL_ROOT_ENV).then(|| OsString::from("/T"));
        assert_eq!(launch_root(exe, env), Some(PathBuf::from("/T")));
        assert_eq!(launch_root(Path::new("Harness.exe"), |_| None), None);
    }
}
````

  Create `pty/src/desktop/pointer.rs`. It adds to B's `single_segment` what a Windows folder name needs: no device name
  and no trailing dot or space.

````rust
//! `current` and `previous`, the install's two pointer files. Each holds one line naming a version folder in `app\`,
//! by B's rules (`launcher::single_segment`, `launcher::read_pointer`): UTF-8 with no BOM written (one read is
//! dropped, as Notepad writes one), CRLF or LF, and one path segment. A version folder name is also never a name
//! Windows keeps for a device (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`…, with or without an extension) and never ends in a dot or a
//! space, which Windows drops: `1.2.3.` would open `1.2.3`.
//!
//! A write goes to `<name>.tmp`, is flushed, then renamed over the pointer, so a reader sees the old value or the
//! new one, never half of one.

use std::fs;
use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::path::Path;

use crate::launcher::{read_pointer, single_segment};

pub const CURRENT: &str = "current";
pub const PREVIOUS: &str = "previous";

fn reserved(value: &str) -> bool {
    let stem = value.split('.').next().unwrap_or("").trim_end().to_ascii_uppercase();
    let numbered = |prefix: &str| {
        stem.len() == 4 && stem.starts_with(prefix) && matches!(stem.as_bytes()[3], b'1'..=b'9')
    };
    matches!(stem.as_str(), "CON" | "PRN" | "AUX" | "NUL" | "CONIN$" | "CONOUT$") || numbered("COM") || numbered("LPT")
}

/// Whether [value] may name a version folder.
pub fn valid(value: &str) -> bool {
    single_segment(value)
        && !reserved(value)
        && !value.ends_with(['.', ' '])
        && !value.chars().any(|c| c.is_control() || matches!(c, '<' | '>' | '"' | '|' | '?' | '*'))
}

/// The version folder [file] names.
pub fn read(file: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    let value = read_pointer(file)?;
    if !valid(&value) {
        return Err(format!("{} names {value:?}, which is not one version folder", file.display()));
    }
    Ok(value)
}

/// Point [file] at [value], through a flushed temporary file and a rename.
pub fn write(file: &Path, value: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    if !valid(value) {
        return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, format!("{value:?} is not one version folder")));
    }
    let tmp = file.with_extension("tmp");
    let written = (|| {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp);
        let mut out = fs::File::create(&tmp)?;
        out.write_all(format!("{value}\r\n").as_bytes())?;
        out.sync_all()?;
        drop(out);
        crate::files::rename(&tmp, file)
    })();
    if written.is_err() {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp);
    }
    written
}

/// Remove [file]; a pointer that is not there is already removed.
pub fn remove(file: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    match fs::remove_file(file) {
        Err(err) if err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(()),
        done => done,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn writes_one_line_with_crlf_and_reads_it_back() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let file = dir.path().join(CURRENT);
        write(&file, "1.2.3").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs::read(&file).unwrap(), b"1.2.3\r\n");
        assert_eq!(read(&file).unwrap(), "1.2.3");
        // Overwritten in place, and no temporary file is left.
        write(&file, "1.2.4-dev.win1").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read(&file).unwrap(), "1.2.4-dev.win1");
        assert!(!dir.path().join("current.tmp").exists());
    }

    #[test]
    fn reads_lf_and_a_byte_order_mark_as_b_does() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let file = dir.path().join(PREVIOUS);
        fs::write(&file, "\u{feff}1.0.0\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read(&file).unwrap(), "1.0.0");
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_anything_but_one_version_folder() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let file = dir.path().join(CURRENT);
        for bad in ["..", "a/b", r"a\b", "C:x", "1.2.3.", "CON", "nul.txt", "com1", "LPT9.1", "a*b", "a\"b"] {
            assert!(!valid(bad), "{bad:?}");
            fs::write(&file, format!("{bad}\r\n")).unwrap();
            assert!(read(&file).is_err(), "{bad:?}");
            assert_eq!(write(&file, bad).unwrap_err().kind(), io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "{bad:?}");
        }
        // A trailing space never reaches a read (the line is trimmed), but a write refuses it.
        assert!(!valid("1.2.3 "));
        for good in ["1.2.3", "0.3.120-dev.abc123", "COM10", "console"] {
            assert!(valid(good), "{good:?}");
        }
        assert!(read(&dir.path().join("missing")).unwrap_err().contains("cannot read"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn removing_a_missing_pointer_is_not_an_error() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        remove(&dir.path().join(PREVIOUS)).unwrap();
        write(&dir.path().join(PREVIOUS), "1.0.0").unwrap();
        remove(&dir.path().join(PREVIOUS)).unwrap();
        assert!(!dir.path().join(PREVIOUS).exists());
    }
}

  Create `pty/src/desktop/system.rs`:

````rust
//! What the launcher asks of Windows, behind one trait: the launch, install and uninstall steps are plain Rust over
//! files, and these are the calls around them. [Real] makes them (win.rs on Windows; on Unix the few that exist
//! there), and the unit tests use [Fake], so every step runs in `cargo test` on any OS.

use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::io;
use std::path::Path;
use std::time::Duration;

pub trait System {
    /// Start `exe` from `dir` with `args`: its process id and creation time.
    fn start_app(&mut self, exe: &Path, dir: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> io::Result<(u32, u64)>;
    /// Wait up to `wait` for `pid` to end.
    fn wait_for_exit(&mut self, pid: u32, wait: Duration);
    fn say(&mut self, text: &str);
    fn now_ms(&mut self) -> u64;
}

/// Set by the tests that run the real program: messages go to stderr instead of a message box.
pub const NO_DIALOG_ENV: &str = "HARNESS_DESKTOP_NO_DIALOG";

/// This computer's.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Real;

/// A message for the person: a message box on Windows (there is no console), stderr elsewhere.
pub fn say(text: &str) {
    Real.say(text)
}

impl System for Real {
    fn start_app(&mut self, exe: &Path, dir: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> io::Result<(u32, u64)> {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            super::win::start_app(exe, dir, args)
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
            use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
            Command::new(exe)
                .args(args)
                .current_dir(dir)
                .stdin(Stdio::null())
                .stdout(Stdio::null())
                .stderr(Stdio::null())
                .process_group(0)
                .spawn()
                .map(|child| (child.id(), 0))
        }
    }

    fn wait_for_exit(&mut self, pid: u32, wait: Duration) {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            super::win::wait_for_exit(pid, wait)
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + wait;
            while unsafe { libc::kill(pid as i32, 0) } == 0 && std::time::Instant::now() < deadline {
                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
            }
        }
    }

    fn say(&mut self, text: &str) {
        // The tests run the real program, where a message box would wait for a click nobody makes.
        if cfg!(unix) || std::env::var_os(NO_DIALOG_ENV).is_some() {
            eprintln!("{text}");
            return;
        }
        #[cfg(windows)]
        super::win::message_box(text);
    }

    fn now_ms(&mut self) -> u64 {
        std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).map(|d| d.as_millis() as u64).unwrap_or(0)
    }
}

/// A recording stand-in for the unit tests.
#[cfg(test)]
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Fake {
    /// (exe, dir, args) of each start.
    pub started: Vec<(std::path::PathBuf, std::path::PathBuf, Vec<OsString>)>,
    pub fail_start: bool,
    pub waited: Vec<u32>,
    pub said: Vec<String>,
    pub now: u64,
}

#[cfg(test)]
impl System for Fake {
    fn start_app(&mut self, exe: &Path, dir: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> io::Result<(u32, u64)> {
        if self.fail_start {
            return Err(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied));
        }
        self.started.push((exe.to_path_buf(), dir.to_path_buf(), args.to_vec()));
        Ok((99 + self.started.len() as u32, self.started.len() as u64))
    }
    fn wait_for_exit(&mut self, pid: u32, _wait: Duration) {
        self.waited.push(pid);
    }
    fn say(&mut self, text: &str) {
        self.said.push(text.to_owned());
    }
    fn now_ms(&mut self) -> u64 {
        self.now += 1_000;
        1_000_000 + self.now
    }
}
````

  Create `pty/src/desktop/win.rs`. The app gets no inherited handle (a GUI app has no stdio to give), and leaves the
  launcher's job through B's `launcher::start`, whose warning goes to `launch.log`:

````rust
//! The Windows calls behind system.rs's [Real](super::system::Real): starting the app, waiting for a process and
//! the message box.

use std::ffi::{OsStr, OsString};
use std::io;
use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
use std::ptr::{null, null_mut};
use std::time::Duration;

use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, FILETIME, HANDLE};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
    CreateProcessW, GetProcessTimes, OpenProcess, PROCESS_INFORMATION, PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE, STARTUPINFOW,
    WaitForSingleObject,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{MB_ICONINFORMATION, MB_OK, MB_SETFOREGROUND, MessageBoxW};

pub fn wide(text: &OsStr) -> Vec<u16> {
    text.encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
}

pub fn message_box(text: &str) {
    let text = wide(OsStr::new(text));
    let caption = wide(OsStr::new(super::DISPLAY_NAME));
    unsafe { MessageBoxW(null_mut(), text.as_ptr(), caption.as_ptr(), MB_OK | MB_ICONINFORMATION | MB_SETFOREGROUND) };
}

/// `"<exe>" <args>`, each argument quoted as the C runtime splits it back (launcher::quote_arg).
pub fn command_line(exe: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> Vec<u16> {
    let mut line = vec![b'"' as u16];
    line.extend(exe.as_os_str().encode_wide());
    line.push(b'"' as u16);
    for arg in args {
        line.push(b' ' as u16);
        crate::launcher::quote_arg(&arg.encode_wide().collect::<Vec<u16>>(), &mut line);
    }
    line
}

fn filetime(time: FILETIME) -> u64 {
    (u64::from(time.dwHighDateTime) << 32) | u64::from(time.dwLowDateTime)
}

/// A process's creation time, which tells it apart from a later process given the same pid.
fn created(process: HANDLE) -> u64 {
    let zero = FILETIME { dwLowDateTime: 0, dwHighDateTime: 0 };
    let (mut creation, mut exit, mut kernel, mut user) = (zero, zero, zero, zero);
    if unsafe { GetProcessTimes(process, &mut creation, &mut exit, &mut kernel, &mut user) } == 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    filetime(creation)
}

/// Start [exe] with no inherited handle, outside this launcher's job when the job allows it (launcher::start): a
/// pane's job would end the app with the pane. Its pid and creation time.
pub fn start_app(exe: &Path, dir: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> io::Result<(u32, u64)> {
    let application = wide(exe.as_os_str());
    let directory = wide(dir.as_os_str());
    let spawn = |flags: u32| -> io::Result<(u32, u64)> {
        let mut line = command_line(exe, args);
        line.push(0);
        let mut startup: STARTUPINFOW = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        startup.cb = std::mem::size_of::<STARTUPINFOW>() as u32;
        let mut info: PROCESS_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        let ok = unsafe {
            CreateProcessW(application.as_ptr(), line.as_mut_ptr(), null(), null(), 0, flags, null(), directory.as_ptr(), &startup, &mut info)
        };
        if ok == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        let made = (info.dwProcessId, created(info.hProcess));
        unsafe {
            CloseHandle(info.hThread);
            CloseHandle(info.hProcess);
        }
        Ok(made)
    };
    let mut made = None;
    let started = crate::launcher::start(
        |flags| {
            spawn(flags).map(|pid_created| {
                made = Some(pid_created);
                pid_created.0
            })
        },
        |warning| super::launch::log(dir.parent().and_then(Path::parent).unwrap_or(dir), &warning),
    );
    started.map(|_| made.unwrap_or((0, 0)))
}

pub fn wait_for_exit(pid: u32, wait: Duration) {
    let process = unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE, 0, pid) };
    if process.is_null() {
        return;
    }
    unsafe {
        WaitForSingleObject(process, wait.as_millis().min(u128::from(u32::MAX - 1)) as u32);
        CloseHandle(process);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::path::PathBuf;

    #[test]
    fn the_command_line_splits_back_into_the_link() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::LocalFree;
        use windows_sys::Win32::UI::Shell::CommandLineToArgvW;
        let exe = PathBuf::from(r"C:\Users\Nguyễn Văn A' & 100% !x\AppData\Local\Programs\Harness\app\1.2.3\harness-desktop.exe");
        let args = [OsString::from("harness://notification/m/a b"), OsString::from(r#"a\"b"#)];
        let mut line = command_line(&exe, &args);
        line.push(0);
        let mut n = 0i32;
        let argv = unsafe { CommandLineToArgvW(line.as_ptr(), &mut n) };
        let words: Vec<String> = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(argv, n as usize) }
            .iter()
            .map(|&w| {
                let len = (0..).take_while(|&i| unsafe { *w.add(i) } != 0).count();
                String::from_utf16_lossy(unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(w, len) })
            })
            .collect();
        unsafe { LocalFree(argv.cast()) };
        assert_eq!(words, [exe.to_string_lossy().into_owned(), "harness://notification/m/a b".into(), r#"a\"b"#.into()]);
    }
}
````

  Create `pty/src/desktop/launch.rs`:

````rust
//! The launch path: `Harness.exe [--wait-pid <pid>] [<link>...]` starts `app\<current>\harness-desktop.exe` from its
//! version folder with the same arguments, and exits. What it did not manage goes to `launch.log` beside it, kept to
//! [LOG_MAX_BYTES].

use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::fs;
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::Path;
use std::time::Duration;

use super::pointer::{self, CURRENT};
use super::system::System;
use super::{APP_DIR, APP_EXE, EXIT_BROKEN, EXIT_OK, EXIT_SPAWN};

pub const LOG: &str = "launch.log";
/// Past this the log keeps its newer half.
pub const LOG_MAX_BYTES: u64 = 64 * 1024;
/// How long `--wait-pid` waits for the app being replaced to end.
pub const WAIT_FOR_REPLACED: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15);

/// One line in `<root>\launch.log`. When the line would take the file past [LOG_MAX_BYTES], the older half goes
/// first, from a line's start. A log that cannot be written is not a second failure.
pub fn log(root: &Path, message: &str) {
    let path = root.join(LOG);
    let seconds = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).map(|d| d.as_secs()).unwrap_or(0);
    let line = format!("{seconds} Harness.exe: {message}\n");
    if let Ok(meta) = fs::metadata(&path)
        && meta.len() + line.len() as u64 > LOG_MAX_BYTES
        && let Ok(text) = fs::read(&path)
    {
        let from = text.len().saturating_sub((LOG_MAX_BYTES / 2) as usize);
        let start = text[from..].iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n').map(|i| from + i + 1).unwrap_or(text.len());
        let _ = fs::write(&path, &text[start..]);
    }
    if let Ok(mut file) = fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(&path) {
        let _ = file.write_all(line.as_bytes());
    }
}

fn broken(root: &Path, reason: &str, system: &mut impl System) -> i32 {
    log(root, reason);
    system.say(&format!("Harness cannot start: {reason}. Download Harness again and open it to repair it."));
    EXIT_BROKEN
}

/// The launch: see the module comment.
pub fn run(root: &Path, wait_pid: Option<u32>, args: &[OsString], system: &mut impl System) -> i32 {
    if let Some(pid) = wait_pid {
        system.wait_for_exit(pid, WAIT_FOR_REPLACED);
    }
    let Ok(version) = pointer::read(&root.join(CURRENT)) else {
        return broken(root, "`current` is missing or does not name one version folder", system);
    };
    let dir = root.join(APP_DIR).join(&version);
    let exe = dir.join(APP_EXE);
    if !exe.is_file() {
        return broken(root, &format!("app\\{version} has no {APP_EXE}"), system);
    }
    match system.start_app(&exe, &dir, args) {
        Ok(_) => EXIT_OK,
        Err(err) => {
            log(root, &format!("could not start {}: {err}", exe.display()));
            system.say(&format!("Harness could not start: {err}."));
            EXIT_SPAWN
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::desktop::system::Fake;

    /// An install with these version folders (each with its exe) and `current`.
    fn install(versions: &[&str], current: Option<&str>) -> tempfile::TempDir {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        for version in versions {
            let folder = dir.path().join(APP_DIR).join(version);
            fs::create_dir_all(&folder).unwrap();
            fs::write(folder.join(APP_EXE), b"").unwrap();
        }
        if let Some(current) = current {
            pointer::write(&dir.path().join(CURRENT), current).unwrap();
        }
        dir
    }

    fn os(args: &[&str]) -> Vec<OsString> {
        args.iter().map(OsString::from).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn starts_the_current_version_from_its_folder_with_the_links() {
        let dir = install(&["1.2.3"], Some("1.2.3"));
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        assert_eq!(run(dir.path(), None, &os(&["harness://x y"]), &mut system), EXIT_OK);
        let folder = dir.path().join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3");
        assert_eq!(system.started, vec![(folder.join(APP_EXE), folder.clone(), os(&["harness://x y"]))]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn waits_for_the_app_being_replaced_first() {
        let dir = install(&["1.2.3"], Some("1.2.3"));
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        run(dir.path(), Some(77), &[], &mut system);
        assert_eq!(system.waited, vec![77]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_broken_install_says_so_and_exits_3() {
        let dir = install(&[], None);
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        assert_eq!(run(dir.path(), None, &[], &mut system), EXIT_BROKEN);
        assert!(system.said[0].contains("Download Harness again"), "{:?}", system.said);
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(LOG)).unwrap().contains("`current` is missing"));
        let dir = install(&[], Some("1.2.3"));
        assert_eq!(run(dir.path(), None, &[], &mut system), EXIT_BROKEN);
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(LOG)).unwrap().contains("has no harness-desktop.exe"));
        assert!(system.started.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_failed_start_says_so_and_exits_4() {
        let dir = install(&["1.2.3"], Some("1.2.3"));
        let mut system = Fake { fail_start: true, ..Fake::default() };
        assert_eq!(run(dir.path(), None, &[], &mut system), EXIT_SPAWN);
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(LOG)).unwrap().contains("could not start"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_log_keeps_its_newer_half_past_its_size() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let old = "x".repeat(99) + "\n";
        fs::write(dir.path().join(LOG), old.repeat((LOG_MAX_BYTES / 100) as usize)).unwrap();
        log(dir.path(), "the newest line");
        let text = fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(LOG)).unwrap();
        assert!(text.len() as u64 <= LOG_MAX_BYTES / 2 + 100, "{}", text.len());
        assert!(text.starts_with('x') && text.ends_with("Harness.exe: the newest line\n"));
    }
}
````

### Task C4.2: `Harness.exe --install`

**Files:**
- Modify: `pty/Cargo.toml`: two `windows-sys` features and a second `[[test]]`.
- Modify (replace): `pty/src/desktop/mod.rs`, `pty/src/desktop/system.rs`, `pty/src/desktop/win.rs`.
- Modify: `pty/src/desktop/launch.rs`: `heal_protocol_key`.
- Create: `pty/src/desktop/registry.rs`, `pty/src/desktop/shortcut.rs`, `pty/src/desktop/install.rs`.
- Create: `pty/tests/desktop_install.rs`.
- Modify: `.github/workflows/windows-desktop.yml`: the "Harness.exe tests" step runs `desktop_install` too.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: C4.1's `launch::{log, WAIT_FOR_REPLACED}`, `pointer`, `System`.
- Produces:
  - `desktop::Paths { own, install, programs, registry: String, profile }`, `Paths::resolve(own_exe, env, known)`,
    `Paths::current()`, `Paths::{launcher, shortcut, running_installed}`, `desktop::KnownFolder`,
    `desktop::same_folder(&Path, &Path) -> bool`;
  - `desktop::install::{run(&Paths, wait_pid, &mut impl System) -> Result<Outcome, String>, main(...) -> i32, newer, copy_tree, replace_file}`
    with `enum Outcome { Installed { version }, AlreadyInstalled { version }, NewerInstalled { zip, installed } }`;
    it takes the `wait_pid` and the `System` it acts through;
  - `desktop::registry::{Key, Value, SCHEME, UNINSTALL_KEY, protocol_key, protocol_command_key, open_command, protocol_keys, uninstall_keys}`;
  - `desktop::shortcut::{LINK_NAME, create(link, target, icon, dir, aumid), read(link) -> (PathBuf, String)}` (Windows);
  - `desktop::win::{known_folder, QUIT_MESSAGE, app_processes, quit_app, read_value, write_keys, delete_key}`;
  - `desktop::launch::heal_protocol_key(root, registry_root, &mut impl System)`.
- `windows-sys` features this task adds, exactly: `Win32_System_Com` (`CoInitializeEx`, `CoCreateInstance`,
  `CoTaskMemFree`, `CoUninitialize`, `CLSCTX_INPROC_SERVER`, `COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED`) and `Win32_System_Registry`
  (`RegCreateKeyExW`, `RegSetValueExW`, `RegGetValueW`, `RegDeleteTreeW`, `RegCloseKey`, and the gate of
  `ShellExecuteExW` the scheme test uses). Already on: `Win32_UI_Shell` (`SHGetKnownFolderPath`, `FOLDERID_*`,
  `KF_FLAG_CREATE`, the `ShellLink` CLSID), `Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging` (`EnumWindows`, `GetClassNameW`,
  `GetWindowThreadProcessId`, `PostMessageW`, `RegisterWindowMessageW`), `Win32_System_Threading` (`OpenProcess`,
  `QueryFullProcessImageNameW`, `TerminateProcess`). windows-sys has no COM interfaces, so `IShellLinkW`,
  `IPersistFile`, `IPropertyStore`, `PKEY_AppUserModel_ID` and a one-pointer `PROPVARIANT` are declared in
  `shortcut.rs`.
- The `harness://` key heals on each launch (spec §2.3): the installed launcher reads
  `<root>\Classes\harness\shell\open\command` once and rewrites the scheme's keys only when they differ. C3.2 may rely
  on it. A zip's copy never takes the links.

  Create `pty/tests/desktop_install.rs`. Off Windows its main runs nothing. On Windows it installs a zip extracted in
  a profile named `Nguyễn Văn A' & 100% !x` (Review Focus 1), reads every value back, reads the shortcut's target and
  AUMID through COM, opens an older zip, and registers a scheme of its own (`harness-test-<id>`, never `harness`) under
  the real `HKCU\Software\Classes` to open a link through `ShellExecuteExW`, as a browser does; that key and the
  `Software\HarnessTest\<id>` root are removed when the test ends.

````rust
//! Windows: the real `Harness.exe --install` from an extracted zip, in a profile named as Review
//! Focus 1 asks, with every override set (HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT, _PROGRAMS_DIR, _REGISTRY_ROOT, USERPROFILE,
//! TEMP), so nothing reaches the real Start Menu, `harness://` key or uninstall entry. One test also registers a
//! scheme of its own and opens it through the shell, which is how a browser opens `harness://`. The app is this
//! test's own executable (desktop_common). Nothing runs off Windows.
mod desktop_common;

fn main() {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    windows::main();
}

#[cfg(windows)]
mod windows {
    use std::fs;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    use std::process::{Command, Output};

    use harness_pty::desktop::{registry, shortcut, win};

    use super::desktop_common::{self, *};

    pub fn main() {
        desktop_common::main(&[
            ("installs_registers_and_opens", installs_registers_and_opens),
            ("an_older_zip_opens_the_installed_harness", an_older_zip_opens_the_installed_harness),
            ("the_shell_opens_a_link_through_the_installed_launcher", the_shell_opens_a_link_through_the_installed_launcher),
        ]);
    }

    /// A profile, a zip of [version] extracted in its Downloads, and the overrides that keep the test to itself.
    struct World {
        dir: tempfile::TempDir,
        profile: PathBuf,
        zip: PathBuf,
        install: PathBuf,
        programs: PathBuf,
        temp: PathBuf,
        /// Under HKCU: `Software\HarnessTest\<id>`, removed when the test ends.
        registry: String,
        id: String,
    }

    impl Drop for World {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            use windows_sys::Win32::System::Registry::{HKEY_CURRENT_USER, RegDeleteKeyW};
            let _ = win::delete_key(r"Software\HarnessTest", &self.id);
            // The parent too once it is empty; RegDeleteKeyW leaves one that still holds another run's key.
            let parent = win::wide(std::ffi::OsStr::new(r"Software\HarnessTest"));
            unsafe { RegDeleteKeyW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, parent.as_ptr()) };
        }
    }

    fn world() -> World {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let profile = dir.path().join(ODD_NAME);
        let id = format!("{}-{}", std::process::id(), std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_nanos());
        let world = World {
            zip: profile.join("Downloads").join("harness-desktop-1.2.3-windows-x64"),
            install: profile.join("AppData").join("Local").join("Programs").join("Harness"),
            programs: profile.join("Start Menu").join("Programs"),
            temp: profile.join("Temp"),
            registry: format!(r"Software\HarnessTest\{id}"),
            profile,
            id,
            dir,
        };
        fs::create_dir_all(&world.temp).unwrap();
        for entry in ["desktop-app-v2", "cli"] {
            fs::create_dir_all(world.profile.join(".harness").join(entry)).unwrap();
            fs::write(world.profile.join(".harness").join(entry).join("state.json"), b"{}").unwrap();
        }
        zip(&world.zip, "1.2.3");
        world
    }

    fn zip(folder: &Path, version: &str) {
        put_app(folder, version);
        point(folder, "current", version);
        fs::copy(LAUNCHER, folder.join("Harness.exe")).unwrap();
        fs::write(folder.join("Harness.ico"), b"").unwrap();
    }

    fn run(world: &World, exe: &Path, args: &[&str], out: &Path) -> Output {
        Command::new(exe)
            .args(args)
            .env("HARNESS_DESKTOP_NO_DIALOG", "1")
            .env("HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT", &world.install)
            .env("HARNESS_DESKTOP_PROGRAMS_DIR", &world.programs)
            .env("HARNESS_DESKTOP_REGISTRY_ROOT", &world.registry)
            .env("USERPROFILE", &world.profile)
            .env("TEMP", &world.temp)
            .env("TMP", &world.temp)
            .env(STANDIN_OUT, out)
            .output()
            .unwrap()
    }

    fn quoted(path: &Path) -> String {
        format!("\"{}\"", path.display())
    }

    fn number(world: &World, name: &str) -> String {
        let key = format!(r"HKCU\{}\{}", world.registry, registry::UNINSTALL_KEY);
        let output = Command::new("reg.exe").args(["query", &key, "/v", name]).output().unwrap();
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).into_owned()
    }

    /// [world], installed from its zip, with the installed app started once and its report read.
    fn installed() -> World {
        let world = world();
        let out = world.dir.path().join("installed.json");
        let output = run(&world, &world.zip.join("Harness.exe"), &["--install"], &out);
        assert!(output.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));
        // The installed copy, started through the installed launcher.
        let report = report(&out);
        assert!(same(report["cwd"].as_str().unwrap().as_ref(), &world.install.join("app").join("1.2.3")));
        world
    }

    fn value(world: &World, key: &str, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
        win::read_value(&world.registry, key, name).map(|value| value.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
    }

    fn installs_registers_and_opens() {
        let world = installed();
        let launcher = world.install.join("Harness.exe");
        assert!(launcher.is_file() && world.install.join("Harness.ico").is_file());
        assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(world.install.join("current")).unwrap(), "1.2.3\r\n");
        // Every value names the install, with the odd profile kept as it is.
        assert_eq!(value(&world, r"Classes\harness\shell\open\command", ""), Some(format!("{} \"%1\"", quoted(&launcher))));
        assert_eq!(value(&world, r"Classes\harness", "URL Protocol"), Some(String::new()));
        let uninstall = registry::UNINSTALL_KEY;
        assert_eq!(value(&world, uninstall, "DisplayName").as_deref(), Some("Harness"));
        assert_eq!(value(&world, uninstall, "DisplayVersion").as_deref(), Some("1.2.3"));
        assert_eq!(value(&world, uninstall, "Publisher").as_deref(), Some("Autonomous"));
        assert_eq!(value(&world, uninstall, "InstallLocation"), Some(world.install.display().to_string()));
        assert_eq!(value(&world, uninstall, "DisplayIcon"), Some(format!("{},0", world.install.join("Harness.ico").display())));
        assert_eq!(value(&world, uninstall, "UninstallString"), Some(format!("{} --uninstall", quoted(&launcher))));
        assert!(number(&world, "NoModify").contains("0x1") && number(&world, "NoRepair").contains("0x1"));
        let (target, aumid) = shortcut::read(&world.programs.join("Harness.lnk")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((target, aumid.as_str()), (launcher, "Autonomous.Harness"));
    }

    fn an_older_zip_opens_the_installed_harness() {
        let world = installed();
        let older = world.profile.join("Downloads").join("old");
        zip(&older, "1.0.0");
        let out = world.dir.path().join("older.json");
        let output = run(&world, &older.join("Harness.exe"), &["--install"], &out);
        assert!(output.status.success());
        assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).contains("version 1.0.0, older than the Harness 1.2.3"));
        assert!(same(report(&out)["cwd"].as_str().unwrap().as_ref(), &world.install.join("app").join("1.2.3")));
        assert!(!world.install.join("app").join("1.0.0").exists());
    }

    /// A scheme of the test's own under the real `HKCU\Software\Classes`, removed after; never `harness`.
    fn the_shell_opens_a_link_through_the_installed_launcher() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle;
        use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::WaitForSingleObject;
        use windows_sys::Win32::UI::Shell::{SEE_MASK_FLAG_NO_UI, SEE_MASK_NOCLOSEPROCESS, SHELLEXECUTEINFOW, ShellExecuteExW};

        let world = installed();
        let scheme = format!("harness-test-{}", world.id);
        struct Scheme(String);
        impl Drop for Scheme {
            fn drop(&mut self) {
                let _ = win::delete_key("Software", &registry::protocol_key(&self.0));
            }
        }
        let _registered = Scheme(scheme.clone());
        win::write_keys("Software", &registry::protocol_keys(&scheme, &world.install.join("Harness.exe"))).unwrap();
        let out = world.dir.path().join("link.json");
        // The shell starts the launcher with this process's environment.
        unsafe {
            std::env::set_var(STANDIN_OUT, &out);
            std::env::set_var("HARNESS_DESKTOP_NO_DIALOG", "1");
        }
        let link = format!("{scheme}://notification/machine/agent?x=1&y=2");
        let file = win::wide(std::ffi::OsStr::new(&link));
        let mut info: SHELLEXECUTEINFOW = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        info.cbSize = std::mem::size_of::<SHELLEXECUTEINFOW>() as u32;
        info.fMask = SEE_MASK_NOCLOSEPROCESS | SEE_MASK_FLAG_NO_UI;
        info.lpFile = file.as_ptr();
        info.nShow = 1;
        assert_ne!(unsafe { ShellExecuteExW(&mut info) }, 0, "{}", std::io::Error::last_os_error());
        if !info.hProcess.is_null() {
            unsafe {
                WaitForSingleObject(info.hProcess, 30_000);
                CloseHandle(info.hProcess);
            }
        }
        unsafe { std::env::remove_var(STANDIN_OUT) };
        let report = report(&out);
        assert_eq!(report["args"], serde_json::json!([link]));
        assert!(same(report["cwd"].as_str().unwrap().as_ref(), &world.install.join("app").join("1.2.3")));
    }
}
````

  Create `pty/src/desktop/registry.rs`:

````rust
//! The keys an install writes under `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\<root>`, where `<root>` is `Software` (or the tests'
//! `HARNESS_DESKTOP_REGISTRY_ROOT`): the `harness://` scheme and the Settings ▸ Apps entry. Here they are data;
//! win.rs writes them.
//!
//! Paths go in as the OS strings they are, never through `display()` or a re-parse, and each one that a command line
//! carries is between double quotes, which a Windows path cannot contain (Review Focus 1). The shell substitutes
//! `%1` in the open command; a profile folder whose name holds `%` followed by a digit, `*` or `~` would be read as
//! another argument by Explorer, which has no escape for it (a known limit).

use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::path::Path;

use super::{DISPLAY_NAME, PUBLISHER};

pub const SCHEME: &str = "harness";
pub const UNINSTALL_KEY: &str = r"Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\Harness";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Value {
    /// REG_SZ.
    Text(OsString),
    /// REG_DWORD.
    Number(u32),
}

/// A key, relative to the registry root, and its values; the name "" is the key's default value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Key {
    pub path: String,
    pub values: Vec<(String, Value)>,
}

pub fn protocol_key(scheme: &str) -> String {
    format!(r"Classes\{scheme}")
}

pub fn protocol_command_key(scheme: &str) -> String {
    format!(r"Classes\{scheme}\shell\open\command")
}

fn quoted(path: &Path) -> OsString {
    let mut text = OsString::from("\"");
    text.push(path.as_os_str());
    text.push("\"");
    text
}

fn text(value: impl Into<OsString>) -> Value {
    Value::Text(value.into())
}

/// `"<launcher>" "%1"`: the link as the launcher's one argument.
pub fn open_command(launcher: &Path) -> OsString {
    let mut command = quoted(launcher);
    command.push(" \"%1\"");
    command
}

/// `<scheme>://` opening [launcher]. The tests register a scheme of their own; the app's is [SCHEME].
pub fn protocol_keys(scheme: &str, launcher: &Path) -> Vec<Key> {
    vec![
        Key {
            path: protocol_key(scheme),
            values: vec![(String::new(), text(format!("URL:{DISPLAY_NAME}"))), ("URL Protocol".to_owned(), text(""))],
        },
        Key { path: protocol_command_key(scheme), values: vec![(String::new(), Value::Text(open_command(launcher)))] },
    ]
}

/// The Settings ▸ Apps entry for the install at [install], showing [icon].
pub fn uninstall_keys(install: &Path, version: &str, icon: &Path) -> Vec<Key> {
    let mut uninstall = quoted(&install.join(super::LAUNCHER_EXE));
    uninstall.push(" --uninstall");
    let mut display_icon = icon.as_os_str().to_owned();
    display_icon.push(",0");
    vec![Key {
        path: UNINSTALL_KEY.to_owned(),
        values: vec![
            ("DisplayName".to_owned(), text(DISPLAY_NAME)),
            ("DisplayVersion".to_owned(), text(version)),
            ("Publisher".to_owned(), text(PUBLISHER)),
            ("InstallLocation".to_owned(), text(install.as_os_str())),
            ("DisplayIcon".to_owned(), Value::Text(display_icon)),
            ("UninstallString".to_owned(), Value::Text(uninstall)),
            ("NoModify".to_owned(), Value::Number(1)),
            ("NoRepair".to_owned(), Value::Number(1)),
        ],
    }]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::path::PathBuf;

    /// Review Focus 1: a profile with a space, an apostrophe, `&`, `%`, `!` and letters outside ASCII.
    const PROFILE: &str = "/Users/Nguyễn Văn A' & 100% !x";

    fn value<'a>(keys: &'a [Key], path: &str, name: &str) -> &'a Value {
        let key = keys.iter().find(|key| key.path == path).unwrap();
        &key.values.iter().find(|(n, _)| n == name).unwrap().1
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_harness_scheme_opens_the_launcher_with_the_link_as_one_argument() {
        let launcher = PathBuf::from(format!("{PROFILE}/Programs/Harness/Harness.exe"));
        let keys = protocol_keys(SCHEME, &launcher);
        assert_eq!(value(&keys, r"Classes\harness", "URL Protocol"), &text(""));
        assert_eq!(value(&keys, r"Classes\harness", ""), &text("URL:Harness"));
        assert_eq!(
            value(&keys, r"Classes\harness\shell\open\command", ""),
            &text(format!("\"{PROFILE}/Programs/Harness/Harness.exe\" \"%1\""))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_uninstall_entry_has_every_value_settings_reads() {
        let install = PathBuf::from(format!("{PROFILE}/Programs/Harness"));
        let icon = install.join("Harness.ico");
        let keys = uninstall_keys(&install, "1.2.3", &icon);
        let at = |name| value(&keys, UNINSTALL_KEY, name);
        assert_eq!(at("DisplayName"), &text("Harness"));
        assert_eq!(at("DisplayVersion"), &text("1.2.3"));
        assert_eq!(at("Publisher"), &text("Autonomous"));
        assert_eq!(at("InstallLocation"), &text(format!("{PROFILE}/Programs/Harness")));
        assert_eq!(at("DisplayIcon"), &text(format!("{},0", icon.display())));
        let launcher = install.join("Harness.exe");
        assert_eq!(at("UninstallString"), &text(format!("\"{}\" --uninstall", launcher.display())));
        assert_eq!(at("NoModify"), &Value::Number(1));
        assert_eq!(at("NoRepair"), &Value::Number(1));
        assert_eq!(keys[0].values.len(), 8);
    }
}
````

  Create `pty/src/desktop/shortcut.rs`:

````rust
//! The Start Menu shortcut, `<FOLDERID_Programs>\Harness.lnk`, through the shell's COM objects: `IShellLinkW` for
//! the target, `IPropertyStore` for `System.AppUserModel.ID` (`PKEY_AppUserModel_ID`), and `IPersistFile` to save
//! it. An unpackaged app's toasts need that AUMID on a Start Menu shortcut (desktop spec section 2.1), and the app
//! sets the same one on its process, so its windows group under the shortcut a person pinned.
//!
//! windows-sys has the functions and the `ShellLink` CLSID but no COM interfaces, so the three interfaces' virtual
//! tables are declared here, in the order ShObjIdl_core.h, ObjIdl.h and PropSys.h give them. Only the slots called
//! have a type; the others are placeholders of the same size.

pub const LINK_NAME: &str = "Harness.lnk";

#[cfg(windows)]
mod com {
    use std::ffi::{OsStr, OsString, c_void};
    use std::io;
    use std::os::windows::ffi::{OsStrExt, OsStringExt};
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    use std::ptr::null_mut;

    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Com::{
        CLSCTX_INPROC_SERVER, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED, CoCreateInstance, CoInitializeEx, CoTaskMemFree, CoUninitialize,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::UI::Shell::ShellLink;
    use windows_sys::core::{GUID, HRESULT, PCWSTR, PWSTR};

    const IID_ISHELLLINKW: GUID = GUID::from_u128(0x000214f9_0000_0000_c000_000000000046);
    const IID_IPERSISTFILE: GUID = GUID::from_u128(0x0000010b_0000_0000_c000_000000000046);
    const IID_IPROPERTYSTORE: GUID = GUID::from_u128(0x886d8eeb_8cf2_4446_8d02_cdba1dbdcf99);
    /// PKEY_AppUserModel_ID: {9F4C2855-9F79-4B39-A8D0-E1D42DE1D5F3}, 5.
    const PKEY_APPUSERMODEL_ID: PropertyKey =
        PropertyKey { fmtid: GUID::from_u128(0x9f4c2855_9f79_4b39_a8d0_e1d42de1d5f3), pid: 5 };
    const VT_LPWSTR: u16 = 31;
    const STGM_READ: u32 = 0;
    /// IShellLinkW::GetPath: the path as stored, environment strings not expanded.
    const SLGP_RAWPATH: u32 = 4;

    #[repr(C)]
    struct PropertyKey {
        fmtid: GUID,
        pid: u32,
    }

    /// A PROPVARIANT holding one pointer (VT_LPWSTR): 24 bytes on a 64-bit Windows, as the real one.
    #[repr(C)]
    struct PropVariant {
        vt: u16,
        reserved: [u16; 3],
        pointer: *mut u16,
        rest: usize,
    }

    type Slot = usize;

    #[repr(C)]
    struct Unknown {
        query_interface: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, *const GUID, *mut *mut c_void) -> HRESULT,
        add_ref: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void) -> u32,
        release: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void) -> u32,
    }

    #[repr(C)]
    struct ShellLinkW {
        unknown: Unknown,
        get_path: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, PWSTR, i32, *mut c_void, u32) -> HRESULT,
        get_id_list: Slot,
        set_id_list: Slot,
        get_description: Slot,
        set_description: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, PCWSTR) -> HRESULT,
        get_working_directory: Slot,
        set_working_directory: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, PCWSTR) -> HRESULT,
        get_arguments: Slot,
        set_arguments: Slot,
        get_hotkey: Slot,
        set_hotkey: Slot,
        get_show_cmd: Slot,
        set_show_cmd: Slot,
        get_icon_location: Slot,
        set_icon_location: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, PCWSTR, i32) -> HRESULT,
        set_relative_path: Slot,
        resolve: Slot,
        set_path: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, PCWSTR) -> HRESULT,
    }

    #[repr(C)]
    struct PersistFile {
        unknown: Unknown,
        get_class_id: Slot,
        is_dirty: Slot,
        load: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, PCWSTR, u32) -> HRESULT,
        save: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, PCWSTR, i32) -> HRESULT,
        save_completed: Slot,
        get_cur_file: Slot,
    }

    #[repr(C)]
    struct PropertyStore {
        unknown: Unknown,
        get_count: Slot,
        get_at: Slot,
        get_value: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, *const PropertyKey, *mut PropVariant) -> HRESULT,
        set_value: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void, *const PropertyKey, *const PropVariant) -> HRESULT,
        commit: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut c_void) -> HRESULT,
    }

    fn check(hr: HRESULT) -> io::Result<()> {
        if hr < 0 { Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(hr)) } else { Ok(()) }
    }

    fn wide(text: &OsStr) -> Vec<u16> {
        text.encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
    }

    /// COM on this thread for as long as it lives.
    struct Apartment(bool);
    impl Apartment {
        fn enter() -> Apartment {
            // S_FALSE (already entered) is a success to undo as well; RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE is a usable apartment.
            Apartment(unsafe { CoInitializeEx(std::ptr::null(), COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED as u32) } >= 0)
        }
    }
    impl Drop for Apartment {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            if self.0 {
                unsafe { CoUninitialize() };
            }
        }
    }

    /// One interface pointer, released when dropped.
    struct Object(*mut c_void);
    impl Object {
        fn table<T>(&self) -> &T {
            unsafe { &**(self.0 as *mut *const T) }
        }
        fn query(&self, iid: &GUID) -> io::Result<Object> {
            let mut out = null_mut();
            check(unsafe { (self.table::<Unknown>().query_interface)(self.0, iid, &mut out) })?;
            Ok(Object(out))
        }
    }
    impl Drop for Object {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            unsafe { (self.table::<Unknown>().release)(self.0) };
        }
    }

    fn shell_link() -> io::Result<Object> {
        let mut out = null_mut();
        check(unsafe { CoCreateInstance(&ShellLink, null_mut(), CLSCTX_INPROC_SERVER, &IID_ISHELLLINKW, &mut out) })?;
        Ok(Object(out))
    }

    pub fn create(link: &Path, target: &Path, icon: &Path, dir: &Path, aumid: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
        let _apartment = Apartment::enter();
        let object = shell_link()?;
        let table = object.table::<ShellLinkW>();
        unsafe {
            check((table.set_path)(object.0, wide(target.as_os_str()).as_ptr()))?;
            check((table.set_working_directory)(object.0, wide(dir.as_os_str()).as_ptr()))?;
            check((table.set_description)(object.0, wide(OsStr::new(super::super::DISPLAY_NAME)).as_ptr()))?;
            check((table.set_icon_location)(object.0, wide(icon.as_os_str()).as_ptr(), 0))?;
        }
        let store = object.query(&IID_IPROPERTYSTORE)?;
        let id = wide(OsStr::new(aumid));
        let value = PropVariant { vt: VT_LPWSTR, reserved: [0; 3], pointer: id.as_ptr() as *mut u16, rest: 0 };
        unsafe {
            check((store.table::<PropertyStore>().set_value)(store.0, &PKEY_APPUSERMODEL_ID, &value))?;
            check((store.table::<PropertyStore>().commit)(store.0))?;
        }
        if let Some(parent) = link.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
        }
        let file = object.query(&IID_IPERSISTFILE)?;
        check(unsafe { (file.table::<PersistFile>().save)(file.0, wide(link.as_os_str()).as_ptr(), 1) })
    }

    /// The target and the AUMID a shortcut holds (the tests', and a check after an install).
    pub fn read(link: &Path) -> io::Result<(PathBuf, String)> {
        let _apartment = Apartment::enter();
        let object = shell_link()?;
        let file = object.query(&IID_IPERSISTFILE)?;
        check(unsafe { (file.table::<PersistFile>().load)(file.0, wide(link.as_os_str()).as_ptr(), STGM_READ) })?;
        let mut buffer = vec![0u16; 32_768];
        check(unsafe {
            (object.table::<ShellLinkW>().get_path)(object.0, buffer.as_mut_ptr(), buffer.len() as i32, null_mut(), SLGP_RAWPATH)
        })?;
        let length = buffer.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(buffer.len());
        let target = PathBuf::from(OsString::from_wide(&buffer[..length]));
        let store = object.query(&IID_IPROPERTYSTORE)?;
        let mut value = PropVariant { vt: 0, reserved: [0; 3], pointer: null_mut(), rest: 0 };
        check(unsafe { (store.table::<PropertyStore>().get_value)(store.0, &PKEY_APPUSERMODEL_ID, &mut value) })?;
        let mut aumid = String::new();
        if value.vt == VT_LPWSTR && !value.pointer.is_null() {
            let length = (0..).take_while(|&i| unsafe { *value.pointer.add(i) } != 0).count();
            aumid = String::from_utf16_lossy(unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(value.pointer, length) });
            unsafe { CoTaskMemFree(value.pointer as *const c_void) };
        }
        Ok((target, aumid))
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_variant_is_the_size_windows_reads() {
        assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<PropVariant>(), if cfg!(target_pointer_width = "64") { 24 } else { 16 });
    }
}

pub use com::{create, read};

  Create `pty/src/desktop/install.rs`:

````rust
//! `Harness.exe --install [--wait-pid <pid>]`, run from an extracted zip (desktop spec section 3.3). The zip has the
//! install's shape (`Harness.exe`, `Harness.ico`, `current`, `app\<ver>\`), and the install is, in order:
//! 1. `app\<ver>` copied to `<install>\app\<ver>.staging`, then renamed to `app\<ver>`;
//! 2. `Harness.exe` and `Harness.ico` copied beside it, each through `<name>.new` and a rename;
//! 3. `previous` (the version installed before, if any) and `current` written;
//! 4. the Start Menu shortcut, `<FOLDERID_Programs>\Harness.lnk`, with the AUMID;
//! 5. the `harness://` key and the Settings ▸ Apps entry;
//! 6. the installed `Harness.exe` started.
//!
//! With the same version installed it only does 4 to 6 (which also repairs them) and opens it. With a newer one
//! installed it says so and opens that one. Before it changes an install it waits for `--wait-pid` (the app that
//! ran it, which still holds the single-instance mutex) and asks any app still running from the install to quit.
//!
//! A copy never follows a link: a symlink or junction inside the zip folder is skipped, and so is `.started`, which
//! belongs to the copy that ran.

use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::Duration;

use super::launch;
use super::pointer::{self, CURRENT, PREVIOUS};
use super::registry;
use super::system::System;
use super::{APP_DIR, APP_EXE, EXIT_FAILED, EXIT_OK, ICON, LAUNCHER_EXE, Paths, STARTED_MARKER};

/// How long a running app from the install has to quit.
pub const QUIT_WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Outcome {
    Installed { version: String },
    AlreadyInstalled { version: String },
    NewerInstalled { zip: String, installed: String },
}

/// `X.Y.Z` of [version], without its prerelease or build: the rule DesktopUpdater's `semverGt` applies.
fn core(version: &str) -> Option<(u64, u64, u64)> {
    let mut parts = version.split(['-', '+']).next()?.split('.');
    let numbers = (parts.next()?.parse().ok()?, parts.next()?.parse().ok()?, parts.next()?.parse().ok()?);
    parts.next().is_none().then_some(numbers)
}

/// Whether [a] is strictly newer than [b].
pub fn newer(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
    matches!((core(a), core(b)), (Some(a), Some(b)) if a > b)
}

/// The same tree under [to], which must not exist, without links and without `.started`.
pub fn copy_tree(from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    fs::create_dir(to)?;
    for entry in fs::read_dir(from)? {
        let entry = entry?;
        let kind = entry.file_type()?;
        if kind.is_symlink() || entry.file_name() == STARTED_MARKER {
            continue;
        }
        let target = to.join(entry.file_name());
        if kind.is_dir() {
            copy_tree(&entry.path(), &target)?;
        } else {
            fs::copy(entry.path(), &target)?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// A folder and what is in it, gone; a link is removed as a link (std's remove_dir_all never follows one).
fn remove_folder(path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    match fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
        Err(err) if err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(()),
        Err(err) => Err(err),
        Ok(meta) if meta.is_symlink() => fs::remove_dir(path).or_else(|_| fs::remove_file(path)),
        Ok(_) => fs::remove_dir_all(path),
    }
}

/// [from] in place of [to], through `<to>.new`; the old file is renamed to `<to>.old` first, since a running
/// program can be renamed but not overwritten. An old `.old` that is still held stays for the next cleanup.
pub fn replace_file(from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    let with = |suffix: &str| {
        let mut name = to.as_os_str().to_owned();
        name.push(suffix);
        PathBuf::from(name)
    };
    let (new, old) = (with(".new"), with(".old"));
    let _ = fs::remove_file(&new);
    fs::copy(from, &new)?;
    if to.exists() {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&old);
        crate::files::rename(to, &old)?;
    }
    if let Err(err) = crate::files::rename(&new, to) {
        let _ = crate::files::rename(&old, to);
        return Err(err);
    }
    let _ = fs::remove_file(&old);
    Ok(())
}

/// The version an install's `current` names, when its folder has the app.
fn installed_version(install: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    pointer::read(&install.join(CURRENT)).ok().filter(|version| install.join(APP_DIR).join(version).join(APP_EXE).is_file())
}

/// Steps 4 and 5: everything outside the install folder. Every value names the install, never the zip.
fn register(paths: &Paths, version: &str, system: &mut impl System) -> Result<(), String> {
    let launcher = paths.launcher();
    let icon = if paths.install.join(ICON).is_file() { paths.install.join(ICON) } else { launcher.clone() };
    system
        .create_shortcut(&paths.shortcut(), &launcher, &icon, &paths.install)
        .map_err(|err| format!("could not create the Start Menu shortcut {}: {err}", paths.shortcut().display()))?;
    let mut keys = registry::protocol_keys(registry::SCHEME, &launcher);
    keys.extend(registry::uninstall_keys(&paths.install, version, &icon));
    system.write_keys(&paths.registry, &keys).map_err(|err| format!("could not register Harness with Windows: {err}"))
}

/// Steps 1 to 3.
fn copy_in(paths: &Paths, version: &str, installed: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), String> {
    let app = paths.install.join(APP_DIR);
    fs::create_dir_all(&app).map_err(|err| format!("could not create {}: {err}", app.display()))?;
    let source = paths.own.join(APP_DIR).join(version);
    let staging = app.join(format!("{version}.staging"));
    let target = app.join(version);
    remove_folder(&staging).map_err(|err| format!("could not clear {}: {err}", staging.display()))?;
    if let Err(err) = copy_tree(&source, &staging) {
        let _ = remove_folder(&staging);
        return Err(format!("could not copy {} into {}: {err}", source.display(), staging.display()));
    }
    // A folder of this version that is not in use (a half-done earlier install) makes way.
    remove_folder(&target).map_err(|err| format!("could not replace {}: {err}", target.display()))?;
    crate::files::rename(&staging, &target).map_err(|err| format!("could not move {} into place: {err}", staging.display()))?;
    replace_file(&paths.own.join(LAUNCHER_EXE), &paths.launcher()).map_err(|err| format!("could not copy Harness.exe: {err}"))?;
    if paths.own.join(ICON).is_file() {
        replace_file(&paths.own.join(ICON), &paths.install.join(ICON)).map_err(|err| format!("could not copy {ICON}: {err}"))?;
    }
    if let Some(installed) = installed.filter(|installed| *installed != version) {
        pointer::write(&paths.install.join(PREVIOUS), installed).map_err(|err| format!("could not write previous: {err}"))?;
    }
    pointer::write(&paths.install.join(CURRENT), version).map_err(|err| format!("could not write current: {err}"))
}

pub fn run(paths: &Paths, wait_pid: Option<u32>, system: &mut impl System) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
    let version = pointer::read(&paths.own.join(CURRENT))?;
    for needed in [paths.own.join(APP_DIR).join(&version).join(APP_EXE), paths.own.join(LAUNCHER_EXE)] {
        if !needed.is_file() {
            return Err(format!("this copy of Harness has no {}", needed.display()));
        }
    }
    if let Some(pid) = wait_pid {
        system.wait_for_exit(pid, launch::WAIT_FOR_REPLACED);
    }
    let installed = if paths.running_installed() { Some(version.clone()) } else { installed_version(&paths.install) };
    let outcome = match installed.as_deref() {
        Some(same) if same == version => Outcome::AlreadyInstalled { version: version.clone() },
        Some(newer_one) if newer(newer_one, &version) => {
            Outcome::NewerInstalled { zip: version.clone(), installed: newer_one.to_owned() }
        }
        _ => {
            system.quit_app(&paths.install, QUIT_WAIT);
            copy_in(paths, &version, installed.as_deref())?;
            Outcome::Installed { version: version.clone() }
        }
    };
    let registered = match &outcome {
        Outcome::NewerInstalled { installed, .. } => installed.clone(),
        Outcome::Installed { version } | Outcome::AlreadyInstalled { version } => version.clone(),
    };
    register(paths, &registered, system)?;
    Ok(outcome)
}

/// The program's `--install`: [run], then the installed Harness started, and every failure said.
pub fn main(paths: &Paths, wait_pid: Option<u32>, system: &mut impl System) -> i32 {
    let outcome = match run(paths, wait_pid, system) {
        Ok(outcome) => outcome,
        Err(err) => {
            launch::log(&paths.install, &format!("install failed: {err}"));
            system.say(&format!("Harness could not install itself: {err}."));
            return EXIT_FAILED;
        }
    };
    match &outcome {
        Outcome::Installed { version } => launch::log(&paths.install, &format!("installed {version}")),
        Outcome::AlreadyInstalled { .. } => {}
        Outcome::NewerInstalled { zip, installed } => system.say(&format!(
            "This copy of Harness is version {zip}, older than the Harness {installed} already on this PC. The installed Harness opens instead."
        )),
    }
    match system.start_app(&paths.launcher(), &paths.install, &[]) {
        Ok(_) => EXIT_OK,
        Err(err) => {
            system.say(&format!("Harness is installed, but did not start: {err}. Open it from the Start Menu."));
            EXIT_FAILED
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::desktop::system::Fake;

    /// An extracted zip of [version] under `<dir>\zip`, and an install folder `<dir>\Harness` (not created).
    struct World {
        _dir: tempfile::TempDir,
        paths: Paths,
    }

    fn world(version: &str) -> World {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        // Review Focus 1: the profile holds a space, an apostrophe, `&`, `%`, `!` and letters outside ASCII.
        let base = dir.path().join("Nguyễn Văn A' & 100% !x");
        let own = base.join("zip");
        zip(&own, version);
        let paths = Paths {
            own,
            install: base.join("Programs").join("Harness"),
            programs: base.join("Start Menu").join("Programs"),
            registry: r"Software\HarnessTest".to_owned(),
            profile: base.clone(),
        };
        World { _dir: dir, paths }
    }

    fn zip(own: &Path, version: &str) {
        let app = own.join(APP_DIR).join(version);
        fs::create_dir_all(app.join("data")).unwrap();
        fs::write(app.join(APP_EXE), version).unwrap();
        fs::write(app.join("data").join("app.so"), b"so").unwrap();
        fs::write(app.join(STARTED_MARKER), b"").unwrap();
        fs::write(own.join(LAUNCHER_EXE), format!("launcher {version}")).unwrap();
        fs::write(own.join(ICON), b"ico").unwrap();
        pointer::write(&own.join(CURRENT), version).unwrap();
    }

    fn text(path: &Path) -> String {
        fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn installs_the_zip_and_registers_the_installed_copy() {
        let World { _dir, paths } = world("1.2.3");
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        assert_eq!(run(&paths, Some(9), &mut system).unwrap(), Outcome::Installed { version: "1.2.3".into() });
        let app = paths.install.join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3");
        assert_eq!(text(&app.join(APP_EXE)), "1.2.3");
        assert_eq!(text(&app.join("data").join("app.so")), "so");
        assert!(!app.join(STARTED_MARKER).exists(), "the zip copy's marker is not the install's");
        assert!(!paths.install.join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3.staging").exists());
        assert_eq!(text(&paths.launcher()), "launcher 1.2.3");
        assert_eq!(pointer::read(&paths.install.join(CURRENT)).unwrap(), "1.2.3");
        assert!(!paths.install.join(PREVIOUS).exists());
        assert_eq!(system.waited, vec![9]);
        assert_eq!(system.quit, vec![paths.install.clone()]);
        let icon = paths.install.join(ICON);
        assert_eq!(system.shortcuts, vec![(paths.shortcut(), paths.launcher(), icon.clone(), paths.install.clone())]);
        let value = |key: &str, name: &str| system.values.get(&(paths.registry.clone(), key.to_owned(), name.to_owned())).cloned();
        assert_eq!(value(r"Classes\harness\shell\open\command", ""), Some(registry::open_command(&paths.launcher())));
        let mut uninstall = std::ffi::OsString::from("\"");
        uninstall.push(paths.launcher());
        uninstall.push("\" --uninstall");
        assert_eq!(value(registry::UNINSTALL_KEY, "UninstallString"), Some(uninstall));
        assert_eq!(value(registry::UNINSTALL_KEY, "InstallLocation"), Some(paths.install.clone().into_os_string()));
        assert_eq!(value(registry::UNINSTALL_KEY, "DisplayVersion"), Some("1.2.3".into()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_newer_zip_keeps_the_installed_version_as_previous() {
        let World { _dir, paths } = world("1.2.3");
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        run(&paths, None, &mut system).unwrap();
        zip(&paths.own, "1.3.0");
        fs::remove_dir_all(paths.own.join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(run(&paths, None, &mut system).unwrap(), Outcome::Installed { version: "1.3.0".into() });
        assert_eq!(pointer::read(&paths.install.join(CURRENT)).unwrap(), "1.3.0");
        assert_eq!(pointer::read(&paths.install.join(PREVIOUS)).unwrap(), "1.2.3");
        assert_eq!(text(&paths.launcher()), "launcher 1.3.0");
        assert!(!paths.install.join("Harness.exe.old").exists() && !paths.install.join("Harness.exe.new").exists());
        assert_eq!(system.values.get(&(paths.registry.clone(), registry::UNINSTALL_KEY.to_owned(), "DisplayVersion".to_owned())), Some(&"1.3.0".into()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_same_version_installed_is_only_registered_again() {
        let World { _dir, paths } = world("1.2.3");
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        run(&paths, None, &mut system).unwrap();
        fs::write(paths.install.join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3").join("mine"), b"").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(run(&paths, None, &mut system).unwrap(), Outcome::AlreadyInstalled { version: "1.2.3".into() });
        assert!(paths.install.join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3").join("mine").exists(), "nothing was copied over it");
        assert_eq!(system.shortcuts.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(system.quit.len(), 1, "an app running the same version is left alone");
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_older_zip_says_so_and_leaves_the_install_alone() {
        let World { _dir, paths } = world("2.0.0");
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        run(&paths, None, &mut system).unwrap();
        zip(&paths.own, "1.9.9");
        assert_eq!(
            run(&paths, None, &mut system).unwrap(),
            Outcome::NewerInstalled { zip: "1.9.9".into(), installed: "2.0.0".into() }
        );
        assert_eq!(pointer::read(&paths.install.join(CURRENT)).unwrap(), "2.0.0");
        assert!(!paths.install.join(APP_DIR).join("1.9.9").exists());
        assert_eq!(main(&paths, None, &mut system), EXIT_OK);
        assert!(system.said.last().unwrap().contains("version 1.9.9, older than the Harness 2.0.0"), "{:?}", system.said);
        assert_eq!(system.started.last().unwrap().0, paths.launcher());
    }

    #[test]
    fn main_starts_the_installed_launcher_and_says_a_failure() {
        let World { _dir, paths } = world("1.2.3");
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        assert_eq!(main(&paths, None, &mut system), EXIT_OK);
        assert_eq!(system.started, vec![(paths.launcher(), paths.install.clone(), vec![])]);
        let mut broken = Fake { fail_shortcut: true, ..Fake::default() };
        assert_eq!(main(&paths, None, &mut broken), EXIT_FAILED);
        assert!(broken.said[0].starts_with("Harness could not install itself: could not create the Start Menu shortcut"));
        assert!(text(&paths.install.join(launch::LOG)).contains("install failed"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_zip_without_its_app_is_refused_before_anything_changes() {
        let World { _dir, paths } = world("1.2.3");
        fs::remove_file(paths.own.join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3").join(APP_EXE)).unwrap();
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        assert!(run(&paths, None, &mut system).unwrap_err().contains("has no"));
        assert!(!paths.install.exists());
        assert!(system.quit.is_empty() && system.shortcuts.is_empty());
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn a_link_in_the_zip_folder_is_never_followed() {
        let World { _dir, paths } = world("1.2.3");
        let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        fs::write(outside.path().join("secret"), b"x").unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(outside.path(), paths.own.join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3").join("elsewhere")).unwrap();
        run(&paths, None, &mut Fake::default()).unwrap();
        assert!(!paths.install.join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3").join("elsewhere").exists());
    }

    #[test]
    fn versions_compare_by_their_numbers() {
        assert!(newer("1.10.0", "1.9.9"));
        assert!(newer("2.0.0", "1.99.99-dev.1"));
        assert!(!newer("1.2.3", "1.2.3"));
        assert!(!newer("1.2.3-dev.2", "1.2.3-dev.1"));
        assert!(!newer("x", "1.0.0"));
    }
}
