  Replace `pty/src/desktop/mod.rs` with this version (C4.1's, plus `Paths`, the known folders, the `Install` arm and
  the heal on launch):

````rust
//! `Harness.exe`, the Harness desktop app's launcher on Windows (desktop spec section 3). It is the one program the
//! Start Menu shortcut, the `harness://` key and the uninstall entry name, so an update, which swaps the app's
//! version folder, never breaks any of them:
//!
//! ```text
//! %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Harness\
//!   Harness.exe   Harness.ico   current   previous   app\<ver>\   launch.log   launch-state.json
//! ```
//!
//! - no arguments, or a `harness://` link: start `app\<current>\harness-desktop.exe` with the same arguments, then
//!   exit (`launch`). `--wait-pid <pid>` first waits for that process to end: the updater and the self-install pass
//!   the app they are replacing, which still holds the single-instance mutex.
//! - `--install [--wait-pid <pid>]`, run from an extracted zip: install that zip's version (`install`).
//! - `--uninstall`, from Settings ▸ Apps (`uninstall`).
//! - `--version`.
//!
//! It is a GUI-subsystem program, so nothing it does opens a console window, and it says what went wrong in a message
//! box and in `launch.log`. It builds and runs on Unix too, where the launch path starts the app with `Command` and
//! the Windows-only steps (registry, Start Menu, windows) are absent, so `cargo test` covers the rest everywhere.

use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

pub mod install;
pub mod launch;
pub mod pointer;
pub mod registry;
pub mod shortcut;
pub mod system;
#[cfg(windows)]
pub mod win;

/// The Flutter app in each version folder (`BINARY_NAME`, desktop/windows/CMakeLists.txt).
pub const APP_EXE: &str = "harness-desktop.exe";
/// This program, as the zip and the install name it.
pub const LAUNCHER_EXE: &str = "Harness.exe";
/// The icon the shortcut and the uninstall entry show, beside the launcher (the launcher has no icon resource).
pub const ICON: &str = "Harness.ico";
/// The version folders.
pub const APP_DIR: &str = "app";
/// What the app writes in its version folder once its first frame is drawn (desktop/lib/update/started_marker.dart).
pub const STARTED_MARKER: &str = ".started";
pub const AUMID: &str = "Autonomous.Harness";
pub const DISPLAY_NAME: &str = "Harness";
pub const PUBLISHER: &str = "Autonomous";

pub const INSTALL_ROOT_ENV: &str = "HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT";
pub const PROGRAMS_DIR_ENV: &str = "HARNESS_DESKTOP_PROGRAMS_DIR";
pub const REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV: &str = "HARNESS_DESKTOP_REGISTRY_ROOT";

pub const EXIT_OK: i32 = 0;
pub const EXIT_FAILED: i32 = 1;
pub const EXIT_USAGE: i32 = 2;
pub const EXIT_BROKEN: i32 = 3;
pub const EXIT_SPAWN: i32 = 4;

pub const USAGE: &str = "usage: Harness.exe [--wait-pid <pid>] [<harness:// link>...] | --install [--wait-pid <pid>] | --uninstall | --version";

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Command {
    Launch { wait_pid: Option<u32>, args: Vec<OsString> },
    Install { wait_pid: Option<u32> },
    Uninstall,
    Version,
}

fn pid_after(args: &[OsString], at: usize) -> Result<u32, String> {
    args.get(at)
        .and_then(|value| value.to_str())
        .and_then(|value| value.parse::<u32>().ok())
        .filter(|&pid| pid > 0)
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("--wait-pid needs a process id\n{USAGE}"))
}

/// Only the first word can be one of this program's own options. A `harness://` link is whatever the shell passes
/// as `%1` and always begins with the scheme, so no link reads as `--uninstall`.
pub fn parse(args: &[OsString]) -> Result<Command, String> {
    match args.first().and_then(|first| first.to_str()) {
        Some("--version") if args.len() == 1 => Ok(Command::Version),
        Some("--uninstall") if args.len() == 1 => Ok(Command::Uninstall),
        Some("--install") => match args.len() {
            1 => Ok(Command::Install { wait_pid: None }),
            3 if args[1] == "--wait-pid" => Ok(Command::Install { wait_pid: Some(pid_after(args, 2)?) }),
            _ => Err(format!("unexpected arguments after --install\n{USAGE}")),
        },
        Some("--version" | "--uninstall") => Err(format!("unexpected arguments after {:?}\n{USAGE}", args[0])),
        Some("--wait-pid") => Ok(Command::Launch { wait_pid: Some(pid_after(args, 1)?), args: args[2..].to_vec() }),
        _ => Ok(Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: args.to_vec() }),
    }
}

/// The folder this program runs from: the root it launches from, unless [INSTALL_ROOT_ENV] names another (tests).
pub fn launch_root(own_exe: &Path, env: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<OsString>) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    if let Some(root) = env(INSTALL_ROOT_ENV).filter(|root| !root.is_empty()) {
        return Some(PathBuf::from(root));
    }
    own_exe.parent().filter(|dir| !dir.as_os_str().is_empty()).map(Path::to_path_buf)
}

/// The folders and the registry root an install and an uninstall use. Each comes from a known folder, never from a
/// hard-coded path or `%LOCALAPPDATA%` text, so a redirected Start Menu or profile is followed (Review Focus 5), and
/// each has an override for the tests (they never write the real Start Menu, `harness://` key or uninstall entry).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Paths {
    /// The folder this Harness.exe runs from: an extracted zip, or the install.
    pub own: PathBuf,
    /// `<FOLDERID_UserProgramFiles>\Harness` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Harness`), or [INSTALL_ROOT_ENV].
    pub install: PathBuf,
    /// `FOLDERID_Programs`, the Start Menu's Programs folder, or [PROGRAMS_DIR_ENV].
    pub programs: PathBuf,
    /// The HKCU subkey that stands for `Software`, or [REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV].
    pub registry: String,
    /// The profile the app keeps `.harness\desktop-app*` in: `USERPROFILE`, as the app's `homeDir()` reads it, then
    /// `FOLDERID_Profile` (`HOME` off Windows).
    pub profile: PathBuf,
}

/// The known folders [Paths] asks for.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum KnownFolder {
    UserProgramFiles,
    Programs,
    Profile,
}

/// A registry override is a relative HKCU path: no leading, trailing or doubled backslash, and no `/`.
pub fn valid_registry_root(value: &str) -> bool {
    !value.is_empty() && !value.contains('/') && value.split('\\').all(|part| !part.is_empty() && part != "..")
}

impl Paths {
    pub fn resolve(
        own_exe: &Path,
        env: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<OsString>,
        known: impl Fn(KnownFolder) -> Option<PathBuf>,
    ) -> Result<Paths, String> {
        let set = |key: &str| env(key).filter(|value| !value.is_empty());
        // A test's install root never comes with the real Start Menu or registry.
        if set(INSTALL_ROOT_ENV).is_some() && (set(PROGRAMS_DIR_ENV).is_none() || set(REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV).is_none()) {
            return Err(format!("{INSTALL_ROOT_ENV} needs {PROGRAMS_DIR_ENV} and {REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV} as well"));
        }
        let own = own_exe.parent().map(Path::to_path_buf).ok_or("Harness.exe does not know its own folder")?;
        let install = match set(INSTALL_ROOT_ENV) {
            Some(root) => PathBuf::from(root),
            None => known(KnownFolder::UserProgramFiles).ok_or("Windows did not say where your programs go")?.join(DISPLAY_NAME),
        };
        let programs = match set(PROGRAMS_DIR_ENV) {
            Some(dir) => PathBuf::from(dir),
            None => known(KnownFolder::Programs).ok_or("Windows did not say where the Start Menu is")?,
        };
        let registry = match set(REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV) {
            Some(root) => {
                let root = root.into_string().map_err(|_| format!("{REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV} is not text"))?;
                if !valid_registry_root(&root) {
                    return Err(format!("{REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV} {root:?} is not a registry path under HKEY_CURRENT_USER"));
                }
                root
            }
            None => "Software".to_owned(),
        };
        let profile = set("USERPROFILE")
            .map(PathBuf::from)
            .or_else(|| known(KnownFolder::Profile))
            .or_else(|| set("HOME").filter(|_| !cfg!(windows)).map(PathBuf::from))
            .ok_or("Windows did not say where your profile is")?;
        for (name, path) in [("the install folder", &install), ("the Start Menu folder", &programs), ("the profile", &profile)] {
            if !path.is_absolute() {
                return Err(format!("{name} {} is not a full path", path.display()));
            }
        }
        Ok(Paths { own, install, programs, registry, profile })
    }

    /// This computer's, for the running program.
    pub fn current() -> Result<Paths, String> {
        let exe = std::env::current_exe().map_err(|err| format!("Harness.exe does not know its own path: {err}"))?;
        #[cfg(windows)]
        let known = win::known_folder;
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        let known = |_: KnownFolder| None;
        Paths::resolve(&exe, |key| std::env::var_os(key), known)
    }

    pub fn launcher(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.install.join(LAUNCHER_EXE)
    }

    pub fn shortcut(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.programs.join(shortcut::LINK_NAME)
    }

    /// Whether this Harness.exe is the installed one.
    pub fn running_installed(&self) -> bool {
        same_folder(&self.own, &self.install)
    }
}

/// Two folders compared as Windows does: resolved when they exist (8.3 names, links), and without case.
pub fn same_folder(a: &Path, b: &Path) -> bool {
    let plain = |path: &Path| {
        let resolved = std::fs::canonicalize(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| path.to_path_buf());
        let text = resolved.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let text = text.strip_prefix(r"\\?\").map(str::to_owned).unwrap_or(text);
        text.trim_end_matches(['\\', '/']).to_lowercase()
    };
    plain(a) == plain(b)
}

/// The program: see the module comment.
pub fn run(args: Vec<OsString>) -> i32 {
    let command = match parse(&args) {
        Ok(command) => command,
        Err(err) => {
            system::say(&err);
            return EXIT_USAGE;
        }
    };
    match command {
        Command::Version => {
            println!("{}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
            EXIT_OK
        }
        Command::Launch { wait_pid, args } => {
            let Some(root) = std::env::current_exe().ok().and_then(|exe| launch_root(&exe, |key| std::env::var_os(key))) else {
                system::say("Harness.exe does not know its own folder.");
                return EXIT_BROKEN;
            };
            let mut system = system::Real::default();
            // Only the installed launcher keeps the harness:// key right; a zip's copy never takes the links.
            if let Some(paths) = Paths::current().ok().filter(|paths| same_folder(&root, &paths.install)) {
                launch::heal_protocol_key(&root, &paths.registry, &mut system);
            }
            launch::run(&root, wait_pid, &args, &mut system)
        }
        Command::Install { wait_pid } => match Paths::current() {
            Ok(paths) => install::main(&paths, wait_pid, &mut system::Real::default()),
            Err(err) => {
                system::say(&format!("Harness could not install itself: {err}."));
                EXIT_FAILED
            }
        },
        // C4.3.
        Command::Uninstall => {
            system::say("This Harness.exe does not uninstall yet.");
            EXIT_USAGE
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn os(args: &[&str]) -> Vec<OsString> {
        args.iter().map(OsString::from).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_each_form_and_passes_a_link_through() {
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&[])).unwrap(), Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: vec![] });
        assert_eq!(
            parse(&os(&["harness://notification/m/a"])).unwrap(),
            Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: os(&["harness://notification/m/a"]) }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse(&os(&["--wait-pid", "42", "harness://x"])).unwrap(),
            Command::Launch { wait_pid: Some(42), args: os(&["harness://x"]) }
        );
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&["--install"])).unwrap(), Command::Install { wait_pid: None });
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&["--install", "--wait-pid", "7"])).unwrap(), Command::Install { wait_pid: Some(7) });
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&["--uninstall"])).unwrap(), Command::Uninstall);
        assert_eq!(parse(&os(&["--version"])).unwrap(), Command::Version);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_option_counts_only_as_the_first_word() {
        // What a link to `harness:--uninstall` would hand over: one argument, the whole link.
        assert_eq!(
            parse(&os(&["harness:--uninstall"])).unwrap(),
            Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: os(&["harness:--uninstall"]) }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse(&os(&["harness://x", "--uninstall"])).unwrap(),
            Command::Launch { wait_pid: None, args: os(&["harness://x", "--uninstall"]) }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_a_malformed_option() {
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--wait-pid"])).unwrap_err().contains("needs a process id"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--wait-pid", "0"])).unwrap_err().contains("needs a process id"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--wait-pid", "x"])).unwrap_err().contains("needs a process id"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--install", "--wait-pid"])).unwrap_err().contains("unexpected arguments"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--install", "extra"])).unwrap_err().contains("unexpected arguments"));
        assert!(parse(&os(&["--uninstall", "now"])).unwrap_err().contains("unexpected arguments"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_launch_root_is_the_programs_folder_unless_the_tests_name_one() {
        let exe = Path::new("/R/Harness.exe");
        assert_eq!(launch_root(exe, |_| None), Some(PathBuf::from("/R")));
        let env = |key: &str| (key == INSTALL_ROOT_ENV).then(|| OsString::from("/T"));
        assert_eq!(launch_root(exe, env), Some(PathBuf::from("/T")));
        assert_eq!(launch_root(Path::new("Harness.exe"), |_| None), None);
    }

    /// A full path on this OS: `C:\<path>` on Windows, `/<path>` elsewhere.
    fn at(path: &str) -> PathBuf {
        Path::new(if cfg!(windows) { "C:\\" } else { "/" }).join(path)
    }

    fn known(folder: KnownFolder) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        Some(at(match folder {
            KnownFolder::UserProgramFiles => "K/Programs",
            KnownFolder::Programs => "K/Start Menu/Programs",
            KnownFolder::Profile => "K/Profile",
        }))
    }

    #[test]
    fn paths_come_from_the_known_folders() {
        let paths = Paths::resolve(&at("zip/Harness.exe"), |_| None, known).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            paths,
            Paths {
                own: at("zip"),
                install: at("K/Programs").join("Harness"),
                programs: at("K/Start Menu/Programs"),
                registry: "Software".to_owned(),
                profile: at("K/Profile"),
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(paths.launcher(), at("K/Programs").join("Harness").join("Harness.exe"));
        assert_eq!(paths.shortcut(), at("K/Start Menu/Programs").join("Harness.lnk"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_tests_overrides_win_and_userprofile_comes_before_the_known_profile() {
        let env = |key: &str| {
            Some(at(match key {
                INSTALL_ROOT_ENV => "T/Harness",
                PROGRAMS_DIR_ENV => "T/Programs",
                "USERPROFILE" => "T/Nguyễn Văn A'",
                REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV => return Some(OsString::from(r"Software\HarnessTest\1")),
                _ => return None,
            }).into_os_string())
        };
        let paths = Paths::resolve(&at("zip/Harness.exe"), env, known).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(paths.install, at("T/Harness"));
        assert_eq!(paths.programs, at("T/Programs"));
        assert_eq!(paths.registry, r"Software\HarnessTest\1");
        assert_eq!(paths.profile, at("T/Nguyễn Văn A'"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_a_registry_override_that_is_not_a_relative_key_and_a_relative_folder() {
        for bad in ["", r"\Software", r"Software\", r"Software\\X", "Software/X", r"Software\..\X"] {
            assert!(!valid_registry_root(bad), "{bad:?}");
        }
        let env = |key: &str| (key == REGISTRY_ROOT_ENV).then(|| OsString::from(r"\Software"));
        assert!(Paths::resolve(&at("zip/Harness.exe"), env, known).unwrap_err().contains("not a registry path"));
        let env = |key: &str| (key == PROGRAMS_DIR_ENV).then(|| OsString::from("relative"));
        assert!(Paths::resolve(&at("zip/Harness.exe"), env, known).unwrap_err().contains("not a full path"));
        // The tests' install root alone would reach the real Start Menu and registry.
        let env = |key: &str| (key == INSTALL_ROOT_ENV).then(|| at("T/Harness").into_os_string());
        assert!(Paths::resolve(&at("zip/Harness.exe"), env, known).unwrap_err().contains("needs"));
        assert!(Paths::resolve(&at("zip/Harness.exe"), |_| None, |_| None).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn folders_compare_without_case_and_trailing_separators() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join("Harness");
        std::fs::create_dir(&path).unwrap();
        let mut trailing = path.clone().into_os_string();
        trailing.push(std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR_STR);
        assert!(same_folder(&path, Path::new(&trailing)));
        assert!(same_folder(Path::new("/X/Harness"), Path::new("/x/harness/")));
        assert!(!same_folder(Path::new("/X/Harness"), Path::new("/X/Harness2")));
    }
}

//! What the launcher asks of Windows, behind one trait: the launch, install and uninstall steps are plain Rust over
//! files, and these are the calls around them. [Real] makes them (win.rs on Windows; on Unix the few that exist
//! there), and the unit tests use [Fake], so every step runs in `cargo test` on any OS.

use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::io;
use std::path::Path;
use std::time::Duration;

use super::registry::Key;

pub trait System {
    /// Start `exe` from `dir` with `args`: its process id and creation time.
    fn start_app(&mut self, exe: &Path, dir: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> io::Result<(u32, u64)>;
    /// Wait up to `wait` for `pid` to end.
    fn wait_for_exit(&mut self, pid: u32, wait: Duration);
    /// Ask the apps from `root` (`<root>\app\*\harness-desktop.exe`) to quit (`WM_HARNESS_QUIT`), wait up to `wait`,
    /// then end any still there. How many there were.
    fn quit_app(&mut self, root: &Path, wait: Duration) -> usize;
    /// A text value under `HKCU\<registry>\<key>`; `name` "" is the key's default value.
    fn read_value(&mut self, registry: &str, key: &str, name: &str) -> Option<OsString>;
    fn write_keys(&mut self, registry: &str, keys: &[Key]) -> io::Result<()>;
    /// The Start Menu shortcut: `link` to `target`, started in `dir`, showing `icon`, with the AUMID.
    fn create_shortcut(&mut self, link: &Path, target: &Path, icon: &Path, dir: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;
    fn say(&mut self, text: &str);
    fn now_ms(&mut self) -> u64;
}

/// Set by the tests that run the real program: messages go to stderr instead of a message box.
pub const NO_DIALOG_ENV: &str = "HARNESS_DESKTOP_NO_DIALOG";

/// This computer's.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Real;

/// A message for the person: a message box on Windows (there is no console), stderr elsewhere.
pub fn say(text: &str) {
    Real.say(text)
}

#[cfg(unix)]
fn unsupported() -> io::Error {
    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Unsupported, "only on Windows")
}

impl System for Real {
    fn start_app(&mut self, exe: &Path, dir: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> io::Result<(u32, u64)> {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            super::win::start_app(exe, dir, args)
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
            use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
            Command::new(exe)
                .args(args)
                .current_dir(dir)
                .stdin(Stdio::null())
                .stdout(Stdio::null())
                .stderr(Stdio::null())
                .process_group(0)
                .spawn()
                .map(|child| (child.id(), 0))
        }
    }

    fn wait_for_exit(&mut self, pid: u32, wait: Duration) {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            super::win::wait_for_exit(pid, wait)
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + wait;
            while unsafe { libc::kill(pid as i32, 0) } == 0 && std::time::Instant::now() < deadline {
                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
            }
        }
    }

    fn quit_app(&mut self, root: &Path, wait: Duration) -> usize {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            super::win::quit_app(root, wait)
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            let _ = (root, wait);
            0
        }
    }

    fn read_value(&mut self, registry: &str, key: &str, name: &str) -> Option<OsString> {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            super::win::read_value(registry, key, name)
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            let _ = (registry, key, name);
            None
        }
    }

    fn write_keys(&mut self, registry: &str, keys: &[Key]) -> io::Result<()> {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            super::win::write_keys(registry, keys)
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            let _ = (registry, keys);
            Err(unsupported())
        }
    }

    fn create_shortcut(&mut self, link: &Path, target: &Path, icon: &Path, dir: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            super::shortcut::create(link, target, icon, dir, super::AUMID)
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            let _ = (link, target, icon, dir);
            Err(unsupported())
        }
    }

    fn say(&mut self, text: &str) {
        // The tests run the real program, where a message box would wait for a click nobody makes.
        if cfg!(unix) || std::env::var_os(NO_DIALOG_ENV).is_some() {
            eprintln!("{text}");
            return;
        }
        #[cfg(windows)]
        super::win::message_box(text);
    }

    fn now_ms(&mut self) -> u64 {
        std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).map(|d| d.as_millis() as u64).unwrap_or(0)
    }
}

/// A recording stand-in for the unit tests.
#[cfg(test)]
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Fake {
    /// (exe, dir, args) of each start.
    pub started: Vec<(std::path::PathBuf, std::path::PathBuf, Vec<OsString>)>,
    pub fail_start: bool,
    pub waited: Vec<u32>,
    /// What quit_app finds running (and ends).
    pub running: Vec<u32>,
    pub quit: Vec<std::path::PathBuf>,
    /// (registry root, key, value name) -> value.
    pub values: std::collections::BTreeMap<(String, String, String), OsString>,
    pub numbers: std::collections::BTreeMap<(String, String, String), u32>,
    pub writes: usize,
    /// (link, target, icon, dir).
    pub shortcuts: Vec<(std::path::PathBuf, std::path::PathBuf, std::path::PathBuf, std::path::PathBuf)>,
    pub fail_shortcut: bool,
    pub said: Vec<String>,
    pub now: u64,
}

#[cfg(test)]
impl System for Fake {
    fn start_app(&mut self, exe: &Path, dir: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> io::Result<(u32, u64)> {
        if self.fail_start {
            return Err(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied));
        }
        self.started.push((exe.to_path_buf(), dir.to_path_buf(), args.to_vec()));
        Ok((99 + self.started.len() as u32, self.started.len() as u64))
    }
    fn wait_for_exit(&mut self, pid: u32, _wait: Duration) {
        self.waited.push(pid);
    }
    fn quit_app(&mut self, root: &Path, _wait: Duration) -> usize {
        self.quit.push(root.to_path_buf());
        std::mem::take(&mut self.running).len()
    }
    fn read_value(&mut self, registry: &str, key: &str, name: &str) -> Option<OsString> {
        self.values.get(&(registry.to_owned(), key.to_owned(), name.to_owned())).cloned()
    }
    fn write_keys(&mut self, registry: &str, keys: &[Key]) -> io::Result<()> {
        use super::registry::Value;
        self.writes += 1;
        for key in keys {
            for (name, value) in &key.values {
                let at = (registry.to_owned(), key.path.clone(), name.clone());
                match value {
                    Value::Text(text) => drop(self.values.insert(at, text.clone())),
                    Value::Number(number) => drop(self.numbers.insert(at, *number)),
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    fn create_shortcut(&mut self, link: &Path, target: &Path, icon: &Path, dir: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        if self.fail_shortcut {
            return Err(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied));
        }
        self.shortcuts.push((link.to_path_buf(), target.to_path_buf(), icon.to_path_buf(), dir.to_path_buf()));
        Ok(())
    }
    fn say(&mut self, text: &str) {
        self.said.push(text.to_owned());
    }
    fn now_ms(&mut self) -> u64 {
        self.now += 1_000;
        1_000_000 + self.now
    }
}

//! The Windows calls behind system.rs's [Real](super::system::Real): known folders, starting the app, finding and
//! quitting it, the registry and the message box.

use std::ffi::{OsStr, OsString, c_void};
use std::io;
use std::os::windows::ffi::{OsStrExt, OsStringExt};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::ptr::{null, null_mut};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{BOOL, CloseHandle, ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, FILETIME, HANDLE, HWND, LPARAM, TRUE, WAIT_OBJECT_0};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Com::CoTaskMemFree;
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Registry::{
    HKEY, HKEY_CURRENT_USER, KEY_SET_VALUE, REG_DWORD, REG_OPTION_NON_VOLATILE, REG_SZ, RRF_RT_REG_SZ, RegCloseKey,
    RegCreateKeyExW, RegDeleteTreeW, RegGetValueW, RegSetValueExW,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
    CreateProcessW, GetProcessTimes, OpenProcess, PROCESS_INFORMATION, PROCESS_NAME_WIN32, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION,
    PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE, PROCESS_TERMINATE, QueryFullProcessImageNameW, STARTUPINFOW, TerminateProcess,
    WaitForSingleObject,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::UI::Shell::{
    FOLDERID_Profile, FOLDERID_Programs, FOLDERID_UserProgramFiles, KF_FLAG_CREATE, SHGetKnownFolderPath,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{
    EnumWindows, GetClassNameW, GetWindowThreadProcessId, MB_ICONINFORMATION, MB_OK, MB_SETFOREGROUND, MessageBoxW,
    PostMessageW, RegisterWindowMessageW,
};

use super::KnownFolder;
use super::registry::{Key, Value};

/// The Flutter runner's window class (desktop/windows/runner/win32_window.cpp, kWindowClassName). Every Flutter app
/// has it, so a window counts only when its process is `<root>\app\*\harness-desktop.exe`; the title is not used.
const WINDOW_CLASS: &str = "FLUTTER_RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW";
/// `WM_HARNESS_QUIT` (desktop/windows/runner/single_instance.h): a registered message, so it means the same in
/// every process and no other program's message collides with it.
pub const QUIT_MESSAGE: &str = "Autonomous.Harness.Quit";

pub fn wide(text: &OsStr) -> Vec<u16> {
    text.encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
}

pub fn known_folder(folder: KnownFolder) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let (id, flags) = match folder {
        // %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs need not exist yet on a new profile.
        KnownFolder::UserProgramFiles => (&FOLDERID_UserProgramFiles, KF_FLAG_CREATE as u32),
        KnownFolder::Programs => (&FOLDERID_Programs, 0),
        KnownFolder::Profile => (&FOLDERID_Profile, 0),
    };
    let mut out = null_mut();
    let hr = unsafe { SHGetKnownFolderPath(id, flags, null_mut(), &mut out) };
    let path = (hr >= 0 && !out.is_null()).then(|| {
        let length = (0..).take_while(|&i| unsafe { *out.add(i) } != 0).count();
        PathBuf::from(OsString::from_wide(unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(out, length) }))
    });
    // Freed whatever the answer: the shell may allocate it on a failure too.
    unsafe { CoTaskMemFree(out as *const c_void) };
    path
}

pub fn message_box(text: &str) {
    let text = wide(OsStr::new(text));
    let caption = wide(OsStr::new(super::DISPLAY_NAME));
    unsafe { MessageBoxW(null_mut(), text.as_ptr(), caption.as_ptr(), MB_OK | MB_ICONINFORMATION | MB_SETFOREGROUND) };
}

/// `"<exe>" <args>`, each argument quoted as the C runtime splits it back (launcher::quote_arg).
pub fn command_line(exe: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> Vec<u16> {
    let mut line = vec![b'"' as u16];
    line.extend(exe.as_os_str().encode_wide());
    line.push(b'"' as u16);
    for arg in args {
        line.push(b' ' as u16);
        crate::launcher::quote_arg(&arg.encode_wide().collect::<Vec<u16>>(), &mut line);
    }
    line
}

fn filetime(time: FILETIME) -> u64 {
    (u64::from(time.dwHighDateTime) << 32) | u64::from(time.dwLowDateTime)
}

/// A process's creation time, which tells it apart from a later process given the same pid.
fn created(process: HANDLE) -> u64 {
    let zero = FILETIME { dwLowDateTime: 0, dwHighDateTime: 0 };
    let (mut creation, mut exit, mut kernel, mut user) = (zero, zero, zero, zero);
    if unsafe { GetProcessTimes(process, &mut creation, &mut exit, &mut kernel, &mut user) } == 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    filetime(creation)
}

/// Start [exe] with no inherited handle, outside this launcher's job when the job allows it (launcher::start): a
/// pane's job would end the app with the pane. Its pid and creation time.
pub fn start_app(exe: &Path, dir: &Path, args: &[OsString]) -> io::Result<(u32, u64)> {
    let application = wide(exe.as_os_str());
    let directory = wide(dir.as_os_str());
    let spawn = |flags: u32| -> io::Result<(u32, u64)> {
        let mut line = command_line(exe, args);
        line.push(0);
        let mut startup: STARTUPINFOW = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        startup.cb = std::mem::size_of::<STARTUPINFOW>() as u32;
        let mut info: PROCESS_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        let ok = unsafe {
            CreateProcessW(application.as_ptr(), line.as_mut_ptr(), null(), null(), 0, flags, null(), directory.as_ptr(), &startup, &mut info)
        };
        if ok == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        let made = (info.dwProcessId, created(info.hProcess));
        unsafe {
            CloseHandle(info.hThread);
            CloseHandle(info.hProcess);
        }
        Ok(made)
    };
    let mut made = None;
    let started = crate::launcher::start(
        |flags| {
            spawn(flags).map(|pid_created| {
                made = Some(pid_created);
                pid_created.0
            })
        },
        |warning| super::launch::log(dir.parent().and_then(Path::parent).unwrap_or(dir), &warning),
    );
    started.map(|_| made.unwrap_or((0, 0)))
}

pub fn wait_for_exit(pid: u32, wait: Duration) {
    let process = unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE, 0, pid) };
    if process.is_null() {
        return;
    }
    unsafe {
        WaitForSingleObject(process, wait.as_millis().min(u128::from(u32::MAX - 1)) as u32);
        CloseHandle(process);
    }
}

fn image_of(pid: u32) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let process = unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, 0, pid) };
    if process.is_null() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut buffer = vec![0u16; 32_768];
    let mut size = buffer.len() as u32;
    let ok = unsafe { QueryFullProcessImageNameW(process, PROCESS_NAME_WIN32, buffer.as_mut_ptr(), &mut size) };
    unsafe { CloseHandle(process) };
    (ok != 0).then(|| PathBuf::from(OsString::from_wide(&buffer[..size as usize])))
}

/// Whether [image] is `<root>\app\<one folder>\harness-desktop.exe`.
fn from_install(image: &Path, root: &Path) -> bool {
    let Some(folder) = image.parent() else { return false };
    let named = image.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name.to_string_lossy().eq_ignore_ascii_case(super::APP_EXE));
    named && folder.parent().is_some_and(|app| super::same_folder(app, &root.join(super::APP_DIR)))
}

/// Each top-level window of [WINDOW_CLASS], hidden ones too (a window hidden to the tray is still there), with its
/// process id.
fn flutter_windows() -> Vec<(HWND, u32)> {
    unsafe extern "system" fn each(window: HWND, found: LPARAM) -> BOOL {
        let found = unsafe { &mut *(found as *mut Vec<(HWND, u32)>) };
        let mut class = [0u16; 64];
        let length = unsafe { GetClassNameW(window, class.as_mut_ptr(), class.len() as i32) };
        if length > 0 && String::from_utf16_lossy(&class[..length as usize]) == WINDOW_CLASS {
            let mut pid = 0u32;
            unsafe { GetWindowThreadProcessId(window, &mut pid) };
            found.push((window, pid));
        }
        TRUE
    }
    let mut found: Vec<(HWND, u32)> = Vec::new();
    unsafe { EnumWindows(Some(each), &mut found as *mut Vec<(HWND, u32)> as LPARAM) };
    found
}

fn app_windows(root: &Path) -> Vec<(HWND, u32)> {
    flutter_windows().into_iter().filter(|(_, pid)| image_of(*pid).is_some_and(|image| from_install(&image, root))).collect()
}

/// The processes of an app from [root] that have a window, each once.
pub fn app_processes(root: &Path) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut pids: Vec<u32> = app_windows(root).into_iter().map(|(_, pid)| pid).collect();
    pids.sort_unstable();
    pids.dedup();
    pids
}

/// Post `WM_HARNESS_QUIT` to each app window from [root], wait up to [wait] for their processes, then end the ones
/// still there (an install or uninstall must not leave the app holding its folder). How many processes there were.
pub fn quit_app(root: &Path, wait: Duration) -> usize {
    let windows = app_windows(root);
    if windows.is_empty() {
        return 0;
    }
    let message = unsafe { RegisterWindowMessageW(wide(OsStr::new(QUIT_MESSAGE)).as_ptr()) };
    for (window, _) in &windows {
        unsafe { PostMessageW(*window, message, 0, 0) };
    }
    let mut pids: Vec<u32> = windows.iter().map(|(_, pid)| *pid).collect();
    pids.sort_unstable();
    pids.dedup();
    let deadline = Instant::now() + wait;
    for &pid in &pids {
        let process = unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE | PROCESS_TERMINATE, 0, pid) };
        if process.is_null() {
            continue;
        }
        let left = deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now()).as_millis() as u32;
        if unsafe { WaitForSingleObject(process, left) } != WAIT_OBJECT_0 {
            super::launch::log(root, &format!("Harness (process {pid}) did not quit when asked; ending it"));
            unsafe { TerminateProcess(process, 1) };
            unsafe { WaitForSingleObject(process, 5_000) };
        }
        unsafe { CloseHandle(process) };
    }
    pids.len()
}

fn key_path(registry: &str, key: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
    wide(OsStr::new(&format!("{registry}\\{key}")))
}

fn win32(code: u32) -> io::Result<()> {
    if code == 0 { Ok(()) } else { Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(code as i32)) }
}

pub fn read_value(registry: &str, key: &str, name: &str) -> Option<OsString> {
    let path = key_path(registry, key);
    let name = wide(OsStr::new(name));
    let mut size = 0u32;
    let probe = unsafe { RegGetValueW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, path.as_ptr(), name.as_ptr(), RRF_RT_REG_SZ, null_mut(), null_mut(), &mut size) };
    if probe != 0 || size == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut buffer = vec![0u16; (size as usize).div_ceil(2)];
    let read = unsafe {
        RegGetValueW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, path.as_ptr(), name.as_ptr(), RRF_RT_REG_SZ, null_mut(), buffer.as_mut_ptr().cast(), &mut size)
    };
    if read != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let length = buffer.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(buffer.len());
    Some(OsString::from_wide(&buffer[..length]))
}

pub fn write_keys(registry: &str, keys: &[Key]) -> io::Result<()> {
    for key in keys {
        let path = key_path(registry, &key.path);
        let mut handle: HKEY = null_mut();
        win32(unsafe {
            RegCreateKeyExW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, path.as_ptr(), 0, null(), REG_OPTION_NON_VOLATILE, KEY_SET_VALUE, null(), &mut handle, null_mut())
        })?;
        let written = key.values.iter().try_for_each(|(name, value)| {
            let name = wide(OsStr::new(name));
            match value {
                Value::Text(text) => {
                    let data = wide(text);
                    win32(unsafe { RegSetValueExW(handle, name.as_ptr(), 0, REG_SZ, data.as_ptr().cast(), (data.len() * 2) as u32) })
                }
                Value::Number(number) => {
                    let data = number.to_le_bytes();
                    win32(unsafe { RegSetValueExW(handle, name.as_ptr(), 0, REG_DWORD, data.as_ptr(), 4) })
                }
            }
        });
        unsafe { RegCloseKey(handle) };
        written?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `HKCU\<registry>\<key>` and everything under it; a missing key is already removed.
pub fn delete_key(registry: &str, key: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    match unsafe { RegDeleteTreeW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, key_path(registry, key).as_ptr()) } {
        0 | ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND => Ok(()),
        code => win32(code),
    }
}

/// The `harness://` key names this launcher; rewritten when it names anything else. One registry read when it does.
pub fn heal_protocol_key(root: &Path, registry_root: &str, system: &mut impl System) {
    let launcher = root.join(LAUNCHER_EXE);
    let want = registry::open_command(&launcher);
    let key = registry::protocol_command_key(registry::SCHEME);
    if system.read_value(registry_root, &key, "").as_deref() == Some(want.as_os_str()) {
        return;
    }
    match system.write_keys(registry_root, &registry::protocol_keys(registry::SCHEME, &launcher)) {
        Ok(()) => log(root, &format!("harness:// links now open {}", launcher.display())),
        Err(err) => log(root, &format!("could not point harness:// links at {}: {err}", launcher.display())),
    }
}

**Files:**
- Modify: `pty/Cargo.toml`: two `windows-sys` features for the test's window.
- Modify: `pty/src/desktop/mod.rs`: `pub mod uninstall;` and the `Uninstall` arm.

- Modify: `pty/src/desktop/win.rs`: `start_script`.
- Modify: `pty/tests/desktop_common/mod.rs`: a stand-in with a window.
- Modify: `pty/tests/desktop_install.rs`: the uninstall test.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: C4.2's `Paths`, `registry::{protocol_key, UNINSTALL_KEY}`, `System::quit_app`; C3.1's
  `WM_HARNESS_QUIT` (`kHarnessQuitMessageName` in `single_instance.h`), under the contract below.
- Produces: `desktop::uninstall::{run(&Paths, &ScriptPlace, &mut impl System) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>, main(&Paths, &mut impl System) -> i32, check_install, remove_app_state, final_removal_script, schedule_final_removal, ScriptPlace, FINAL_MESSAGE, QUIT_WAIT, DESKTOP_STATE_PREFIX}`.
  It takes the script place and the `System` it acts through.

**The quit contract (`WM_HARNESS_QUIT`), shared with C3.1 word for word.**
- `WM_HARNESS_QUIT` is the registered window message `RegisterWindowMessageW(L"Autonomous.Harness.Quit")`. It is not a
  `WM_APP` value, so it means the same in every process and no other program's private message can be read as it.
- The app quits on it as the tray's Quit does (`FlutterWindow::RequestQuit`), hidden to the tray or not. It answers it
  on two windows: its main window, of the Flutter runner's class `FLUTTER_RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW`, and its single-instance
  window (class `HarnessSingleInstance`, message-only, titled with the instance name).
- `Harness.exe` (`--uninstall`, and `--install` over a running different version) posts it to the main window of each
  process whose image is `<install>\app\<one folder>\harness-desktop.exe` (`pty/src/desktop/win.rs`, `QUIT_MESSAGE`,
  `quit_app`), waits up to 10 s, and ends a process that is still there. It never uses the instance name or `--quit`.
- `harness-desktop.exe --quit` posts it to this user's single-instance window and waits up to 10 s. C3.7's race test
  uses it.
- The window: `FindWindow` by title is not used. Every top-level window of class `FLUTTER_RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW`
  (`win32_window.cpp`'s `kWindowClassName`, hidden windows included) counts when its process's image is
  `<install>\app\<one folder>\harness-desktop.exe`; the class alone is any Flutter app's, and the title may change.
- `windows-sys` features this task adds, exactly: `Win32_Graphics_Gdi` (gates `RegisterClassW`/`WNDCLASSW`) and
  `Win32_System_LibraryLoader` (`GetModuleHandleW`), both for the test's stand-in window only.

````rust
/// A window of the Flutter runner's class that ends its process on `WM_HARNESS_QUIT`, as the app does.
#[cfg(windows)]
mod window {
    use std::ffi::OsStr;
    use std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{HWND, LPARAM, LRESULT, WPARAM};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::GetModuleHandleW;
    use windows_sys::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{
        CreateWindowExW, DefWindowProcW, DispatchMessageW, GetMessageW, MSG, PostQuitMessage, RegisterClassW,
        RegisterWindowMessageW, WNDCLASSW,
    };

    static QUIT: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

    fn wide(text: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        OsStr::new(text).encode_wide().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
    }

    unsafe extern "system" fn procedure(window: HWND, message: u32, wparam: WPARAM, lparam: LPARAM) -> LRESULT {
        if message == QUIT.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            unsafe { PostQuitMessage(0) };
            return 0;
        }
        unsafe { DefWindowProcW(window, message, wparam, lparam) }
    }

    pub fn run() {
        unsafe {
            QUIT.store(RegisterWindowMessageW(wide(harness_pty::desktop::win::QUIT_MESSAGE).as_ptr()), Ordering::Relaxed);
            let instance = GetModuleHandleW(std::ptr::null());
            let class = wide("FLUTTER_RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW");
            let mut definition: WNDCLASSW = std::mem::zeroed();
            definition.lpfnWndProc = Some(procedure);
            definition.hInstance = instance;
            definition.lpszClassName = class.as_ptr();
            RegisterClassW(&definition);
            let title = wide("Harness");
            // Hidden, as a window hidden to the tray is.
            CreateWindowExW(0, class.as_ptr(), title.as_ptr(), 0, 0, 0, 100, 100, std::ptr::null_mut(), std::ptr::null_mut(), instance, std::ptr::null());
            let mut message: MSG = std::mem::zeroed();
            while GetMessageW(&mut message, std::ptr::null_mut(), 0, 0) > 0 {
                DispatchMessageW(&message);
            }
        }
    }
}

    /// The installed app runs, with a window, when Settings uninstalls it: it is asked to quit, everything of the
    /// app goes, and the CLI's files stay.
    fn uninstall_quits_the_app_and_leaves_the_cli() {
        let world = installed();
        let launcher = world.install.join("Harness.exe");
        let running = world.dir.path().join("running.json");
        let mut app = Command::new(world.install.join("app").join("1.2.3").join("harness-desktop.exe"))
            .env(STANDIN_OUT, &running)
            .env(STANDIN_WINDOW, "1")
            .spawn()
            .unwrap();
        report(&running);
        // The window is up once the stand-in has written; give it a moment to be listed.
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
        let output = run(&world, &launcher, &["--uninstall"], &world.dir.path().join("unused.json"));
        assert!(output.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));
        assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).ends_with("To remove them, run `harness uninstall`.\n"));
        let quit = app.try_wait().unwrap();
        assert!(quit.is_some_and(|status| status.success()), "the app did not quit when asked: {quit:?}");

        assert!(!world.programs.join("Harness.lnk").exists());
        assert_eq!(value(&world, r"Classes\harness\shell\open\command", ""), None);
        assert_eq!(value(&world, registry::UNINSTALL_KEY, "DisplayName"), None);
        assert!(!world.profile.join(".harness").join("desktop-app-v2").exists());
        assert!(world.profile.join(".harness").join("cli").join("state.json").exists(), "the CLI's files stay");
        // The folder goes once the launcher has exited.
        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60);
        while world.install.exists() {
            assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "{} is still there", world.install.display());
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250));
        }
    }

  launcher's pid with `tasklist`, refuses a root that has become a link (`%~a` has an `l`), removes it with `rmdir /s /q`
  (never `del` on a folder), retries a busy folder, and deletes itself. It is started with `CreateProcessW` through
  `launcher::start`, outside the launcher's job when the job allows it, rather than through WMI as B's: the launcher
  is no Node process in libuv's job.

````rust
//! `Harness.exe --uninstall`, which Settings ▸ Apps ▸ Harness ▸ Uninstall runs (desktop spec section 3.5):
//! 1. the running app is asked to quit through its window (`WM_HARNESS_QUIT`), and ended if it has not within
//!    [QUIT_WAIT];
//! 2. the Start Menu shortcut, the `harness://` key and the uninstall entry are removed;
//! 3. the app's own state, `%USERPROFILE%\.harness\desktop-app*`, is removed. The rest of `.harness` is the CLI's
//!    and is never touched;
//! 4. the install folder is removed by a cmd.exe step that waits for this launcher to exit, since a running
//!    program's file cannot be deleted. It is B's "remove after the process has exited" step
//!    (cli/src/lib/uninstall/removal.ts, finalRemovalScript), for one folder;
//! 5. one message says what stays.
//!
//! This deletes folders, and a wrong path deletes a person's files, so the install folder is checked first: a full
//! path, named `Harness`, not a drive's root, not the profile nor a folder above it, and not a link. Nothing is ever
//! followed through a link: a link is removed as a link.

use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::path::{Component, Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::Duration;

use super::system::System;
use super::{DISPLAY_NAME, EXIT_FAILED, EXIT_OK, Paths, registry};

pub const QUIT_WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
/// The app's own entries in `.harness`, as B's uninstall leaves them to this one (removal.ts DESKTOP_STATE).
pub const DESKTOP_STATE_PREFIX: &str = "desktop-app";
pub const FINAL_MESSAGE: &str =
    "Harness's command line and agents stay on this PC. To remove them, run `harness uninstall`.";
/// How long the step waits for the launcher (one try a second), and how often it tries a busy folder.
pub const WAIT_TRIES: u32 = 120;
pub const REMOVE_PASSES: u32 = 10;

/// The install folder, checked before anything is removed.
pub fn check_install(install: &Path, profile: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    let refuse = |why: &str| Err(format!("Harness did not remove {} because {why}", install.display()));
    if !install.is_absolute() {
        return refuse("it is not a full path");
    }
    if install.components().any(|part| matches!(part, Component::ParentDir | Component::CurDir)) {
        return refuse("it goes up a folder with ..");
    }
    if install.parent().is_none() {
        return refuse("it is the root of a drive");
    }
    if !install.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name.to_string_lossy().eq_ignore_ascii_case(DISPLAY_NAME)) {
        return refuse("it is not a folder named Harness");
    }
    if super::same_folder(install, profile) || profile.starts_with(install) {
        return refuse("your profile is in it");
    }
    if fs::symlink_metadata(install).is_ok_and(|meta| meta.is_symlink()) {
        return refuse("it is a link to another folder");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The app's state in [profile]'s `.harness`: each `desktop-app*` entry, a link removed as a link. What could not be
/// removed is returned.
pub fn remove_app_state(profile: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let root = profile.join(".harness");
    // A `.harness` that is itself a link is not followed: what it points to is not this app's to empty.
    if fs::symlink_metadata(&root).map(|meta| meta.is_symlink()).unwrap_or(true) {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(&root) else { return Vec::new() };
    let mut left = Vec::new();
    for entry in entries.flatten() {
        if !entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().starts_with(DESKTOP_STATE_PREFIX) {
            continue;
        }
        let path = entry.path();
        let removed = match entry.file_type() {
            Ok(kind) if kind.is_symlink() => fs::remove_dir(&path).or_else(|_| fs::remove_file(&path)),
            Ok(kind) if kind.is_dir() => fs::remove_dir_all(&path),
            Ok(_) => fs::remove_file(&path),
            Err(err) => Err(err),
        };
        if removed.is_err() {
            left.push(path);
        }
    }
    left
}

/// A path a cmd.exe script can carry between double quotes: a full path with no quote, wildcard, redirection or
/// control character (none of which a Windows path holds anyway).
pub fn script_safe(path: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    let text = path.to_str().ok_or_else(|| format!("{} is not text cmd.exe can read", path.display()))?;
    if text.chars().any(|c| c.is_control() || matches!(c, '"' | '*' | '?' | '<' | '>' | '|')) || text.get(2..).is_some_and(|rest| rest.contains(':')) {
        return Err(format!("{text} holds a character a Windows path cannot have"));
    }
    Ok(text.to_owned())
}

/// Inside double quotes in a batch file: cmd expands `%` even there.
fn quoted(text: &str) -> String {
    format!("\"{}\"", text.replace('%', "%%"))
}

/// As `echo` prints it: `%` doubled and cmd's operators escaped.
fn echoed(text: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    for c in text.chars() {
        match c {
            '%' => out.push_str("%%"),
            '^' | '&' | '|' | '<' | '>' | '(' | ')' => {
                out.push('^');
                out.push(c);
            }
            _ => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The cmd.exe script of step 4: wait for [pid] to exit, then remove [install] (retrying a busy folder a few times),
/// note in [log] what stayed, and delete itself. Every tool by its full path under [system_root], every path between
/// double quotes with `%` doubled, under DisableDelayedExpansion so that a `!` is only a `!`; `chcp 65001` first,
/// so the UTF-8 lines after it read right. Before it removes anything it looks again: an install folder that has
/// become a link since (`%~a` has an `l`) is left, and the log says so.
pub fn final_removal_script(pid: u32, install: &Path, log: &Path, system_root: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    let root = script_safe(install)?;
    let log = script_safe(log)?;
    let tool = |name: &str| script_safe(&system_root.join("System32").join(name)).map(|path| quoted(&path));
    let (chcp, tasklist, find, ping) = (tool("chcp.com")?, tool("tasklist.exe")?, tool("find.exe")?, tool("PING.EXE")?);
    let (q, l) = (quoted(&root), quoted(&log));
    Ok([
        "@echo off".to_owned(),
        "setlocal DisableDelayedExpansion".to_owned(),
        format!("{chcp} 65001 >nul"),
        "set tries=0".to_owned(),
        ":wait".to_owned(),
        format!("{tasklist} /FI \"PID eq {pid}\" /NH 2>nul | {find} \" {pid} \" >nul"),
        "if errorlevel 1 goto remove".to_owned(),
        "set /a tries+=1".to_owned(),
        format!("if %tries% GEQ {WAIT_TRIES} goto remove"),
        format!("{ping} -n 2 127.0.0.1 >nul"),
        "goto wait".to_owned(),
        ":remove".to_owned(),
        "set \"attr=-\"".to_owned(),
        format!("for %%A in ({q}) do set \"attr=-%%~aA\""),
        "if not \"%attr%\"==\"%attr:l=%\" goto refused".to_owned(),
        "set pass=0".to_owned(),
        ":again".to_owned(),
        format!("rmdir /s /q {q} 2>nul"),
        format!("if not exist {q} goto done"),
        "set /a pass+=1".to_owned(),
        format!("if %pass% GEQ {REMOVE_PASSES} goto report"),
        format!("{ping} -n 3 127.0.0.1 >nul"),
        "goto again".to_owned(),
        ":report".to_owned(),
        format!(">{l} echo Harness could not remove {} after it was uninstalled: a program still had it open.", echoed(&root)),
        "goto done".to_owned(),
        ":refused".to_owned(),
        format!(">{l} echo Harness did not remove {} because it has become a link to another folder.", echoed(&root)),
        ":done".to_owned(),
        "(goto) 2>nul & del \"%~f0\"".to_owned(),
        String::new(),
    ]
    .join("\r\n"))
}

/// The temp folder and Windows' folder the step uses.
pub struct ScriptPlace {
    pub temp: PathBuf,
    pub system_root: PathBuf,
}

impl ScriptPlace {
    pub fn current() -> ScriptPlace {
        let system_root = std::env::var_os("SystemRoot").or_else(|| std::env::var_os("windir")).unwrap_or_else(|| OsString::from(r"C:\Windows"));
        ScriptPlace { temp: std::env::temp_dir(), system_root: PathBuf::from(system_root) }
    }
}

/// Writes and starts step 4; on a failure to start it, the script goes again.
pub fn schedule_final_removal(install: &Path, place: &ScriptPlace, system: &mut impl System) -> Result<(), String> {
    let stamp = format!("{}-{}", system.pid(), system.now_ms());
    let script = place.temp.join(format!("harness-desktop-uninstall-{stamp}.cmd"));
    let log = place.temp.join(format!("harness-desktop-uninstall-{stamp}.log"));
    if super::same_folder(&place.temp, install) || place.temp.starts_with(install) {
        return Err(format!("the temp folder {} is inside {}", place.temp.display(), install.display()));
    }
    let text = final_removal_script(system.pid(), install, &log, &place.system_root)?;
    fs::write(&script, text).map_err(|err| format!("could not write {}: {err}", script.display()))?;
    system.start_script(&script).map_err(|err| {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&script);
        format!("Windows did not start the step that removes {}: {err}", install.display())
    })
}

/// Everything but the message: what could not be done, as sentences; empty when all of it was.
pub fn run(paths: &Paths, place: &ScriptPlace, system: &mut impl System) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    check_install(&paths.install, &paths.profile)?;
    let mut problems = Vec::new();
    let windows = system.quit_app(&paths.install, QUIT_WAIT);
    if windows > 0 {
        super::launch::log(&paths.install, &format!("uninstall: asked {windows} running Harness to quit"));
    }
    match fs::remove_file(paths.shortcut()) {
        Err(err) if err.kind() != io::ErrorKind::NotFound => problems.push(format!("the Start Menu shortcut stayed ({err})")),
        _ => {}
    }
    for key in [registry::protocol_key(registry::SCHEME), registry::UNINSTALL_KEY.to_owned()] {
        if let Err(err) = system.delete_key(&paths.registry, &key) {
            problems.push(format!("HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\{}\\{key} stayed ({err})", paths.registry));
        }
    }
    for left in remove_app_state(&paths.profile) {
        problems.push(format!("{} stayed", left.display()));
    }
    if paths.install.exists() {
        if let Err(err) = schedule_final_removal(&paths.install, place, system) {
            problems.push(format!("{err}; delete {} yourself", paths.install.display()));
        }
    }
    Ok(problems)
}

/// The program's `--uninstall`.
pub fn main(paths: &Paths, system: &mut impl System) -> i32 {
    match run(paths, &ScriptPlace::current(), system) {
        Ok(problems) if problems.is_empty() => {
            system.say(&format!("The Harness desktop app has been removed.\n\n{FINAL_MESSAGE}"));
            EXIT_OK
        }
        Ok(problems) => {
            system.say(&format!("The Harness desktop app has been removed, except: {}.\n\n{FINAL_MESSAGE}", problems.join("; ")));
            EXIT_FAILED
        }
        Err(err) => {
            system.say(&format!("{err}. Nothing was removed."));
            EXIT_FAILED
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::desktop::system::Fake;

    struct World {
        _dir: tempfile::TempDir,
        paths: Paths,
        place: ScriptPlace,
    }

    /// An installed Harness under a profile named as Review Focus 1 asks, with the CLI's `.harness` beside the app's.
    fn world() -> World {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let profile = dir.path().join("Nguyễn Văn A' & 100% !x");
        let install = profile.join("Programs").join("Harness");
        fs::create_dir_all(install.join("app").join("1.2.3")).unwrap();
        fs::write(install.join("Harness.exe"), b"").unwrap();
        let programs = profile.join("Start Menu");
        fs::create_dir_all(&programs).unwrap();
        fs::write(programs.join("Harness.lnk"), b"").unwrap();
        for entry in ["desktop-app", "desktop-app-v2", "cli", "runtime"] {
            fs::create_dir_all(profile.join(".harness").join(entry)).unwrap();
            fs::write(profile.join(".harness").join(entry).join("state.json"), b"{}").unwrap();
        }
        fs::write(profile.join(".harness").join("daemon-token"), b"t").unwrap();
        let temp = dir.path().join("temp");
        fs::create_dir_all(&temp).unwrap();
        let place = ScriptPlace { temp, system_root: PathBuf::from(r"C:\Windows") };
        let paths = Paths { own: install.clone(), install, programs, registry: r"Software\HarnessTest".into(), profile };
        World { _dir: dir, paths, place }
    }

    #[test]
    fn removes_the_app_and_leaves_the_cli_alone() {
        let World { _dir, paths, place } = world();
        let mut system = Fake { running: vec![3], ..Fake::default() };
        assert_eq!(run(&paths, &place, &mut system).unwrap(), Vec::<String>::new());
        assert_eq!(system.quit, vec![paths.install.clone()]);
        assert!(!paths.shortcut().exists());
        assert_eq!(
            system.deleted,
            vec![(paths.registry.clone(), r"Classes\harness".to_owned()), (paths.registry.clone(), registry::UNINSTALL_KEY.to_owned())]
        );
        let harness = paths.profile.join(".harness");
        assert!(!harness.join("desktop-app").exists() && !harness.join("desktop-app-v2").exists());
        assert!(harness.join("cli").join("state.json").exists() && harness.join("runtime").exists());
        assert!(harness.join("daemon-token").exists());
        // The folder itself goes once the launcher has exited.
        assert!(paths.install.exists());
        assert_eq!(system.scripts.len(), 1);
        assert!(system.scripts[0].1.contains(&format!("rmdir /s /q \"{}\"", paths.install.display().to_string().replace('%', "%%"))));
    }

    #[test]
    fn main_ends_with_the_line_about_the_cli() {
        let World { _dir, paths, .. } = world();
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        main(&paths, &mut system);
        assert!(system.said[0].ends_with(FINAL_MESSAGE), "{:?}", system.said);
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_an_install_folder_that_is_not_harness_or_holds_the_profile() {
        let World { _dir, paths, place } = world();
        for install in [paths.profile.clone(), paths.profile.join("Programs"), PathBuf::from("Harness"), paths.profile.join("x").join("..").join("Harness")] {
            let bad = Paths { install, ..paths.clone() };
            assert!(run(&bad, &place, &mut Fake::default()).is_err(), "{:?}", bad.install);
        }
        let above = Paths { install: paths.profile.parent().unwrap().join("Harness"), profile: paths.profile.parent().unwrap().join("Harness").join("me"), ..paths.clone() };
        assert!(check_install(&above.install, &above.profile).unwrap_err().contains("your profile is in it"));
        // Nothing was touched.
        assert!(paths.shortcut().exists() && paths.profile.join(".harness").join("desktop-app").exists());
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn links_are_removed_as_links_and_never_followed() {
        let World { _dir, paths, place } = world();
        let outside = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        fs::write(outside.path().join("keep"), b"x").unwrap();
        let harness = paths.profile.join(".harness");
        fs::remove_dir_all(harness.join("desktop-app")).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(outside.path(), harness.join("desktop-app")).unwrap();
        run(&paths, &place, &mut Fake::default()).unwrap();
        assert!(fs::symlink_metadata(harness.join("desktop-app")).is_err());
        assert!(outside.path().join("keep").exists());
        // An install folder that is a link is refused.
        let linked = paths.profile.join("Linked").join("Harness");
        fs::create_dir_all(linked.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(outside.path(), &linked).unwrap();
        assert!(check_install(&linked, &paths.profile).unwrap_err().contains("is a link"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_script_waits_for_the_launcher_and_carries_the_path_as_data() {
        let install = PathBuf::from(r"C:\Users\Nguyễn Văn A' & 100% !x (2)\AppData\Local\Programs\Harness");
        let text = final_removal_script(4242, &install, Path::new(r"C:\T\h.log"), Path::new(r"C:\Windows")).unwrap();
        // Joined by the host's rules, so the test reads the same on every OS.
        let tool = |name: &str| Path::new(r"C:\Windows").join("System32").join(name).display().to_string();
        assert!(text.starts_with(&format!("@echo off\r\nsetlocal DisableDelayedExpansion\r\n\"{}\" 65001 >nul\r\n", tool("chcp.com"))), "{text}");
        assert!(text.contains(&format!(r#""{}" /FI "PID eq 4242" /NH 2>nul | "{}" " 4242 " >nul"#, tool("tasklist.exe"), tool("find.exe"))));
        assert!(text.contains(r#"rmdir /s /q "C:\Users\Nguyễn Văn A' & 100%% !x (2)\AppData\Local\Programs\Harness" 2>nul"#));
        assert!(text.contains(r#"echo Harness could not remove C:\Users\Nguyễn Văn A' ^& 100%% !x ^(2^)\AppData\Local\Programs\Harness after"#));
        assert!(text.contains(r#"for %%A in ("C:\Users\Nguyễn Văn A' & 100%% !x (2)\AppData\Local\Programs\Harness") do set "attr=-%%~aA""#));
        assert!(text.ends_with("(goto) 2>nul & del \"%~f0\"\r\n"));
        assert!(final_removal_script(1, Path::new("C:\\a\"b\\Harness"), Path::new(r"C:\T\h.log"), Path::new(r"C:\Windows")).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_step_that_cannot_be_written_or_started_leaves_no_script_and_says_what_to_delete() {
        let World { _dir, paths, place } = world();
        // A temp folder inside the install is refused before anything is written.
        let inside = ScriptPlace { temp: paths.install.join("tmp"), system_root: place.system_root.clone() };
        assert!(schedule_final_removal(&paths.install, &inside, &mut Fake::default()).unwrap_err().contains("is inside"));
        let mut system = Fake { fail_script: true, ..Fake::default() };
        let problems = run(&paths, &place, &mut system).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(problems.len(), 1, "{problems:?}");
        assert!(problems[0].contains("Windows did not start the step") && problems[0].contains("yourself"), "{problems:?}");
        assert!(fs::read_dir(&place.temp).unwrap().next().is_none());
    }
}

````rust
/// `cmd.exe /d /v:off /c .\<script>`, from the script's folder, hidden and outside this job when the job allows it.
/// cmd gets the script's name only: `cmd /c` expands a `%VAR%` in its command line, so a full path holding `%` would
/// run as another. /v:off keeps a `!` a `!`; /d skips the AutoRun commands the registry may give every cmd.
pub fn start_script(script: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    let dir = script.parent().ok_or_else(|| io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput))?;
    let name = script.file_name().ok_or_else(|| io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput))?;
    let system_root = std::env::var_os("SystemRoot").unwrap_or_else(|| OsString::from(r"C:\Windows"));
    let cmd = PathBuf::from(system_root).join("System32").join("cmd.exe");
    let mut target = OsString::from(r".\");
    target.push(name);
    let args = [OsString::from("/d"), OsString::from("/v:off"), OsString::from("/c"), target];
    let application = wide(cmd.as_os_str());
    let directory = wide(dir.as_os_str());
    crate::launcher::start(
        |flags| {
            let mut line = command_line(&cmd, &args);
            line.push(0);
            let mut startup: STARTUPINFOW = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
            startup.cb = std::mem::size_of::<STARTUPINFOW>() as u32;
            let mut info: PROCESS_INFORMATION = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
            let ok = unsafe {
                CreateProcessW(application.as_ptr(), line.as_mut_ptr(), null(), null(), 0, flags, null(), directory.as_ptr(), &startup, &mut info)
            };
            if ok == 0 {
                return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
            }
            unsafe {
                CloseHandle(info.hThread);
                CloseHandle(info.hProcess);
            }
            Ok(info.dwProcessId)
        },
        |_| {},
    )
    .map(|_| ())
}

- Create: `desktop/lib/update/started_marker.dart`, `desktop/test/started_marker_test.dart`.
- Modify: `desktop/lib/main.dart`.

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  - `desktop::rollback::decide(&LaunchHistory) -> Choice`, pure, with
    `struct LaunchHistory { now_ms, current: Option<String>, current_exe, current_started, previous: Option<String>, previous_exe, instance_running, starts: Vec<Looked> }`,
    `struct Looked { start: Start, liveness: Liveness }`, `struct Start { version, at_ms, pid, created }`,
    `enum Liveness { Running, Ended, Unknown }`, `enum Choice { Launch { version, record: Record }, RollBack { to, reason }, Broken { reason } }`,
    `enum Record { Append, Clear, Keep }`, `outcome`, `recorded`, `START_WINDOW_MS = 10_000`, `KEPT_STARTS = 2`;
  - `desktop::launch::{State, read_state, write_state, look, STATE}` (`launch-state.json` beside `launch.log`);
  - `desktop::win::liveness(pid, created) -> Liveness`;
  - Dart `const startedMarkerName = '.started'`, `File? startedMarkerFile({String? executablePath, bool? isWindows})`,
    `Future<void> markStartedAfterFirstFrame({required Future<void> firstFrame, String? executablePath, bool? isWindows})`.
- The state machine, which `rollback.rs`'s module comment states as the code's contract:
  - The launcher cannot see the app end, since it exits first. It records each start (version, time, pid and the
    process's creation time) in `launch-state.json`, keeping two. At the next start it looks at two facts:
    `app\<current>\.started`, written once per version folder after the first frame; and whether each recorded
    start's process still runs, where a pid now owned by a process created later reads as ended.
  - A recorded start of a version without `.started` is Running (its process is there: still starting, or a slow
    first frame, which is never a failure, Review Focus 4), or Failed (its process ended without a first frame). When
    the process cannot be looked at, the start counts as Failed once it is 10 s old (`START_WINDOW_MS`), the spec's
    window.
  - In order:
    1. `current` unreadable, or its folder has no `harness-desktop.exe`: roll back to `previous` if it has its exe,
       else Broken (message box, exit 3).
    2. An app from this install is running: launch, recording nothing (the new process hands over its link and ends).
    3. `.started` exists: launch and forget the recorded starts.
    4. The last two recorded starts are both `current`'s and both Failed: roll back to `previous` if it has its exe.
    5. Otherwise: launch and record the start.
  - A rollback writes `current` = previous, removes `previous` and the recorded starts, logs why, and launches the
    version gone back to in the same run. So `current` names a broken folder for at most two starts, and the third
    start is the working version (Review Focus 3).

//! The real `Harness.exe` launch path: it starts `app\<current>\harness-desktop.exe` from its version folder with the
//! link it was given, records the start and exits; `--wait-pid` waits for the app being replaced; a broken install
//! exits 3 and says why in launch.log. On Windows, two starts that end without a first frame go back to `previous`.
//! The app is this test's own executable (desktop_common).
mod desktop_common;

use std::fs;
use std::process::Command;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use desktop_common::*;

fn main() {
    desktop_common::main(&[
        ("starts_the_current_version_with_the_link_from_its_folder", starts_the_current_version_with_the_link_from_its_folder),
        ("waits_for_the_app_being_replaced", waits_for_the_app_being_replaced),
        ("a_broken_install_exits_3_and_says_why_in_the_log", a_broken_install_exits_3_and_says_why_in_the_log),
        ("a_usage_error_exits_2", a_usage_error_exits_2),
        #[cfg(windows)]
        ("two_starts_without_a_window_go_back_to_previous", two_starts_without_a_window_go_back_to_previous),
    ]);
}

fn starts_the_current_version_with_the_link_from_its_folder() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = dir.path().join(ODD_NAME).join("Harness");
    put_app(&root, "1.2.3");
    point(&root, "current", "1.2.3");
    let out = dir.path().join("report.json");
    let started = Instant::now();
    let status = launcher()
        .arg("harness://notification/machine 1/agent")
        .env("HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT", &root)
        .env(STANDIN_OUT, &out)
        .env(STANDIN_SLEEP_MS, "3000")
        .status()
        .unwrap();
    assert!(status.success(), "{status:?}");
    // It does not wait for the app.
    assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(3), "{:?}", started.elapsed());
    let report = report(&out);
    assert_eq!(report["args"], serde_json::json!(["harness://notification/machine 1/agent"]));
    assert!(same(report["cwd"].as_str().unwrap().as_ref(), &root.join("app").join("1.2.3")));
    let state: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(root.join("launch-state.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(state["starts"][0]["version"], "1.2.3");
    // The one line allowed is a job's refused breakaway: an SSH session's job is one, and the app then starts in it.
    let log = fs::read_to_string(root.join("launch.log")).unwrap_or_default();
    assert!(log.lines().all(|line| line.contains("refuses a breakaway")), "{log}");
}

fn waits_for_the_app_being_replaced() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = dir.path().join("Harness");
    put_app(&root, "1.2.3");
    point(&root, "current", "1.2.3");
    // The app being replaced: this executable as the stand-in, for two seconds.
    let mut old = Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
        .env(STANDIN_OUT, dir.path().join("old.json"))
        .env(STANDIN_SLEEP_MS, "2000")
        .spawn()
        .unwrap();
    let started = Instant::now();
    let out = dir.path().join("new.json");
    let status = launcher()
        .args(["--wait-pid", &old.id().to_string()])
        .env("HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT", &root)
        .env(STANDIN_OUT, &out)
        .status()
        .unwrap();
    assert!(status.success());
    assert!(started.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(1500), "{:?}", started.elapsed());
    old.wait().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(report(&out)["args"], serde_json::json!([]));
}

fn a_broken_install_exits_3_and_says_why_in_the_log() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let output = launcher().env("HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT", dir.path()).output().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(output.status.code(), Some(3));
    assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).contains("Download Harness again"));
    assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join("launch.log")).unwrap().contains("`current` is missing"));
}

fn a_usage_error_exits_2() {
    let status = launcher().args(["--install", "now"]).status().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status.code(), Some(2));
}

/// Review Focus 3: 2.0.0 ends at once without `.started`; the third start is 1.0.0, which has drawn its window.
#[cfg(windows)]
fn two_starts_without_a_window_go_back_to_previous() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = dir.path().join("Harness");
    put_app(&root, "1.0.0");
    fs::write(root.join("app").join("1.0.0").join(".started"), b"").unwrap();
    put_app(&root, "2.0.0");
    point(&root, "current", "2.0.0");
    point(&root, "previous", "1.0.0");
    let mut folders = Vec::new();
    for n in 0..3 {
        let out = dir.path().join(format!("{n}.json"));
        let status = launcher().env("HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT", &root).env(STANDIN_OUT, &out).status().unwrap();
        assert!(status.success());
        let cwd = report(&out)["cwd"].as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
        folders.push(std::path::Path::new(&cwd).file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().into_owned());
        // The stand-in has ended once its report is whole; give Windows a moment to finish it off.
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
    }
    assert_eq!(folders, ["2.0.0", "2.0.0", "1.0.0"]);
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(root.join("current")).unwrap(), "1.0.0\r\n");
    assert!(!root.join("previous").exists());
    assert!(fs::read_to_string(root.join("launch.log")).unwrap().contains("went back to 1.0.0"));
}
