````rust
//! When `Harness.exe` goes back to the version before an update (desktop spec section 3.4, Review Focus 3).
//!
//! The launcher starts the app and exits, so it never sees the app end. It learns what became of a start at the
//! next one, from two facts:
//! - whether the version folder holds `.started`, which the app writes once its first frame is drawn
//!   (desktop/lib/update/started_marker.dart). It is written once per version folder: a version that has drawn a
//!   window once is a working version, and is never rolled back for a later crash.
//! - whether the process that start created is still running: the pid and its creation time are recorded, so a pid
//!   Windows has given to another process since reads as ended.
//!
//! Each recorded start of a version that has no `.started` is then:
//! - `Running`: its process is still there (still starting, or a slow first frame). Never a failure: a second
//!   launch while the first is still starting must not count (Review Focus 4).
//! - `Failed`: its process has ended without a first frame. When the process could not be looked at (`Unknown`),
//!   the start counts as failed once it is [START_WINDOW_MS] old with no `.started`, the spec's 10 s.
//!
//! The state machine, run on every launch over `current`, `previous`, the version folders and the recorded starts:
//!
//! ```text
//! current unreadable, or app\<current> has no harness-desktop.exe
//!     -> RollBack to previous, if previous has its exe; else Broken
//! an instance from this install is already running
//!     -> Launch, recording nothing (the new process hands its link to the open window and ends)
//! app\<current>\.started exists
//!     -> Launch, and forget the recorded starts
//! the last two recorded starts are both current's, and both Failed
//!     -> RollBack to previous, if previous has its exe; else Launch, recording the start
//! otherwise
//!     -> Launch, recording the start (two are kept)
//! ```
//!
//! A rollback writes `current` = previous, removes `previous` and the recorded starts, and logs why; the next pass
//! of the machine then launches the version gone back to. So `current` names a broken folder for at most two
//! starts, and the third start is the working version.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// How long a start whose process cannot be looked at has to draw its first frame.
pub const START_WINDOW_MS: u64 = 10_000;
/// How many starts are kept, and how many failures in a row roll back.
pub const KEPT_STARTS: usize = 2;

/// A start the launcher made: the version, when (ms since the Unix epoch), and the process it created.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Start {
    pub version: String,
    pub at_ms: u64,
    pub pid: u32,
    /// The process's creation time (a FILETIME), 0 when unknown.
    pub created: u64,
}

/// Whether a recorded start's process is still there.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Liveness {
    Running,
    Ended,
    Unknown,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Looked {
    pub start: Start,
    pub liveness: Liveness,
}

/// Everything [decide] reads.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LaunchHistory {
    pub now_ms: u64,
    /// The version `current` names; None when it is missing or does not name one folder.
    pub current: Option<String>,
    pub current_exe: bool,
    pub current_started: bool,
    pub previous: Option<String>,
    pub previous_exe: bool,
    /// An app from this install is running now.
    pub instance_running: bool,
    /// The recorded starts, oldest first.
    pub starts: Vec<Looked>,
}

/// What a launch does with the recorded starts.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Record {
    /// Add this start (keeping the last [KEPT_STARTS]).
    Append,
    /// Forget them: the version has drawn its window.
    Clear,
    /// Leave them: this start only hands a link to the open window.
    Keep,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Choice {
    Launch { version: String, record: Record },
    RollBack { to: String, reason: String },
    Broken { reason: String },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Outcome {
    Running,
    Failed,
    Waiting,
}

/// What became of [looked], a start of a version with no `.started`.
pub fn outcome(looked: &Looked, now_ms: u64) -> Outcome {
    match looked.liveness {
        Liveness::Running => Outcome::Running,
        Liveness::Ended => Outcome::Failed,
        Liveness::Unknown if now_ms.saturating_sub(looked.start.at_ms) >= START_WINDOW_MS => Outcome::Failed,
        Liveness::Unknown => Outcome::Waiting,
    }
}

pub fn decide(history: &LaunchHistory) -> Choice {
    let fallback = history
        .previous
        .as_ref()
        .filter(|previous| history.previous_exe && Some(*previous) != history.current.as_ref());
    let go_back = |reason: String| match fallback {
        Some(previous) => Choice::RollBack { to: previous.clone(), reason },
        None => Choice::Broken { reason: format!("{reason}, and there is no earlier version to go back to") },
    };
    let Some(current) = history.current.as_ref() else {
        return go_back("`current` is missing or does not name one version folder".to_owned());
    };
    if !history.current_exe {
        return go_back(format!("app\\{current} has no {}", super::APP_EXE));
    }
    if history.instance_running {
        return Choice::Launch { version: current.clone(), record: Record::Keep };
    }
    if history.current_started {
        return Choice::Launch { version: current.clone(), record: Record::Clear };
    }
    let last = &history.starts[history.starts.len().saturating_sub(KEPT_STARTS)..];
    let failed = last.len() == KEPT_STARTS
        && last.iter().all(|looked| &looked.start.version == current && outcome(looked, history.now_ms) == Outcome::Failed);
    if failed && fallback.is_some() {
        return go_back(format!("{current} ended {KEPT_STARTS} times in a row before it drew its first window"));
    }
    Choice::Launch { version: current.clone(), record: Record::Append }
}

/// [starts] after a launch: [record] applied to the [start] just made.
pub fn recorded(mut starts: Vec<Start>, start: Option<Start>, record: Record) -> Vec<Start> {
    match (record, start) {
        (Record::Clear, _) => Vec::new(),
        (Record::Keep, _) | (Record::Append, None) => starts,
        (Record::Append, Some(start)) => {
            starts.push(start);
            let drop = starts.len().saturating_sub(KEPT_STARTS);
            starts.drain(..drop);
            starts
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const NOW: u64 = 1_000_000;

    fn start(version: &str, ago_ms: u64, liveness: Liveness) -> Looked {
        Looked { start: Start { version: version.into(), at_ms: NOW - ago_ms, pid: 10, created: 1 }, liveness }
    }

    /// An updated install: current 2.0.0 and previous 1.0.0, both with their exe, nothing running, no `.started`.
    fn updated(starts: Vec<Looked>) -> LaunchHistory {
        LaunchHistory {
            now_ms: NOW,
            current: Some("2.0.0".into()),
            current_exe: true,
            current_started: false,
            previous: Some("1.0.0".into()),
            previous_exe: true,
            instance_running: false,
            starts,
        }
    }

    fn launch(record: Record) -> Choice {
        Choice::Launch { version: "2.0.0".into(), record }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_exe_goes_back_at_once() {
        let history = LaunchHistory { current_exe: false, ..updated(vec![]) };
        assert!(matches!(decide(&history), Choice::RollBack { ref to, ref reason } if to == "1.0.0" && reason.contains("has no harness-desktop.exe")));
        let history = LaunchHistory { current: None, ..updated(vec![]) };
        assert!(matches!(decide(&history), Choice::RollBack { ref to, .. } if to == "1.0.0"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn with_nothing_to_go_back_to_a_missing_exe_is_broken() {
        let history = LaunchHistory { current_exe: false, previous: None, ..updated(vec![]) };
        assert!(matches!(decide(&history), Choice::Broken { ref reason } if reason.contains("no earlier version")));
        let history = LaunchHistory { current_exe: false, previous_exe: false, ..updated(vec![]) };
        assert!(matches!(decide(&history), Choice::Broken { .. }));
        // previous naming the broken current is no way back either.
        let history = LaunchHistory { current_exe: false, previous: Some("2.0.0".into()), ..updated(vec![]) };
        assert!(matches!(decide(&history), Choice::Broken { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn two_starts_that_ended_without_a_first_frame_go_back() {
        let history = updated(vec![start("2.0.0", 60_000, Liveness::Ended), start("2.0.0", 2_000, Liveness::Ended)]);
        assert!(matches!(decide(&history), Choice::RollBack { ref to, ref reason } if to == "1.0.0" && reason.contains("2 times in a row")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn one_failed_start_is_not_enough() {
        assert_eq!(decide(&updated(vec![start("2.0.0", 2_000, Liveness::Ended)])), launch(Record::Append));
        assert_eq!(decide(&updated(vec![])), launch(Record::Append));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_start_still_running_never_counts_against_its_version() {
        let history = updated(vec![start("2.0.0", 2_000, Liveness::Ended), start("2.0.0", 1_000, Liveness::Running)]);
        assert_eq!(decide(&history), launch(Record::Append));
        let history = updated(vec![start("2.0.0", 90_000, Liveness::Running), start("2.0.0", 1_000, Liveness::Ended)]);
        assert_eq!(decide(&history), launch(Record::Append));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_running_instance_takes_the_launch_and_nothing_is_recorded() {
        // Review Focus 4: a second launch while the first is starting, or a link clicked while it runs.
        let history = LaunchHistory {
            instance_running: true,
            ..updated(vec![start("2.0.0", 3_000, Liveness::Ended), start("2.0.0", 2_000, Liveness::Ended)])
        };
        assert_eq!(decide(&history), launch(Record::Keep));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_version_that_drew_its_window_once_is_never_rolled_back() {
        let history = LaunchHistory {
            current_started: true,
            ..updated(vec![start("2.0.0", 3_000, Liveness::Ended), start("2.0.0", 2_000, Liveness::Ended)])
        };
        assert_eq!(decide(&history), launch(Record::Clear));
    }

    #[test]
    fn when_a_start_cannot_be_looked_at_it_has_ten_seconds() {
        let young = updated(vec![start("2.0.0", 30_000, Liveness::Unknown), start("2.0.0", 9_999, Liveness::Unknown)]);
        assert_eq!(decide(&young), launch(Record::Append));
        let old = updated(vec![start("2.0.0", 30_000, Liveness::Unknown), start("2.0.0", START_WINDOW_MS, Liveness::Unknown)]);
        assert!(matches!(decide(&old), Choice::RollBack { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn only_two_failures_of_current_in_a_row_count() {
        // The older failure was the previous version's.
        let history = updated(vec![start("1.0.0", 60_000, Liveness::Ended), start("2.0.0", 2_000, Liveness::Ended)]);
        assert_eq!(decide(&history), launch(Record::Append));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_first_install_that_keeps_failing_keeps_launching_its_only_version() {
        let history = LaunchHistory {
            previous: None,
            previous_exe: false,
            ..updated(vec![start("2.0.0", 3_000, Liveness::Ended), start("2.0.0", 2_000, Liveness::Ended)])
        };
        assert_eq!(decide(&history), launch(Record::Append));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_rollback_leaves_a_working_app_by_the_third_start() {
        // The whole sequence, as launch.rs runs it: two failed starts of 2.0.0, then the third goes back.
        let mut starts: Vec<Start> = Vec::new();
        let mut current = "2.0.0".to_owned();
        let mut previous = Some("1.0.0".to_owned());
        let mut launched = Vec::new();
        for n in 0..3u64 {
            let looked = starts.iter().map(|s| Looked { start: s.clone(), liveness: Liveness::Ended }).collect();
            let history = LaunchHistory {
                now_ms: NOW + n * 1_000,
                current: Some(current.clone()),
                current_exe: true,
                current_started: current == "1.0.0",
                previous: previous.clone(),
                previous_exe: previous.is_some(),
                instance_running: false,
                starts: looked,
            };
            let choice = match decide(&history) {
                Choice::RollBack { to, .. } => {
                    current = to;
                    previous = None;
                    starts.clear();
                    let history = LaunchHistory { current: Some(current.clone()), current_started: true, previous: None, previous_exe: false, starts: vec![], ..history };
                    decide(&history)
                }
                other => other,
            };
            let Choice::Launch { version, record } = choice else { panic!("{choice:?}") };
            let made = Start { version: version.clone(), at_ms: NOW + n * 1_000, pid: n as u32 + 1, created: n + 1 };
            starts = recorded(starts, Some(made), record);
            launched.push(version);
        }
        assert_eq!(launched, ["2.0.0", "2.0.0", "1.0.0"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn records_keep_the_last_two_starts() {
        let s = |n: u64| Start { version: "2.0.0".into(), at_ms: n, pid: n as u32, created: n };
        assert_eq!(recorded(vec![s(1), s(2)], Some(s(3)), Record::Append), vec![s(2), s(3)]);
        assert_eq!(recorded(vec![s(1)], Some(s(2)), Record::Keep), vec![s(1)]);
        assert_eq!(recorded(vec![s(1)], Some(s(2)), Record::Clear), vec![]);
        assert_eq!(recorded(vec![s(1)], None, Record::Append), vec![s(1)]);
    }
}
````

````rust
/// Whether the process [pid] still runs. [recorded] is its creation time when it was started: a pid Windows has
/// since given to another process reads as ended.
pub fn liveness(pid: u32, recorded: u64) -> Liveness {
    let process = unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, 0, pid) };
    if process.is_null() {
        // No such process; any other refusal is one we may not look at.
        return match io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error() {
            Some(code) if code == ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER as i32 => Liveness::Ended,
            _ => Liveness::Unknown,
        };
    }
    let mut code = 0u32;
    let state = if recorded != 0 && created(process) != recorded {
        Liveness::Ended
    } else if unsafe { GetExitCodeProcess(process, &mut code) } == 0 {
        Liveness::Unknown
    } else if code == STILL_ACTIVE as u32 {
        Liveness::Running
    } else {
        Liveness::Ended
    };
    unsafe { CloseHandle(process) };
    state
}

  Replace `pty/src/desktop/launch.rs` with (C4.2's, with the machine in `run`, the state file and its tests):

````rust
//! The launch path: `Harness.exe [--wait-pid <pid>] [<link>...]` starts `app\<current>\harness-desktop.exe` from its
//! version folder with the same arguments, records the start, and exits. Before that it heals the `harness://` key
//! when it is the installed launcher (spec section 2.3: a moved install heals itself), and it applies the rollback
//! rules (rollback.rs). What it did not manage goes to `launch.log` beside it, kept to [LOG_MAX_BYTES].

use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::fs;
use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::path::Path;
use std::time::Duration;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use super::pointer::{self, CURRENT, PREVIOUS};
use super::registry;
use super::rollback::{self, Choice, LaunchHistory, Looked, Start};
use super::system::System;
use super::{APP_DIR, APP_EXE, EXIT_BROKEN, EXIT_OK, EXIT_SPAWN, LAUNCHER_EXE, STARTED_MARKER};

pub const LOG: &str = "launch.log";
pub const STATE: &str = "launch-state.json";
/// Past this the log keeps its newer half.
pub const LOG_MAX_BYTES: u64 = 64 * 1024;
/// How long `--wait-pid` waits for the app being replaced to end.
pub const WAIT_FOR_REPLACED: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15);

/// One line in `<root>\launch.log`. When the line would take the file past [LOG_MAX_BYTES], the older half goes
/// first, from a line's start. A log that cannot be written is not a second failure.
pub fn log(root: &Path, message: &str) {
    let path = root.join(LOG);
    let seconds = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).map(|d| d.as_secs()).unwrap_or(0);
    let line = format!("{seconds} Harness.exe: {message}\n");
    if let Ok(meta) = fs::metadata(&path)
        && meta.len() + line.len() as u64 > LOG_MAX_BYTES
        && let Ok(text) = fs::read(&path)
    {
        let from = text.len().saturating_sub((LOG_MAX_BYTES / 2) as usize);
        let start = text[from..].iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n').map(|i| from + i + 1).unwrap_or(text.len());
        let _ = fs::write(&path, &text[start..]);
    }
    if let Ok(mut file) = fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(&path) {
        let _ = file.write_all(line.as_bytes());
    }
}

/// `launch-state.json`: the starts rollback.rs judges.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct State {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub starts: Vec<Start>,
}

/// The recorded starts; none when the file is missing or unreadable (a lost record only delays a rollback).
pub fn read_state(root: &Path) -> State {
    fs::read(root.join(STATE)).ok().and_then(|bytes| serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).ok()).unwrap_or_default()
}

pub fn write_state(root: &Path, state: &State) -> io::Result<()> {
    let path = root.join(STATE);
    let tmp = root.join(format!("{STATE}.tmp"));
    let written = (|| {
        let mut out = fs::File::create(&tmp)?;
        out.write_all(&serde_json::to_vec(state).map_err(io::Error::other)?)?;
        out.sync_all()?;
        drop(out);
        crate::files::rename(&tmp, &path)
    })();
    if written.is_err() {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp);
    }
    written
}

/// What the machine in rollback.rs reads, looked up now.
pub fn look(root: &Path, state: &State, system: &mut impl System) -> LaunchHistory {
    let app = root.join(APP_DIR);
    let current = pointer::read(&root.join(CURRENT)).ok();
    let previous = pointer::read(&root.join(PREVIOUS)).ok();
    let has = |version: &Option<String>, name: &str| version.as_ref().is_some_and(|v| app.join(v).join(name).is_file());
    LaunchHistory {
        now_ms: system.now_ms(),
        current_exe: has(&current, APP_EXE),
        current_started: has(&current, STARTED_MARKER),
        previous_exe: has(&previous, APP_EXE),
        instance_running: !system.app_processes(root).is_empty(),
        starts: state.starts.iter().map(|start| Looked { start: start.clone(), liveness: system.liveness(start.pid, start.created) }).collect(),
        current,
        previous,
    }
}

/// `current` back to [to], and no `previous`: there is nothing older to go back to after this.
fn go_back(root: &Path, to: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    pointer::write(&root.join(CURRENT), to)?;
    pointer::remove(&root.join(PREVIOUS))
}

/// The `harness://` key names this launcher; rewritten when it names anything else. One registry read when it does.
pub fn heal_protocol_key(root: &Path, registry_root: &str, system: &mut impl System) {
    let launcher = root.join(LAUNCHER_EXE);
    let want = registry::open_command(&launcher);
    let key = registry::protocol_command_key(registry::SCHEME);
    if system.read_value(registry_root, &key, "").as_deref() == Some(want.as_os_str()) {
        return;
    }
    match system.write_keys(registry_root, &registry::protocol_keys(registry::SCHEME, &launcher)) {
        Ok(()) => log(root, &format!("harness:// links now open {}", launcher.display())),
        Err(err) => log(root, &format!("could not point harness:// links at {}: {err}", launcher.display())),
    }
}

/// The launch: see the module comment.
pub fn run(root: &Path, wait_pid: Option<u32>, args: &[OsString], system: &mut impl System) -> i32 {
    if let Some(pid) = wait_pid {
        system.wait_for_exit(pid, WAIT_FOR_REPLACED);
    }
    let mut state = read_state(root);
    // At most one rollback: it removes `previous`, so the second pass launches or is broken.
    for _ in 0..2 {
        let history = look(root, &state, system);
        match rollback::decide(&history) {
            Choice::RollBack { to, reason } => {
                if let Err(err) = go_back(root, &to) {
                    log(root, &format!("could not go back to {to} ({reason}): {err}"));
                    system.say(&format!("Harness could not start, and could not go back to version {to}: {err}."));
                    return EXIT_BROKEN;
                }
                log(root, &format!("went back to {to}: {reason}"));
                state = State::default();
                if let Err(err) = write_state(root, &state) {
                    log(root, &format!("could not clear the recorded starts: {err}"));
                }
            }
            Choice::Broken { reason } => {
                log(root, &reason);
                system.say(&format!("Harness cannot start: {reason}. Download Harness again and open it to repair it."));
                return EXIT_BROKEN;
            }
            Choice::Launch { version, record } => {
                let dir = root.join(APP_DIR).join(&version);
                let exe = dir.join(APP_EXE);
                return match system.start_app(&exe, &dir, args) {
                    Ok((pid, created)) => {
                        let start = Start { version, at_ms: history.now_ms, pid, created };
                        let starts = rollback::recorded(state.starts, Some(start), record);
                        if let Err(err) = write_state(root, &State { starts }) {
                            log(root, &format!("could not record the start: {err}"));
                        }
                        EXIT_OK
                    }
                    Err(err) => {
                        log(root, &format!("could not start {}: {err}", exe.display()));
                        system.say(&format!("Harness could not start: {err}."));
                        EXIT_SPAWN
                    }
                };
            }
        }
    }
    EXIT_BROKEN
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::desktop::rollback::Liveness;
    use crate::desktop::system::Fake;
    use std::path::PathBuf;

    /// An install with these version folders (each with its exe) and pointers.
    fn install(versions: &[&str], current: Option<&str>, previous: Option<&str>) -> tempfile::TempDir {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        for version in versions {
            let folder = dir.path().join(APP_DIR).join(version);
            fs::create_dir_all(&folder).unwrap();
            fs::write(folder.join(APP_EXE), b"").unwrap();
        }
        if let Some(current) = current {
            pointer::write(&dir.path().join(CURRENT), current).unwrap();
        }
        if let Some(previous) = previous {
            pointer::write(&dir.path().join(PREVIOUS), previous).unwrap();
        }
        dir
    }

    fn os(args: &[&str]) -> Vec<OsString> {
        args.iter().map(OsString::from).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn starts_the_current_version_from_its_folder_with_the_links_and_records_it() {
        let dir = install(&["1.2.3"], Some("1.2.3"), None);
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        assert_eq!(run(dir.path(), None, &os(&["harness://x y"]), &mut system), EXIT_OK);
        let folder = dir.path().join(APP_DIR).join("1.2.3");
        assert_eq!(system.started, vec![(folder.join(APP_EXE), folder.clone(), os(&["harness://x y"]))]);
        let state = read_state(dir.path());
        assert_eq!(state.starts.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!((state.starts[0].version.as_str(), state.starts[0].pid), ("1.2.3", 100));
    }

    #[test]
    fn waits_for_the_app_being_replaced_first() {
        let dir = install(&["1.2.3"], Some("1.2.3"), None);
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        run(dir.path(), Some(77), &[], &mut system);
        assert_eq!(system.waited, vec![77]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_broken_install_says_so_and_exits_3() {
        let dir = install(&[], None, None);
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        assert_eq!(run(dir.path(), None, &[], &mut system), EXIT_BROKEN);
        assert!(system.said[0].contains("Download Harness again"), "{:?}", system.said);
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(LOG)).unwrap().contains("`current` is missing"));
        assert!(system.started.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_exe_goes_back_to_previous_and_logs_why() {
        let dir = install(&["1.0.0"], Some("2.0.0"), Some("1.0.0"));
        fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join(APP_DIR).join("2.0.0")).unwrap();
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        assert_eq!(run(dir.path(), None, &[], &mut system), EXIT_OK);
        assert_eq!(pointer::read(&dir.path().join(CURRENT)).unwrap(), "1.0.0");
        assert!(!dir.path().join(PREVIOUS).exists());
        assert!(system.started[0].0.ends_with(Path::new("1.0.0").join(APP_EXE)));
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(LOG)).unwrap().contains("went back to 1.0.0"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn two_starts_that_ended_without_a_window_go_back_on_the_third() {
        let dir = install(&["1.0.0", "2.0.0"], Some("2.0.0"), Some("1.0.0"));
        fs::write(dir.path().join(APP_DIR).join("1.0.0").join(STARTED_MARKER), b"").unwrap();
        let mut system = Fake { liveness: Liveness::Ended, ..Fake::default() };
        let mut versions = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..3 {
            run(dir.path(), None, &[], &mut system);
            versions.push(system.started.last().unwrap().1.file_name().unwrap().to_owned());
        }
        assert_eq!(versions, ["2.0.0", "2.0.0", "1.0.0"]);
        // 1.0.0 has drawn its window before: its starts are not kept.
        assert!(read_state(dir.path()).starts.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_start_while_the_app_runs_records_nothing() {
        let dir = install(&["2.0.0"], Some("2.0.0"), None);
        let mut system = Fake { running: vec![5], ..Fake::default() };
        run(dir.path(), None, &os(&["harness://link"]), &mut system);
        assert_eq!(system.started.len(), 1);
        assert!(read_state(dir.path()).starts.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_failed_start_says_so_and_exits_4() {
        let dir = install(&["1.2.3"], Some("1.2.3"), None);
        let mut system = Fake { fail_start: true, ..Fake::default() };
        assert_eq!(run(dir.path(), None, &[], &mut system), EXIT_SPAWN);
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(LOG)).unwrap().contains("could not start"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_installed_launcher_rewrites_a_harness_key_that_names_another_launcher() {
        let dir = install(&["1.2.3"], Some("1.2.3"), None);
        let mut system = Fake::default();
        let key = registry::protocol_command_key(registry::SCHEME);
        system.values.insert((r"Software\T".to_owned(), key.clone(), String::new()), OsString::from(r#""C:\old\Harness.exe" "%1""#));
        heal_protocol_key(dir.path(), r"Software\T", &mut system);
        let want = registry::open_command(&dir.path().join(LAUNCHER_EXE));
        assert_eq!(system.values.get(&(r"Software\T".to_owned(), key.clone(), String::new())), Some(&want));
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(LOG)).unwrap().contains("harness:// links now open"));
        // Right already: one read and no write.
        let writes = system.writes;
        heal_protocol_key(dir.path(), r"Software\T", &mut system);
        assert_eq!(system.writes, writes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_log_keeps_its_newer_half_past_its_size() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let old = "x".repeat(99) + "\n";
        fs::write(dir.path().join(LOG), old.repeat((LOG_MAX_BYTES / 100) as usize)).unwrap();
        log(dir.path(), "the newest line");
        let text = fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(LOG)).unwrap();
        assert!(text.len() as u64 <= LOG_MAX_BYTES / 2 + 100, "{}", text.len());
        assert!(text.starts_with('x') && text.ends_with("Harness.exe: the newest line\n"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unreadable_state_is_no_starts() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        fs::write(dir.path().join(STATE), b"{ not json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read_state(dir.path()), State::default());
        let starts = vec![Start { version: "1.0.0".into(), at_ms: 1, pid: 2, created: 3 }];
        write_state(dir.path(), &State { starts: starts.clone() }).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read_state(dir.path()).starts, starts);
        assert!(!PathBuf::from(dir.path()).join(format!("{STATE}.tmp")).exists());
    }
}

  Create `desktop/lib/update/started_marker.dart`:

````dart
import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;

import '../core/runtime_platform.dart';

/// The file Windows' `Harness.exe` looks for in a version folder: this version
/// has drawn a window once (pty/src/desktop/rollback.rs). Without it, two
/// starts in a row that end early send the launcher back to the version before
/// an update.
const startedMarkerName = '.started';

/// `app\<ver>\.started`, beside the running executable; null off Windows.
File? startedMarkerFile({String? executablePath, bool? isWindows}) {
  if (!(isWindows ?? RuntimePlatform.isWindows)) return null;
  final exe = executablePath ?? RuntimePlatform.resolvedExecutable;
  return File(p.join(p.dirname(exe), startedMarkerName));
}

/// Writes the marker once [firstFrame] completes (the engine's first frame,
/// `WidgetsBinding.waitUntilFirstFrameRasterized`). Once per version folder: a
/// marker already there is left as it is. A folder that cannot be written (a
/// copy run from a read-only place) only costs the rollback its signal, so a
/// failure is logged and swallowed.
Future<void> markStartedAfterFirstFrame({
  required Future<void> firstFrame,
  String? executablePath,
  bool? isWindows,
}) async {
  final marker = startedMarkerFile(
    executablePath: executablePath,
    isWindows: isWindows,
  );
  if (marker == null) return;
  await firstFrame;
  try {
    if (await marker.exists()) return;
    await marker.writeAsString(
      '${DateTime.now().toUtc().toIso8601String()}\n',
      flush: true,
    );
  } on FileSystemException catch (error) {
    debugPrint('startedMarker: could not write ${marker.path}: $error');
  }
}
````

  Replace `desktop/lib/main.dart` with (the same entry point, then the marker after the first frame; the helper does
  nothing off Windows, so macOS, Linux and the web are unchanged):

````dart
import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

import 'app_shell.dart';
import 'core/connected_semantics.dart';
import 'desktop_workspace.dart'
    if (dart.library.js_interop) 'web/web_entry.dart';
import 'update/started_marker.dart';

/// Harness: a swarm of terminal panes in one window. Everything before the
/// first frame, and every screen up to sign-in, is [startHarness]; only the
/// signed-in workspace and the frame around the app differ, picked at compile
/// time — a browser build gets the mouse-first `lib/web/` composition under
/// its store bar, native builds never compile it.
/// `../mobile` mounts a phone shell into its own vendored copy of
/// [startHarness] rather than depending on this package.
Future<void> main() async {
  HarnessWidgetsBinding();
  await startHarness(
    authenticatedScreen: authenticatedWorkspace,
    frame: appFrame,
    transportPlugins: terminalTransportPlugins,
  );
  // Windows only (it does nothing elsewhere): the version folder's `.started`,
  // which tells Harness.exe this version draws its window (rollback.rs).
  unawaited(
    markStartedAfterFirstFrame(
      firstFrame: WidgetsBinding.instance.waitUntilFirstFrameRasterized,
    ),
  );
}

### Task C4.5: The updater's Windows branch

**Files:**
- Create: `desktop/lib/update/windows_update_swap.dart`, `desktop/test/windows_update_swap_test.dart`.
- Modify: `desktop/lib/update/desktop_updater.dart`: keys, the staging manifest, `currentBundlePath`, constructor,
  `_otaKeys`, `downloadAndStage`, `applyStaged`; and the C1.6 guard removed.
- Modify: `desktop/test/desktop_updater_test.dart` (C1.6's "no update until its own branch" test removed),
  `desktop/test/manual_update_check_test.dart`.
- Modify: `desktop/CLAUDE.md`: C1.6's sentence that self-update is off on Windows.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the zip layout C4.7 packages; the launcher's `--wait-pid` launch form (C4.1) and pointer rules (C4.1).
- Produces:
  - `class WindowsUpdateSwap({required String installRoot, ExtractStep? extract, Future<void> Function(String, List<String>)? start})`
    with `Future<String?> stage({required String zipPath, required String version})`,
    `String? commit({required String version})`, `Future<void> relaunch(int selfPid)`, `Future<void> cleanUp()`;
  - top-level `String? extractUpdate(String zipPath, String installRoot, String version, {FileWriter write})`,
    `void cleanUpInstall(String installRoot)`, `bool validVersionFolder(String)`, `String? readPointer(String)`,
    `void writePointer(String, String)`, `String? windowsInstallRootOf(String executable)`,
    `String windowsMachineArchitecture()`, `typedef ExtractStep`, `typedef FileWriter`;
  - `DesktopUpdater({…, bool? isWindows, String? windowsInstallRoot, Future<void> Function(String, List<String>)? startDetached})`
    (`isWindows` and its default are C1.6's, unchanged; this task adds the other two);
    `currentBundlePath({…, bool? isWindows})`;
  - `@visibleForTesting String desktopUpdateMetadataUrl({String override, bool staging})`: the override
    (`DESKTOP_UPDATE_METADATA_URL`), else the staging manifest for a staging build (`kHarnessStagingBuild`, C1.3's
    `lib/core/staging_build.dart`), else the production one.
- The swap, in order, in two calls: `downloadAndStage` downloads, checks size and sha256, writes the zip to a temp
  folder and calls `stage` (the zip's `app\<ver>\` to `<root>\app\<ver>.staging`, `Harness.exe` and `Harness.ico` to
  `<name>.new`, off the UI isolate); `applyStaged` calls `commit` (rename to `app\<ver>`, `Harness.exe` replaced by
  rename through `.old`, then `previous`, then `current`, each atomic) and `relaunch` (`Harness.exe --wait-pid <pid>`),
  and the caller quits, as today. `cleanUp` runs at the next start (C4.6 calls it).
- The C1.6 guard: C1.6 keeps a Windows build from checking for updates until this task. It is the `!_isWindows` term
  in `DesktopUpdater.canCheck` (`bool get canCheck => !kIsWeb && !_isWindows && _enabled && _releaseMode;`); this task
  removes that term, and the new test `a release build on Windows checks for updates` pins `canCheck` and
  `AppNotifier.updateChecksEnabled`. C1.6 already added the `isWindows` parameter, the `_isWindows` field and their
  default (`isWindows ?? (isLinux == null && RuntimePlatform.isWindows)`): they stay as they are, and this task adds
  only `windowsInstallRoot` and `startDetached`.

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:harness/update/windows_update_swap.dart';

/// A Windows update zip as scripts/package-windows.ps1 builds it, with
/// [leave] entries missing and [extra] ones added.
Uint8List updateZip(
  String version, {
  Set<String> leave = const {},
  Map<String, String> extra = const {},
  String? current,
}) {
  final files = <String, String>{
    'Harness.exe': 'launcher $version',
    'Harness.ico': 'icon $version',
    'current': '${current ?? version}\r\n',
    'app/$version/harness-desktop.exe': 'app $version',
    'app/$version/data/app.so': 'so $version',
    ...extra,
  };
  final archive = Archive();
  for (final MapEntry(:key, :value) in files.entries) {
    if (leave.contains(key)) continue;
    archive.addFile(ArchiveFile.bytes(key, utf8.encode(value)));
  }
  return ZipEncoder().encodeBytes(archive);
}

  group('Windows', () {
    /// An install as `Harness.exe --install` left it: 1.0.0 in use.
    late String root;

    setUp(() {
      root = '${scratch.path}/Programs/Harness';
      Directory('$root/app/1.0.0').createSync(recursive: true);
      File('$root/app/1.0.0/harness-desktop.exe')
          .writeAsStringSync('app 1.0.0');
      File('$root/Harness.exe').writeAsStringSync('launcher 1.0.0');
      File('$root/current').writeAsStringSync('1.0.0\r\n');
    });

    /// The zip scripts/package-windows.ps1 builds for [version].
    List<int> windowsZip(String version) {
      final archive = Archive()
        ..addFile(
          ArchiveFile.bytes('Harness.exe', utf8.encode('launcher $version')),
        )
        ..addFile(ArchiveFile.bytes('current', utf8.encode('$version\r\n')))
        ..addFile(
          ArchiveFile.bytes(
            'app/$version/harness-desktop.exe',
            utf8.encode('app $version'),
          ),
        );
      return ZipEncoder().encodeBytes(archive);
    }

    /// A manifest of [versions] (key -> version), each entry serving [bytes].
    Future<String> serveWindows(
      Map<String, String> versions,
      List<int> bytes, {
      String? sha,
    }) async {
      final digest = sha ?? await _sha256Hex(bytes);
      server = await HttpServer.bind(InternetAddress.loopbackIPv4, 0);
      final base = 'http://127.0.0.1:${server!.port}';
      server!.listen((request) async {
        if (request.uri.path == '/metadata.json') {
          request.response.headers.contentType = ContentType.json;
          request.response.write(
            jsonEncode({
              for (final MapEntry(:key, :value) in versions.entries)
                key: {
                  'version': value,
                  'url': '$base/$key.zip',
                  'sha256': digest,
                  'size': bytes.length,
                },
            }),
          );
        } else {
          request.response.add(bytes);
        }
        await request.response.close();
      });
      return '$base/metadata.json';
    }

    DesktopUpdater windows(
      String url, {
      String architecture = 'x64',
      List<(String, List<String>)>? started,
    }) => DesktopUpdater(
      enabled: true,
      dio: Dio(),
      metadataUrl: url,
      releaseMode: true,
      isWindows: true,
      isLinux: false,
      architecture: architecture,
      windowsInstallRoot: root,
      startDetached: (exe, args) async => started?.add((exe, args)),
    );

        config: AppConfig.dev,
        authSession: AuthSession(),

      addTearDown(app.dispose);

    });

    test('a staging build polls the staging manifest, and the override wins over both', () {
      const production =

      const staging =
          'https://storage.googleapis.com/s3-autonomous-upgrade-3/harness/staging/desktop/metadata.json';
      expect(desktopUpdateMetadataUrl(override: '', staging: false), production);
      expect(desktopUpdateMetadataUrl(override: '', staging: true), staging);
      expect(
        desktopUpdateMetadataUrl(override: 'http://127.0.0.1:9/m.json', staging: true),

    test('an x64 PC reads desktop-windows-x64 only', () async {

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation.**

  Create `desktop/lib/update/windows_update_swap.dart`:

````dart
import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:ffi';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:isolate';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:archive/archive.dart';
import 'package:ffi/ffi.dart';
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;

import '../core/runtime_architecture.dart';

/// The Windows half of a self-update (desktop spec section 3.4), over the
/// per-user install `Harness.exe --install` made:
///
/// ```text
/// <root>\  Harness.exe  Harness.ico  current  previous  app\<ver>\
/// ```
///
/// [stage] unpacks a downloaded zip whose sha256 and size the updater has
/// already checked: its `app\<ver>\` to `app\<ver>.staging`, its `Harness.exe`
/// and `Harness.ico` to `<name>.new`. [commit] then renames the staged folder to
/// `app\<ver>`, swaps `Harness.exe` (and the icon) by rename (the launcher is not
/// running: it exits once it has started the app), and writes `previous` (the
/// version running now) and then `current`, each through a flushed temporary
/// file and a rename. [relaunch] starts `Harness.exe --wait-pid <this pid>`, so
/// the new app starts once this one has quit and let go of the single-instance
/// mutex.
///
/// Review Focus 3. A truncated or corrupt download never reaches here (the
/// sha256 and size). A zip that is not an install's shape, a full disk while
/// unpacking, or a staged folder with no `harness-desktop.exe` makes [stage]
/// fail, clear what it wrote, and leave `current` alone. Only [commit] moves
/// `current`, and only to a folder that has its executable; a version that
/// then fails to start is the launcher's to roll back. [cleanUp] removes, at
/// the next start, every `app\*` but `current` and `previous`, any
/// `*.staging`, and the `.new`/`.old` files.
class WindowsUpdateSwap {
  WindowsUpdateSwap({
    required this.installRoot,
    ExtractStep? extract,
    Future<void> Function(String executable, List<String> arguments)? start,
  }) : _extract = extract ?? _extractOffUiIsolate,
       _start = start ?? _startDetached;

  final String installRoot;
  final ExtractStep _extract;
  final Future<void> Function(String executable, List<String> arguments) _start;

  static const appExe = 'harness-desktop.exe';
  static const launcherExe = 'Harness.exe';
  static const icon = 'Harness.ico';

  String get _app => p.join(installRoot, 'app');
  String _staging(String version) => p.join(_app, '$version.staging');

  /// Unpacks [zipPath] for [version]. Null when it is staged, or why not.
  Future<String?> stage({
    required String zipPath,
    required String version,
  }) async {
    if (!validVersionFolder(version)) {
      return '"$version" is not a version folder name';
    }
    final current = readPointer(p.join(installRoot, 'current'));
    if (current == version) return 'Harness $version is already the one in use';
    _clearStaged(version);
    String? error;
    try {
      error = await _extract(zipPath, installRoot, version);
    } catch (e) {
      error = 'could not unpack the update: $e';
    }
    if (error == null &&
        !File(p.join(_staging(version), appExe)).existsSync()) {
      error = 'the update has no $appExe';
    }
    if (error == null &&
        !File(p.join(installRoot, '$launcherExe.new')).existsSync()) {
      error = 'the update has no $launcherExe';
    }
    if (error != null) _clearStaged(version);
    return error;
  }

  void _clearStaged(String version) {
    _deleteQuietly(_staging(version));
    for (final name in [launcherExe, icon]) {
      _deleteQuietly(p.join(installRoot, '$name.new'));
    }
  }

  /// Puts a staged [version] in place and points `current` at it. Null when
  /// done, or why not; on a failure `current` still names the running version.
  String? commit({required String version}) {
    final staged = Directory(_staging(version));
    if (!File(p.join(staged.path, appExe)).existsSync()) {
      return 'nothing is staged for $version';
    }
    final running = readPointer(p.join(installRoot, 'current'));
    final target = p.join(_app, version);
    try {
      if (running != version) _deleteQuietly(target);
      staged.renameSync(target);
    } on FileSystemException catch (e) {
      return 'could not move $version into place: ${e.message}';
    }
    final launcher = _replaceByRename(launcherExe);
    if (launcher != null) return launcher;
    // The icon is the shortcut's: an old one is no reason to stop.
    _replaceByRename(icon);
    try {
      if (running != null) {
        writePointer(p.join(installRoot, 'previous'), running);
      }
      writePointer(p.join(installRoot, 'current'), version);
    } on FileSystemException catch (e) {
      return 'could not point current at $version: ${e.message}';
    }
    return null;
  }

  /// `<name>.new` in place of `<name>`, the old one renamed to `<name>.old`
  /// first: a program can be renamed while something runs it, never replaced.
  String? _replaceByRename(String name) {
    final fresh = File(p.join(installRoot, '$name.new'));
    if (!fresh.existsSync()) return null;
    final live = File(p.join(installRoot, name));
    final old = p.join(installRoot, '$name.old');
    try {
      _deleteQuietly(old);
      if (live.existsSync()) live.renameSync(old);
      fresh.renameSync(live.path);
      return null;
    } on FileSystemException catch (e) {
      if (!live.existsSync() && File(old).existsSync()) {
        try {
          File(old).renameSync(live.path);
        } on FileSystemException {
          // Left as Harness.exe.old; the shortcut fails until a reinstall.
        }
      }
      return 'could not replace $name: ${e.message}';
    }
  }

  /// Starts the installed launcher, which waits for [selfPid] to end.
  Future<void> relaunch(int selfPid) =>
      _start(p.join(installRoot, launcherExe), ['--wait-pid', '$selfPid']);

  /// [cleanUpInstall] off the UI isolate: old version folders are thousands of
  /// files.
  Future<void> cleanUp() {
    final root = installRoot;
    return Isolate.run(() => cleanUpInstall(root));
  }
}

/// Unpacks a zip for [version] into [installRoot]; null when done, or why not.
typedef ExtractStep = Future<String?> Function(
  String zipPath,
  String installRoot,
  String version,
);

/// Writes one unpacked file (a seam for the full-disk test).
typedef FileWriter = void Function(String path, Uint8List bytes);

Future<String?> _extractOffUiIsolate(
  String zipPath,
  String installRoot,
  String version,
) => Isolate.run(() => extractUpdate(zipPath, installRoot, version));

Future<void> _startDetached(String executable, List<String> arguments) =>
    Process.start(
      executable,
      arguments,
      mode: ProcessStartMode.detached,
    ).then((_) {});

void _writeFile(String path, Uint8List bytes) {
  final file = File(path);
  file.parent.createSync(recursive: true);
  file.writeAsBytesSync(bytes, flush: true);
}

/// The zip's `app/<version>/…` under `<root>\app\<version>.staging`, and its
/// `Harness.exe` and `Harness.ico` as `<root>\<name>.new`. Everything else in
/// the zip is ignored. An entry that would land outside those (`..`, a drive,
/// a rooted path) or that is a link refuses the whole zip, as does a `current`
/// that names another version. Null when done, or why not.
String? extractUpdate(
  String zipPath,
  String installRoot,
  String version, {
  FileWriter write = _writeFile,
}) {
  final input = InputFileStream(zipPath);
  try {
    final archive = ZipDecoder().decodeStream(input);
    final prefix = 'app/$version/';
    final staging = p.join(installRoot, 'app', '$version.staging');
    var pointer = '';
    final writes = <(String, ArchiveFile)>[];
    for (final entry in archive.files) {
      final name = entry.name.replaceAll(r'\', '/');
      final parts = name.split('/');
      if (name.startsWith('/') ||
          name.contains(':') ||
          parts.any((part) => part == '..')) {
        return 'the update holds a file outside its folder: ${entry.name}';
      }
      if (entry.isSymbolicLink) {
        return 'the update holds a link: ${entry.name}';
      }
      if (!entry.isFile) continue;
      if (name == 'current') {
        pointer = String.fromCharCodes(entry.readBytes() ?? Uint8List(0));
      } else if (name == WindowsUpdateSwap.launcherExe ||
          name == WindowsUpdateSwap.icon) {
        writes.add((p.join(installRoot, '$name.new'), entry));
      } else if (name.startsWith(prefix) && name.length > prefix.length) {
        final rest = name.substring(prefix.length).split('/');
        writes.add((p.joinAll([staging, ...rest]), entry));
      }
    }
    final named = pointer.replaceFirst('﻿', '').trim();
    if (named != version) {
      return 'the update is for "$named", not $version';
    }
    Directory(staging).createSync(recursive: true);
    for (final (path, entry) in writes) {
      write(path, entry.readBytes() ?? Uint8List(0));
    }
    return null;
  } on FileSystemException catch (e) {
    return 'could not unpack the update: ${e.message} (${e.path})';
  } on Object catch (e) {
    return 'the update is not a readable zip: $e';
  } finally {
    input.closeSync();
  }
}

/// Every `app\*` but `current` and `previous`, every `*.staging`, and the
/// `.new`/`.old` launcher and icon files, removed. A link is removed as a link,
/// never followed. A folder still in use stays for the next start.
void cleanUpInstall(String installRoot) {
  final keep = {
    readPointer(p.join(installRoot, 'current')),
    readPointer(p.join(installRoot, 'previous')),
  }.whereType<String>().toSet();
  // Never empty an install whose pointers cannot be read: that is not the
  // state a running app comes from.
  if (keep.isEmpty) return;
  final app = Directory(p.join(installRoot, 'app'));
  if (app.existsSync()) {
    for (final entry in app.listSync(followLinks: false)) {
      final name = p.basename(entry.path);
      if (keep.contains(name)) continue;
      _deleteQuietly(entry.path);
    }
  }
  for (final name in [WindowsUpdateSwap.launcherExe, WindowsUpdateSwap.icon]) {
    for (final suffix in ['.new', '.old']) {
      _deleteQuietly(p.join(installRoot, '$name$suffix'));
    }
  }
}

void _deleteQuietly(String path) {
  try {
    switch (FileSystemEntity.typeSync(path, followLinks: false)) {
      case FileSystemEntityType.link:
        Link(path).deleteSync();
      case FileSystemEntityType.directory:
        Directory(path).deleteSync(recursive: true);
      case FileSystemEntityType.notFound:
        break;
      default:
        File(path).deleteSync();
    }
  } on FileSystemException {
    // In use (the running version's folder) or held by a scanner: next time.
  }
}

/// The launcher's rule for a version folder name (pty/src/desktop/pointer.rs).
bool validVersionFolder(String value) {
  if (value.isEmpty || value == '.' || value.contains('..')) return false;
  if (RegExp(r'[/\\:\x00-\x1f<>"|?*]').hasMatch(value)) return false;
  if (value.endsWith('.') || value.endsWith(' ')) return false;
  final stem = value.split('.').first.trimRight().toUpperCase();
  const devices = {'CON', 'PRN', 'AUX', 'NUL', r'CONIN$', r'CONOUT$'};
  if (devices.contains(stem)) return false;
  return !RegExp(r'^(COM|LPT)[1-9]$').hasMatch(stem);
}

/// A pointer's version folder, or null when it is missing or not one.
String? readPointer(String path) {
  try {
    final text = File(path).readAsStringSync().replaceFirst('﻿', '');
    final line = text.split(RegExp(r'\r?\n')).first.trim();
    return validVersionFolder(line) ? line : null;
  } on FileSystemException {
    return null;
  }
}

/// One line, `<value>\r\n`, through `<path>.tmp`, flushed, then renamed over
/// [path] (which replaces it on Windows as on POSIX).
void writePointer(String path, String value) {
  if (!validVersionFolder(value)) {
    throw FileSystemException('not one version folder: "$value"', path);
  }
  final tmp = File('$path.tmp');
  tmp.writeAsStringSync('$value\r\n', flush: true);
  tmp.renameSync(path);
}

/// The install root the running app is in: `<root>\app\<ver>\harness-desktop.exe`
/// with `Harness.exe` at `<root>`. Null for anything else (a development build).
String? windowsInstallRootOf(String executable) {
  if (p.basename(executable).toLowerCase() != WindowsUpdateSwap.appExe) {
    return null;
  }
  final versionFolder = p.dirname(executable);
  final app = p.dirname(versionFolder);
  if (p.basename(app).toLowerCase() != 'app') return null;
  final root = p.dirname(app);
  if (!File(p.join(root, WindowsUpdateSwap.launcherExe)).existsSync()) {
    return null;
  }
  return root;
}

/// `arm64` on an arm64 PC even when this build is x64 under emulation, so an
/// x64 build that stood in for a missing arm64 one (desktop spec Decision 6)
/// moves to arm64 once it is published. `IsWow64Process2`'s native machine;
/// the process's own architecture where Windows lacks it (before 1709).
String windowsMachineArchitecture() {
  const imageFileMachineArm64 = 0xAA64;
  try {
    final kernel32 = DynamicLibrary.open('kernel32.dll');
    final isWow64Process2 = kernel32
        .lookupFunction<
          Int32 Function(IntPtr, Pointer<Uint16>, Pointer<Uint16>),
          int Function(int, Pointer<Uint16>, Pointer<Uint16>)
        >('IsWow64Process2');
    final process = calloc<Uint16>();
    final native = calloc<Uint16>();
    try {
      // -1: GetCurrentProcess()'s pseudo handle.
      if (isWow64Process2(-1, process, native) != 0) {
        return native.value == imageFileMachineArm64 ? 'arm64' : 'x64';
      }
    } finally {
      calloc.free(process);
      calloc.free(native);
    }
  } catch (_) {
    // No IsWow64Process2: the process's own architecture below.
  }
  return runtimeArchitecture;
}
````

### Task C4.6: App-side self-install

**Files:**
- Create: `desktop/lib/bootstrap/windows_self_install.dart`, `desktop/test/windows_self_install_test.dart`,
  `desktop/test/windows_self_install_boot_test.dart`.
- Modify: `desktop/lib/state/app_state.dart`: imports, two fields, two constructor parameters, `bootstrap()`, and a
  new `_selfInstallTookOver()`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Harness.exe --install --wait-pid <pid>` (C4.2); `WindowsUpdateSwap` (its `cleanUp`, `appExe` and
  `launcherExe`, C4.5).
- Produces:
  - `sealed class SelfInstallOutcome` with `SelfInstallOutcome.alreadyInstalled`, `SelfInstallOutcome.relaunching`
    and `SelfInstallOutcome.failed(String message)`, whose classes are `AlreadyInstalled`, `Relaunching` and
    `SelfInstallFailed(message)`;
  - `class WindowsSelfInstall({bool? isWindows, bool? releaseMode, String? executablePath, String? installRoot, Map<String, String>? environment, int? pid, start, cleanUp})`
    with `Future<SelfInstallOutcome> ensureInstalled()`, `String? installRoot()` and `@visibleForTesting Future<void>? lastCleanUp`;
  - top-level `layoutRootOf(String executable)`, `sameFolder(String, String)`, `userProgramFilesFolder()`;
  - `AppNotifier({…, WindowsSelfInstall? windowsSelfInstall, void Function(int code)? exitApp})` and the field
    `final WindowsSelfInstall? windowsSelfInstall` (null off Windows, in a viewer build and under test).
- The install root is the launcher's (`HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT`, else `FOLDERID_UserProgramFiles` through
  `SHGetKnownFolderPath`, never `%LOCALAPPDATA%` text: Review Focus 5).
- Outcomes: from the install (or a build outside the layout, or not release mode), `alreadyInstalled`, and the old
  version folders are cleared in the background. From a zip folder, `relaunching`: the app logs, flushes and exits 0
  before `_startUpdateChecking` and before any provisioning; the launcher waits for it, installs (or opens a same or
  newer installed copy, saying so for an older zip) and starts the installed copy. A zip folder with no `Harness.exe`
  or a launcher that does not start is `failed(message)`: logged, and the app carries on from where it is (it works,
  but cannot update itself; the launcher's own failures are its message boxes).

    'macOS, Linux, development builds and builds outside the layout do nothing',
    () async {
      final exe = layout(zip, '1.2.3');
      expect(
        await subject(exe, isWindows: false).ensureInstalled(),
        SelfInstallOutcome.alreadyInstalled,
      );
      expect(
        await subject(exe, releaseMode: false).ensureInstalled(),
        SelfInstallOutcome.alreadyInstalled,
      );
      final built = p.join(
        dir.path,
        'build',
        'windows',
        'x64',
        'runner',
        'Release',
        'harness-desktop.exe',
      );
      expect(
        await subject(built).ensureInstalled(),
        SelfInstallOutcome.alreadyInstalled,
      );
      expect(started, isEmpty);
    },
  );

  test('a zip folder without its launcher, or a launcher that does not start, says why', () async {
    final exe = layout(zip, '1.2.3');
    File(p.join(zip, 'Harness.exe')).deleteSync();
    final missing = await subject(exe).ensureInstalled();
    expect(missing, isA<SelfInstallFailed>());
    expect(
      (missing as SelfInstallFailed).message,
      contains('has no Harness.exe'),

    layout(zip, '1.2.3');
    final refused = await subject(

      failStart: const ProcessException(

  test('the tests\' install root override is the launcher\'s', () {
    final installer = WindowsSelfInstall(
      isWindows: true,
      environment: {'HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT': install},
    );
    expect(installer.installRoot(), install);

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:harness/auth/auth_session.dart';
import 'package:harness/auth/cli_login.dart';
import 'package:harness/bootstrap/environment_provisioner.dart';

import 'package:harness/update/desktop_updater.dart';
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;

class _SignedOut extends CliLogin {
  @override
  Future<CliAuthStatus> checkStatus() async =>
      const CliAuthStatus(loggedIn: false);
}

/// Ready at once, and says whether it was asked.
class _Ready extends EnvironmentProvisioner {
  _Ready() : super(isMacOS: true);
  var asked = false;

  @override
  Future<EnvironmentReadiness> ensureReady({
    required void Function(EnvironmentReadiness value) onProgress,
    EnvironmentReadiness? resumeFrom,
    bool install = true,
    EnvironmentSetupMode? mode,
  }) async {
    asked = true;
    final ready = EnvironmentReadiness(
      steps: {
        for (final step in EnvironmentStep.values)
          step: EnvironmentStepStatus.ready,
      },
      phase: EnvironmentSetupPhase.ready,
    );
    onProgress(ready);
    return ready;
  }
}

void main() {
  late Directory dir;
  late String exe;

  setUp(() {
    dir = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('self-install-boot-');
    final zip = p.join(
      dir.path,
      'Downloads',
      'harness-desktop-1.2.3-windows-x64',
    );
    Directory(p.join(zip, 'app', '1.2.3')).createSync(recursive: true);
    exe = p.join(zip, 'app', '1.2.3', 'harness-desktop.exe');
    File(exe).writeAsStringSync('');
    File(p.join(zip, 'Harness.exe')).writeAsStringSync('');
    File(p.join(zip, 'current')).writeAsStringSync('1.2.3\r\n');
  });

  tearDown(() => dir.deleteSync(recursive: true));

  AppNotifier app({
    required _Ready provisioner,
    required List<int> exits,
    Object? failStart,
  }) => AppNotifier(
    config: AppConfig.dev,
    authSession: AuthSession(),
    configStore: null,
    environmentProvisioner: provisioner,
    cliLogin: _SignedOut(),
    desktopUpdater: DesktopUpdater(enabled: false),
    windowsSelfInstall: WindowsSelfInstall(
      isWindows: true,
      releaseMode: true,
      executablePath: exe,
      installRoot: p.join(dir.path, 'Programs', 'Harness'),
      pid: 4242,
      start: (exe, args) async {
        if (failStart != null) throw failStart;
      },
      cleanUp: (root) async {},
    ),
    exitApp: exits.add,
  );

  test('a copy run from its zip hands over and ends before anything is provisioned', () async {
    final provisioner = _Ready();
    final exits = <int>[];
    final notifier = app(provisioner: provisioner, exits: exits);
    addTearDown(notifier.dispose);
    await notifier.bootstrap();
    expect(exits, [0]);
    expect(provisioner.asked, isFalse);
    expect(notifier.status, AppStatus.bootstrapping);
  });

  test(
    'a hand-over that cannot start leaves the app running from where it is',
    () async {
      final provisioner = _Ready();
      final exits = <int>[];
      final notifier = app(
        provisioner: provisioner,
        exits: exits,
        failStart: const ProcessException('Harness.exe', [], 'denied', 5),
      );
      addTearDown(notifier.dispose);
      await notifier.bootstrap();
      expect(exits, isEmpty);
      expect(provisioner.asked, isTrue);
      expect(
        notifier.status,
        isNot(AppStatus.bootstrapping),
        reason: "boot went on to sign-in",

  );

````dart
import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:ffi';
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:ffi/ffi.dart';
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;

import '../core/runtime_platform.dart';
import '../update/windows_update_swap.dart';

/// What [WindowsSelfInstall.ensureInstalled] found.
sealed class SelfInstallOutcome {
  const SelfInstallOutcome();

  /// Running from the install (or not a packaged Windows build): carry on.
  static const alreadyInstalled = AlreadyInstalled();

  /// `Harness.exe --install` has started from the zip folder: exit now.
  static const relaunching = Relaunching();

  const factory SelfInstallOutcome.failed(String message) = SelfInstallFailed;
}

final class AlreadyInstalled extends SelfInstallOutcome {
  const AlreadyInstalled();
}

final class Relaunching extends SelfInstallOutcome {
  const Relaunching();
}

final class SelfInstallFailed extends SelfInstallOutcome {
  const SelfInstallFailed(this.message);
  final String message;
}

/// The counterpart of macOS's `MoveToApplications.swift` (desktop spec section
/// 3.3). A person extracts `harness-desktop-<ver>-windows-<arch>.zip` anywhere
/// and opens `app\<ver>\harness-desktop.exe` (or the zip's `Harness.exe`, which
/// opens it). This app, finding it is not in the per-user install
/// (`<FOLDERID_UserProgramFiles>\Harness`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Harness`),
/// starts `<zip folder>\Harness.exe --install --wait-pid <its pid>` and exits.
/// The launcher owns every install step, says what went wrong itself, and opens
/// the installed copy once this one has gone. An already-installed same or
/// newer version is the launcher's to open as well.
///
/// From the install it is [SelfInstallOutcome.alreadyInstalled], and it clears
/// what an update left behind (`WindowsUpdateSwap.cleanUp`) in the
/// background. Development builds (not in the layout, or not release mode)
/// never install themselves.
class WindowsSelfInstall {
  WindowsSelfInstall({
    bool? isWindows,
    bool? releaseMode,
    this._executablePath,
    this._installRoot,
    this._environment,
    this._pid,
    Future<void> Function(String executable, List<String> arguments)? start,
    Future<void> Function(String installRoot)? cleanUp,
  }) : _isWindows = isWindows ?? RuntimePlatform.isWindows,
       _releaseMode = releaseMode ?? kReleaseMode,
       _start = start ?? _startDetached,
       _cleanUp = cleanUp ?? _cleanUpInBackground;

  final bool _isWindows;
  final bool _releaseMode;
  final String? _executablePath;
  final String? _installRoot;
  final Map<String, String>? _environment;
  final int? _pid;
  final Future<void> Function(String executable, List<String> arguments) _start;
  final Future<void> Function(String installRoot) _cleanUp;

  /// The cleanup started by the last [ensureInstalled] from the install, for
  /// tests to wait on.
  @visibleForTesting
  Future<void>? lastCleanUp;

  static Future<void> _startDetached(
    String executable,
    List<String> arguments,
  ) => Process.start(
    executable,
    arguments,
    mode: ProcessStartMode.detached,
  ).then((_) {});

  static Future<void> _cleanUpInBackground(String installRoot) =>
      WindowsUpdateSwap(installRoot: installRoot).cleanUp();

  /// The per-user install root: the launcher's own rule
  /// (pty/src/desktop/mod.rs, `Paths`): `HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT` for
  /// tests, else the known folder, never `%LOCALAPPDATA%` text (Review Focus 5).
  String? installRoot() {
    if (_installRoot != null) return _installRoot;
    final override =
        (_environment ??
        RuntimePlatform.environment)['HARNESS_DESKTOP_INSTALL_ROOT'];
    if (override != null && override.isNotEmpty) return override;
    final programs = userProgramFilesFolder();
    return programs == null ? null : p.join(programs, 'Harness');
  }

  Future<SelfInstallOutcome> ensureInstalled() async {
    if (!_isWindows || !_releaseMode) {
      return SelfInstallOutcome.alreadyInstalled;
    }
    final exe = _executablePath ?? RuntimePlatform.resolvedExecutable;
    final here = layoutRootOf(exe);
    // Not a zip's or an install's layout: a build run from build\windows\…
    if (here == null) return SelfInstallOutcome.alreadyInstalled;
    final install = installRoot();
    if (install == null) {
      return const SelfInstallOutcome.failed(
        'Harness could not find where Windows keeps your programs, so it is running from this folder.',
      );
    }
    if (sameFolder(here, install)) {
      lastCleanUp = _cleanUp(install).catchError((Object error) {
        debugPrint('WindowsSelfInstall: cleanup failed: $error');
      });
      return SelfInstallOutcome.alreadyInstalled;
    }
    final launcher = p.join(here, WindowsUpdateSwap.launcherExe);
    if (!File(launcher).existsSync()) {
      return SelfInstallOutcome.failed(
        'This copy of Harness has no ${WindowsUpdateSwap.launcherExe} beside its app folder, so it cannot install itself. Download Harness again.',
      );
    }
    try {
      await _start(launcher, ['--install', '--wait-pid', '${_pid ?? pid}']);
      return SelfInstallOutcome.relaunching;
    } catch (error) {
      return SelfInstallOutcome.failed(
        'Harness could not start its installer ($error), so it is running from this folder.',
      );
    }
  }
}

/// `<root>` for `<root>\app\<ver>\harness-desktop.exe` beside `<root>\current`
/// and `<root>\Harness.exe`, the shape both the zip and the install have.
String? layoutRootOf(String executable) {
  if (p.basename(executable).toLowerCase() != WindowsUpdateSwap.appExe) {
    return null;
  }
  final app = p.dirname(p.dirname(executable));
  if (p.basename(app).toLowerCase() != 'app') return null;
  final root = p.dirname(app);
  return File(p.join(root, 'current')).existsSync() ? root : null;
}

/// Two folders as Windows compares them: resolved when they exist, and
/// without case or a trailing separator.
bool sameFolder(String a, String b) {
  String plain(String path) {
    var resolved = path;
    try {
      resolved = Directory(path).resolveSymbolicLinksSync();
    } on FileSystemException {
      // Not there: compared as written.
    }
    return p
        .normalize(resolved)
        .replaceAll(RegExp(r'[\\/]+$'), '')
        .toLowerCase();
  }

  return plain(a) == plain(b);
}

/// `FOLDERID_UserProgramFiles` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`), created if missing,
/// as `SHGetKnownFolderPath` gives it; null off Windows or when it fails.
String? userProgramFilesFolder() {
  if (!RuntimePlatform.isWindows) return null;
  final shell32 = DynamicLibrary.open('shell32.dll');
  final ole32 = DynamicLibrary.open('ole32.dll');
  final getPath = shell32
      .lookupFunction<
        Int32 Function(Pointer<_Guid>, Uint32, IntPtr, Pointer<Pointer<Utf16>>),
        int Function(Pointer<_Guid>, int, int, Pointer<Pointer<Utf16>>)
      >('SHGetKnownFolderPath');
  final free = ole32
      .lookupFunction<
        Void Function(Pointer<Void>),
        void Function(Pointer<Void>)
      >('CoTaskMemFree');
  final id = calloc<_Guid>();
  final out = calloc<Pointer<Utf16>>();
  try {
    // {5CD7AEE2-2219-4A67-B85D-6C9CE15660CB}
    id.ref
      ..data1 = 0x5CD7AEE2
      ..data2 = 0x2219
      ..data3 = 0x4A67;
    const tail = [0xB8, 0x5D, 0x6C, 0x9C, 0xE1, 0x56, 0x60, 0xCB];
    for (var i = 0; i < tail.length; i++) {
      id.ref.data4[i] = tail[i];
    }
    const kfFlagCreate = 0x8000;
    final hr = getPath(id, kfFlagCreate, 0, out);
    final path = hr >= 0 && out.value != nullptr
        ? out.value.toDartString()
        : null;
    free(out.value.cast());
    return path;
  } finally {
    calloc.free(id);
    calloc.free(out);
  }
}

final class _Guid extends Struct {
  @Uint32()
  external int data1;
  @Uint16()
  external int data2;
  @Uint16()
  external int data3;
  @Array(8)
  external Array<Uint8> data4;
}
````

````dart
  /// Windows, before anything is provisioned: a copy run from its zip folder
  /// hands over to `Harness.exe --install`, which installs it and opens the
  /// installed copy once this one has gone, so this one ends here. A hand-over
  /// that could not start leaves this copy running from where it is (it works
  /// there, but cannot update itself), with the reason in the log.
  Future<bool> _selfInstallTookOver() async {
    final selfInstall = windowsSelfInstall;
    if (selfInstall == null) return false;
    switch (await selfInstall.ensureInstalled()) {
      case Relaunching():
        appLog.info('setup', 'handing over to Harness.exe --install');
        flushAppLog(durable: true);
        _exitApp(0);
        return true;
      case SelfInstallFailed(:final message):
        appLog.warn('setup', message);
        return false;
      case AlreadyInstalled():
        return false;
    }
  }

### Task C4.7: Packaging and the staging release

**Files:**
- Create: `desktop/scripts/package-windows.ps1`.
- Create: `desktop/scripts/publish-desktop-windows-staging.sh` (mode 0755).
- Create: `cli/src/scripts/publishDesktopWindowsStaging.spec.ts`.
- Modify: `cli/src/scripts/windowsWorkflows.spec.ts`: one test for the desktop workflow's release mode.
- Modify: `.github/workflows/windows-desktop.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` inputs, the `concurrency` block, a `mode` job,
  `build-test`'s `needs`/`if`, and two release jobs.
- Modify: `desktop/RELEASE.md`: a "Windows (staging)" section.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the bin `harness-desktop-launcher` (C4.1); the layout `Harness.exe --install` (C4.2) and
  `WindowsUpdateSwap` (C4.5) read; B's `cli/scripts/lib/gcs.sh` (`exists`, `fetch_manifest`, `sha256_of`) and
  `cli/scripts/lib/runtimeManifest.mjs` (`entry`, `readDocument`, `mergeKey`).
- Produces:
  - `pwsh desktop/scripts/package-windows.ps1 -Version <v> -Arch x64|arm64 -Launcher <exe> [-Bundle <dir>] [-OutDir <dir>]`,
    writing `desktop/build/windows-zip/harness-desktop-<v>-windows-<arch>.zip` and printing `<zip> <sha256> <size>`;
  - `bash desktop/scripts/publish-desktop-windows-staging.sh <version> <x64 zip> <arm64 zip>` with `STAGING_PREFIX`
    (default `harness/staging`, nothing outside it), `DRY_RUN=1 DRY_RUN_OUT=<dir>`, `GCS_BUCKET`, `CDN_ASSET_BASE_URL`;
    objects `<prefix>/desktop/<version>/harness-desktop-<version>-windows-<arch>.zip`, manifest
    `<prefix>/desktop/metadata.json`, keys `desktop-windows-x64` and `desktop-windows-arm64`;
  - workflow inputs `release` (boolean), `version` (string), `dry_run` (boolean, default true); jobs `mode` (outputs
    `release`, `version`, `dry_run`), `release-build` (matrix x64/arm64, artifacts `harness-desktop-zip-windows-<arch>`)
    and `release-staging`; the artifact `harness-desktop-windows-dry-run` of a dry run;
  - the TEMPORARY branch path, until C5.3 removes it with the push trigger: a push to `feat/windows-desktop` whose head
    commit's subject is `ci(windows): desktop staging release <version>` publishes that version to staging, and
    `ci(windows): desktop staging dry run <version>` runs the release mode as a dry run.
- Version stamping: Linux writes `version.txt` because `flutter build linux` has nowhere to keep one
  (`lib/core/app_version.dart`). Windows does have one: `flutter build windows --build-name <v>` writes it into
  `harness-desktop.exe`'s version resource (`Runner.rc`'s `ProductVersion` = `FLUTTER_VERSION`), which
  `package_info_plus` reads on Windows (`ProductVersion`, split at `+`). So `runningAppVersion()` needs no Windows
  branch, and the package script refuses a bundle whose `ProductVersion` is not the version it packages. The folder
  name `app\<ver>` and `current` carry the same version.
- The staging build passes `--dart-define=HARNESS_STAGING=true` (C1.3's `kHarnessStagingBuild`). That one flag makes
  it poll the staging manifest (C4.5's `desktopUpdateMetadataUrl`) and install the staging `install.ps1` (C1.3's
  `harnessInstallScriptUrl`), so the E2E's N to N+1 runs entirely on staging. `DESKTOP_UPDATE_METADATA_URL` and
  `HARNESS_INSTALL_PS1_URL` stay test overrides and are not passed. Production is D's.
- **Ruling: how the release mode runs before merge.** `workflow_dispatch` needs the workflow file on `main`, and this
  one reaches `main` only when the PR merges, after C5's E2E has needed two staging releases. So, while the TEMPORARY
  push trigger exists, the `mode` job also reads the pushed head commit's subject (above). The commit is an empty one
  (`git commit --allow-empty`), pushed while the PR is still a draft, so PR CI runs its process checks only. A release
  run is in its own concurrency group: it never cancels a test run and is never cancelled. C5.3 removes the subject
  path with the push trigger; after the merge the release mode runs by dispatch only.
