- [ ] **Step 6: Write the Mac-side driver**

`desktop/scripts/windows-e2e/desktop-e2e.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# desktop-e2e.sh <command> [args]: the Mac side of the Windows desktop end to end (docs/testing/windows-desktop-e2e.md).
# It drives the UTM VM over SSH (admin by its key; the test user by the key first-login.sh installs), and keeps every
# password, zip and key in $E2E_WORK (git-ignored), never in the repository. What it prints is redacted (e2e_tools.py
# redact): pipe it to `tee -a "$EV/<step>.log"`. Nothing here runs the Mac's own Harness CLI or touches ~/.harness.
#
#   preflight                      the VM, its users and tasks, 1847x listeners, Winlogon, the fake CDN, staging
#   user-add [<user>]              a new standard user (password in $E2E_WORK/users.txt), its profile and key, the tools
#   push [<user>]                  the VM-side tools into the user's %USERPROFILE%\e2e and admin's e2e-desktop
#   driver [<user>]                B's PTY driver, for the user's daemon on 18473 (e2e\driver.cmd <command>)
#   kilo [<user>]                  Kilo Code for the user (npm) and npm's folder on its PATH: an engine that answers
#                                  without a sign-in, for the toast and tray checks. Before session-on.
#   session-on [<user>]            the user signed in at the VM's desktop: Winlogon autologon for one boot, a power
#                                  cycle, the desktop up, Winlogon put back, the display kept on
#   session-off [<user>]           Winlogon put back (if still set) and keep-awake stopped; the session stays
#   fetch <version> <arch> [--run <id>]   a desktop zip into $E2E_WORK/zips: from staging (checked against its
#                                  manifest), or from a workflow run's artifacts
#   put <zip> [<user>]             the zip into the user's Downloads
#   run <script.ps1> [Name=value ...]     a tool in the user's desktop session (session-run.ps1)
#   ps <script.ps1> [Name=value ...]      a tool as the user over SSH (invoke.ps1)
#   admin <script.ps1> [Name=value ...]   a tool as admin over SSH (invoke.ps1)
#   sh <cmd line> | sh-admin <cmd line>   a cmd line as the user, or as admin
#   shot <name> [Window=<process>] [Mask=x,y,w,h;...]   a screenshot of the session into $EV/<name>.png
#   state | logs [Log=... Match=... Tail=...] | procs   desktop-state.ps1, desktop-logs.ps1, desktop-procs.ps1
#   variant <no-exe|no-start> <zip> <version>   a broken build made from a good zip, for the rollback checks
#   truncated <zip>                the zip cut in half, for the download check
#   cdn-ca | cdn-stage <arch>=<zip>[@<claimed>] ... | cdn-serve | cdn-stop | cdn-on | cdn-off | cdn-status
#                                  B5.13's fake HTTPS CDN (fake-cdn.mjs, vm-cdn.ps1), serving desktop updates
#   stamp <label>                  a "# <label> <time>" line for the evidence and the time ledger
#   cleanup [<user>]               the user, its profile, the run's tasks, Winlogon, the fake CDN; then what is left
#
# VM_HOST (default 192.168.65.3), E2E_USER (default hxe2e), E2E_WORK (default .work beside this script), EV (default
# evidence/ beside it), RUN_TIMEOUT (seconds a `run` may take, default 120), E2E_RAW=1 (full ids, for a value a later
# command needs: never tee it into the evidence), UTMCTL and UTM_VM (the VM to power-cycle, default "Windows").
# Never C:\work\e2e; never the admin profile's engine settings.
#
# SC2154: zip_name, zip_url and manifest_url are set by eval, from e2e_tools.py layout. SC2016, SC2028, SC2029:
# those strings are Windows command lines, expanded on the VM and never here.
# shellcheck disable=SC2154,SC2016,SC2028,SC2029
set -euo pipefail
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
root=$(git -C "$here" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
b=$root/cli/scripts/windows-cli-e2e
host=${VM_HOST:-192.168.65.3}
work=${E2E_WORK:-$here/.work}
ev=${EV:-$here/evidence}
cdn=${FAKE_CDN_DIR:-$work/fake-cdn}
utm=${UTMCTL:-/Applications/UTM.app/Contents/MacOS/utmctl}
utm_vm=${UTM_VM:-Windows}
admin_dir=e2e-desktop
ssh_opts=(-o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=15 -o LogLevel=ERROR)
vm_tools=(invoke.ps1 session-run.ps1 screenshot.ps1 input.ps1 uia.ps1 watch-windows.ps1 start-app.ps1 clipboard.ps1
  keep-awake.ps1 stage-zip.ps1 desktop-state.ps1 desktop-logs.ps1 browser-link.ps1 parse-check.ps1 selftest.ps1 driver.cmd)
admin_tools=(invoke.ps1 session-run.ps1 winlogon.ps1 desktop-procs.ps1 cleanup.ps1 parse-check.ps1)
mkdir -p "$work" "$ev"
chmod 700 "$work"

tools() { python3 -I "$here/e2e_tools.py" "$@"; }
# OpenSSH's post-quantum notice is not evidence (B5.14 dropped it the same way).
quiet() { grep -v -e 'post-quantum' -e 'store now, decrypt later' -e 'pq.html' -e 'may need to be upgraded' || true; }
scrub() { if [ "${E2E_RAW:-}" = 1 ]; then cat; else tools redact; fi; }
vm() { ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$1@$host" "$2" 2>&1 | quiet | scrub; }
the_user() { printf '%s' "${1:-${E2E_USER:-hxe2e}}"; }
password_of() { if [ -f "$work/users.txt" ]; then awk -v u="$1" '$1 == u { print $2 }' "$work/users.txt"; fi; }
stamp() { echo "# $* $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z')"; }

put_files() {
  local who=$1 dir=$2
  shift 2
  ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$who@$host" "if not exist $dir mkdir $dir" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  scp -q "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$@" "$who@$host:$dir/"
}

push_admin() {
  local files=() f
  for f in "${admin_tools[@]}"; do files+=("$here/$f"); done
  put_files admin "$admin_dir" "${files[@]}" "$b/vm-cdn.ps1"
}

push() {
  local u files=() f
  u=$(the_user "${1:-}")
  for f in "${vm_tools[@]}"; do files+=("$here/$f"); done
  put_files "$u" e2e "${files[@]}"
  push_admin
  echo "tools copied to $u's %USERPROFILE%\\e2e and admin's %USERPROFILE%\\$admin_dir"
}

# A tool in <who>'s <dir>, through invoke.ps1: its parameters travel as base64 JSON, never through cmd's quoting.
invoke() {
  local who=$1 dir=$2 script=$3 encoded
  shift 3
  encoded=$(tools args-b64 "$@")
  vm "$who" "powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $dir\\invoke.ps1 -Script $script -ArgsB64 $encoded"
}

# A tool of the user's e2e folder, inside its desktop session. RUN_TIMEOUT bounds it; NO_WAIT=1 leaves it running.
session() {
  local u=$1 script=$2 inner
  shift 2
  inner=$(tools args-b64 "$@")
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # an unset NO_WAIT must add no argument at all
  invoke admin "$admin_dir" session-run.ps1 "User=$u" "Script=$script" "ArgsB64=$inner" "TimeoutSec=${RUN_TIMEOUT:-120}" ${NO_WAIT:+NoWait=true}
}

has_session() { E2E_RAW=1 invoke admin "$admin_dir" session-run.ps1 "User=$1" Probe=true >/dev/null 2>&1; }

preflight() {
  local listeners
  stamp preflight
  push_admin >/dev/null
  echo '## the VM'
  vm admin 'ver & whoami & hostname'
  vm admin 'powershell -NoProfile -Command "(Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).Caption; $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE; (Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).NumberOfLogicalProcessors"'
  echo '## listeners on 1847x (the desktop app supervises 127.0.0.1:18473, so it must be free)'
  listeners=$(vm admin 'netstat -ano | findstr LISTENING | findstr :1847' || true)
  echo "${listeners:-none}"
  echo '## local users'
  vm admin 'net user'
  echo '## Harness and run tasks'
  vm admin 'schtasks /Query /FO LIST | findstr /C:"Harness" /C:"HxDesktopE2E" || echo none'
  echo '## C:\work\e2e (never opened by this run)'
  vm admin 'if exist C:\work\e2e (echo present) else (echo absent)'
  echo '## Winlogon'
  invoke admin "$admin_dir" winlogon.ps1 Status=true
  echo '## fake CDN (B5.13)'
  invoke admin "$admin_dir" vm-cdn.ps1 Status=true
  echo '## staging: the desktop manifest, and the CLI the app installs'
  eval "$(tools layout 0.0.0 arm64)"
  curl -fsS "$manifest_url" 2>&1 | scrub || echo "no desktop manifest at $manifest_url"
  curl -fsS https://storage.googleapis.com/s3-autonomous-upgrade-3/harness/staging/cli/metadata.json | grep '"version"' || echo 'no staging CLI manifest'
  if printf '%s\n' "$listeners" | grep -q ':18473 '; then
    echo 'STOP: something listens on 18473, and the app would talk to it. Do not stop it from this run: ask the owner.' >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

user_add() {
  local u pw script encoded
  u=$(the_user "${1:-}")
  [[ "$u" =~ ^hx[a-z0-9]*$ ]] || { echo "error: a test user's name is hx followed by letters or digits (cleanup.ps1 refuses any other)" >&2; return 2; }
  [ -z "$(password_of "$u")" ] || { echo "error: $u is in $work/users.txt already: run cleanup $u first" >&2; return 1; }
  stamp "user-add $u"
  pw=$(openssl rand -base64 18 | tr -d '/+=')
  ( umask 077; printf '%s %s\n' "$u" "$pw" >> "$work/users.txt" )
  script="if (Get-LocalUser -Name '$u' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { throw 'the user $u exists already' }
\$p = ConvertTo-SecureString '$pw' -AsPlainText -Force
New-LocalUser -Name '$u' -Password \$p -PasswordNeverExpires -AccountNeverExpires -Description 'Harness desktop end to end (throwaway)' | Out-Null
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group Users -Member '$u'
'created $u, a standard user'"
  encoded=$(printf '%s' "$script" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-16LE | base64 | tr -d '\n')
  vm admin "powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand $encoded"
  "$b/first-login.sh" "$u" "$pw" 2>&1 | grep -v -i -e 'password' -e 'spawn ssh' | quiet
  if vm admin 'net localgroup Administrators' | tr -d '\r' | grep -qix "$u"; then echo "error: $u is an administrator" >&2; return 1; fi
  push "$u"
  vm "$u" 'whoami & echo %USERPROFILE%'
}

driver() {
  local u
  u=$(the_user "${1:-}")
  "$root/cli/scripts/windows-pty-e2e/build.sh" "$work" >/dev/null
  put_files "$u" e2e "$work/e2e.mjs" "$b/run.cmd" "$here/driver.cmd"
  vm "$u" 'e2e\driver.cmd list' || true
}

kilo() {
  local u ps encoded
  u=$(the_user "${1:-}")
  # npm's per-user folder on the user PATH, raw (REG_EXPAND_SZ), as B5.14 did; read by the sessions that start later.
  ps='$key = "HKCU:\Environment"
$raw = [string](Get-Item -LiteralPath $key).GetValue("Path", "", "DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames")
if ($raw -notmatch "(?i)%APPDATA%\\npm") {
  $new = if ($raw) { $raw.TrimEnd(";") + ";%APPDATA%\npm" } else { "%APPDATA%\npm" }
  Set-ItemProperty -LiteralPath $key -Name Path -Value $new -Type ExpandString
}
"user PATH: " + [string](Get-Item -LiteralPath $key).GetValue("Path", "", "DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames")'
  encoded=$(printf '%s' "$ps" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-16LE | base64 | tr -d '\n')
  vm "$u" "powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand $encoded"
  vm "$u" 'npm install -g --allow-scripts=@kilocode/cli @kilocode/cli'
  vm "$u" '"%APPDATA%\npm\kilo.cmd" --version'
}

session_on() {
  local u pw
  u=$(the_user "${1:-}")
  pw=$(password_of "$u")
  [ -n "$pw" ] || { echo "error: no password for $u in $work/users.txt (user-add makes one)" >&2; return 1; }
  stamp "session-on $u"
  push_admin >/dev/null
  if has_session "$u"; then
    echo "$u is signed in at the desktop already"
  else
    trap 'echo "Winlogon may still hold the test autologon: run desktop-e2e.sh session-off once the VM answers" >&2' EXIT
    invoke admin "$admin_dir" winlogon.ps1 Enable=true "User=$u" "PasswordB64=$(printf '%s' "$pw" | base64)"
    echo "power cycle, as B5.14 did (a warm reboot hangs this VM in UTM's firmware): $(date '+%H:%M:%S')"
    vm admin 'shutdown /s /t 0' || true
    for _ in $(seq 1 60); do "$utm" status "$utm_vm" 2>/dev/null | grep -qi stopped && break; sleep 3; done
    "$utm" start "$utm_vm"
    for _ in $(seq 1 100); do ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "admin@$host" 'echo up' >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 3; done
    echo "SSH answers: $(date '+%H:%M:%S')"
    for _ in $(seq 1 60); do has_session "$u" && break; sleep 5; done
    invoke admin "$admin_dir" session-run.ps1 "User=$u" Probe=true
    echo "desktop up: $(date '+%H:%M:%S')"
  fi
  invoke admin "$admin_dir" winlogon.ps1 Disable=true
  trap - EXIT
  NO_WAIT=1 session "$u" keep-awake.ps1
  E2E_USER=$u shot session-on
}

session_off() {
  local u
  u=$(the_user "${1:-}")
  stamp "session-off $u"
  invoke admin "$admin_dir" winlogon.ps1 Disable=true
  if has_session "$u"; then RUN_TIMEOUT=30 session "$u" keep-awake.ps1 Stop=true; fi
}

fetch() {
  local version=${1:?usage: fetch <version> <x64|arm64> [--run <id>]} arch=${2:?usage: fetch <version> <x64|arm64> [--run <id>]}
  local run_id='' out found
  if [ "${3:-}" = --run ]; then run_id=${4:?--run needs a workflow run id}; fi
  eval "$(tools layout "$version" "$arch")"
  mkdir -p "$work/zips"
  out=$work/zips/$zip_name
  stamp "fetch $zip_name${run_id:+ from run $run_id}"
  if [ -n "$run_id" ]; then
    rm -rf "${work:?}/runs/$run_id"
    mkdir -p "$work/runs/$run_id"
    gh run download "$run_id" --pattern 'harness-desktop-*' --dir "$work/runs/$run_id"
    found=$(find "$work/runs/$run_id" -type f -name "$zip_name" | head -1)
    if [ -z "$found" ]; then
      echo "error: run $run_id has no $zip_name; its zips:" >&2
      find "$work/runs/$run_id" -type f -name '*.zip' >&2
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$found" "$out"
    gh run view "$run_id" --json url,headSha,conclusion,displayTitle
  else
    curl -fsS -o "$out" "$zip_url"
    curl -fsS -o "$work/zips/metadata.json" "$manifest_url"
    tools verify "$work/zips/metadata.json" "$arch" "$out"
  fi
  echo "$out"
  shasum -a 256 "$out" | scrub
  tools zip-info "$out"
}

put() {
  local zip=${1:?usage: put <zip> [<user>]} u
  u=$(the_user "${2:-}")
  put_files "$u" Downloads "$zip"
  echo "copied $(basename "$zip") to $u's Downloads"
}

shot() {
  local name=${1:?usage: shot <name> [Window=<process>] [Mask=x,y,w,h;...]} u
  shift
  u=$(the_user "")
  session "$u" screenshot.ps1 "Out=shots\\$name.png" "$@"
  scp -q "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$u@$host:e2e/shots/$name.png" "$ev/$name.png"
  echo "evidence: ${ev#"$root"/}/$name.png (look at it before committing it: no email, machine name, QR or code)"
}

cdn_ca() { FAKE_CDN_DIR=$cdn "$b/fake-cdn.sh" make-ca; }
cdn_stage() { tools cdn-stage "$cdn/root" "$@"; }
cdn_serve() {
  [ -f "$cdn/ca/leaf.pem" ] || { echo "error: no certificate: run cdn-ca" >&2; return 1; }
  [ -d "$cdn/root" ] || { echo "error: nothing staged: run cdn-stage" >&2; return 1; }
  if [ -f "$cdn/serve.pid" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$cdn/serve.pid")" 2>/dev/null; then echo "the fake CDN runs already (pid $(cat "$cdn/serve.pid"))"; return 0; fi
  nohup node "$b/fake-cdn.mjs" serve --root "$cdn/root" --cert "$cdn/ca/leaf.pem" --key "$cdn/ca/leaf.key" \
    --bind "${VM_BIND:-192.168.65.1}" --port 443 --http-port 0 > "$cdn/serve.log" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "$cdn/serve.pid"
  sleep 1
  cat "$cdn/serve.log"
}
cdn_stop() {
  if [ -f "$cdn/serve.pid" ]; then kill "$(cat "$cdn/serve.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f "$cdn/serve.pid"; echo 'fake CDN stopped; what it served:'; scrub < "$cdn/serve.log"; else echo 'the fake CDN is not running'; fi
}
cdn_on() { put_files admin "$admin_dir" "$cdn/ca/fake-cdn-ca.pem" "$b/vm-cdn.ps1"; invoke admin "$admin_dir" vm-cdn.ps1 Enable=true; }
cdn_off() { invoke admin "$admin_dir" vm-cdn.ps1 Disable=true; }
cdn_status() { invoke admin "$admin_dir" vm-cdn.ps1 Status=true; }

cleanup() {
  local u
  u=$(the_user "${1:-}")
  stamp "cleanup $u"
  push_admin >/dev/null
  if has_session "$u"; then RUN_TIMEOUT=30 session "$u" keep-awake.ps1 Stop=true || true; fi
  if E2E_RAW=1 invoke admin "$admin_dir" vm-cdn.ps1 Status=true | grep -q '^enabled at'; then cdn_off; fi
  [ -f "$cdn/serve.pid" ] && cdn_stop
  invoke admin "$admin_dir" cleanup.ps1 "User=$u"
  vm admin "rmdir /s /q %USERPROFILE%\\$admin_dir && echo admin's $admin_dir folder removed"
  echo '## this Mac'
  if [ -f "$work/users.txt" ]; then
    grep -v "^$u " "$work/users.txt" > "$work/users.txt.new" || true
    mv "$work/users.txt.new" "$work/users.txt"
    [ -s "$work/users.txt" ] || rm -f "$work/users.txt"
  fi
  echo "the password of $u is gone from $work"
  rm -rf "${cdn:?}/ca" && echo "the fake CDN's CA and keys removed"
  if lsof -nP -iTCP:443 -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'something still listens on 443 here: look at it'; else echo 'nothing listens on 443 here'; fi
}

command=${1:-}
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
case "$command" in
  preflight) preflight ;;
  user-add) user_add "$@" ;;
  push) push "$@" ;;
  driver) driver "$@" ;;
  kilo) kilo "$@" ;;
  session-on) session_on "$@" ;;
  session-off) session_off "$@" ;;
  fetch) fetch "$@" ;;
  put) put "$@" ;;
  run)
    script=${1:?usage: run <script.ps1> [Name=value ...]}
    shift
    put_files "$(the_user "")" e2e "$here/$script"
    session "$(the_user "")" "$script" "$@" ;;
  ps)
    script=${1:?usage: ps <script.ps1> [Name=value ...]}
    shift
    put_files "$(the_user "")" e2e "$here/$script"
    invoke "$(the_user "")" e2e "$script" "$@" ;;
  admin)
    script=${1:?usage: admin <script.ps1> [Name=value ...]}
    shift
    put_files admin "$admin_dir" "$here/$script"
    invoke admin "$admin_dir" "$script" "$@" ;;
  sh) vm "$(the_user "")" "${1:?usage: sh <cmd line>}" ;;
  sh-admin) vm admin "${1:?usage: sh-admin <cmd line>}" ;;
  shot) shot "$@" ;;
  state)
    put_files "$(the_user "")" e2e "$here/desktop-state.ps1"
    if has_session "$(the_user "")"; then session "$(the_user "")" desktop-state.ps1 "$@"; else invoke "$(the_user "")" e2e desktop-state.ps1 "$@"; fi ;;
  logs) invoke "$(the_user "")" e2e desktop-logs.ps1 "$@" ;;
  procs) invoke admin "$admin_dir" desktop-procs.ps1 "User=$(the_user "")" ;;
  variant) tools zip-variant "${1:?usage: variant <no-exe|no-start> <zip> <version>}" "${2:?}" "${3:?}" --out-dir "$work/zips" ;;
  truncated) tools truncate "${1:?usage: truncated <zip>}" --out-dir "$work/zips/truncated" ;;
  cdn-ca) cdn_ca ;;
  cdn-stage) cdn_stage "$@" ;;
  cdn-serve) cdn_serve ;;
  cdn-stop) cdn_stop ;;
  cdn-on) cdn_on ;;
  cdn-off) cdn_off ;;
  cdn-status) cdn_status ;;
  stamp) stamp "$@" ;;
  cleanup) cleanup "$@" ;;
  *) sed -n '2,31p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
```

Then `chmod +x desktop/scripts/windows-e2e/desktop-e2e.sh desktop/scripts/windows-e2e/e2e_tools.py`.

checked by `parse-check.ps1` and the step that failed. The selftest's probe must say `probe: seen`. If it does not,
the console detector is broken, and C5.2's no-flash check would be blind.

### Task C5.2: The seven scenarios on the VM, and `docs/testing/windows-desktop-e2e.md`

**Files:**
- Create: `docs/testing/windows-desktop-e2e.md`
- Create: `desktop/scripts/windows-e2e/evidence/<step>.log` and `<name>.png` (one per step below; redacted; every
  screenshot reviewed and masked before commit)
- Modify: only through a fix found during the run. Each fix is its own commit with a test that fails without it, in
  the file of the phase that owns it (header file map). Then the scenario runs again.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - C5.1's tools.
  - C1–C4 on this branch.
  - C4's staging release mode, run twice: version N, then N1 = N's X.Y.(Z+1). It publishes
    `harness/staging/desktop/<ver>/harness-desktop-<ver>-windows-{x64,arm64}.zip` and the manifest entries.
  - A staging build reads the staging desktop manifest (its `DESKTOP_UPDATE_METADATA_URL`) and installs the CLI from
    `…/harness/staging/cli/install.ps1`.
  - The staging CLI (`harness/staging/cli/metadata.json`) is at least C1.3's `kMinimumWindowsHarnessCliVersion`.
- Produces: the E2E doc. Its sections: summary table, setup recipe, each scenario's steps, evidence and timings,
  the Mac half, fixes, findings G1…, known limits, safety rules and clean-up.

**Who checks what.** Every check below is tagged:
- **Script** runs unattended: logs, files, registry, process lists, the PTY driver's screen;
- **UIA** is driven by `uia.ps1` and `input.ps1`, and is seen in a screenshot;
- **Person** needs the owner, at the VM's screen (UTM's window) or at the Mac. The executor asks, waits, and records
  what the person reports.

When a UIA step cannot find its control (a name differs, or Flutter exposes no semantics for it), it falls back to a
person. The doc records which way each check ran.

Record the wall-clock time of every step (`$D stamp <label> | tee -a "$SCR/c5-times.log"` at each start and end).
The doc reports these separately (AGENTS.md):
- implementation (fixes);
- validation;
- waiting (CI builds, the 5-minute update poll, power cycles);
- writing.

- [ ] **Step 6: Scenario 4, update N → N1, and broken builds roll back**

A terminal keeps counting through every app update. App updates never touch the daemon or its agents:

```bash

CID=<its id>
$D sh "e2e\\driver.cmd type $CID \"1..100000 | % { 'COUNT_' + \$_; Start-Sleep 1 }\r\" 3000" | tee "$EV/s4-before.log"
$D state | tee -a "$EV/s4-before.log"
$D procs | tee -a "$EV/s4-before.log"
```

N1 through the real staging manifest (spec §4.4 item 4, the first choice):

```bash
N1=<N with Z+1>
git commit --allow-empty -m "ci(windows): desktop staging release $N1" -m "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
git push origin feat/windows-desktop      # C4.7's TEMPORARY subject path, as in Step 1
sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

gh run watch "$R2" --exit-status
$D fetch "$N1" arm64 | tee "$EV/s4-offer.log"
$D fetch "$N1" x64 | tee -a "$EV/s4-offer.log"

# A check runs at start and then every 5 minutes: restart the app instead of waiting
$D run uia.ps1 Root=Tray "Find=Harness*" Do=RightClick && $D run uia.ps1 Root=Menu "Find=Quit*" Do=Invoke
sleep 5
$D run start-app.ps1 'Path=%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Harness.lnk' | tee -a "$EV/s4-offer.log"
RUN_TIMEOUT=360 $D run uia.ps1 Find=Update Type=Button Do=Exists TimeoutSec=330 | tee -a "$EV/s4-offer.log"

$D run uia.ps1 Find=Update Type=Button Do=Invoke | tee -a "$EV/s4-update.log"

sleep 15
$D stamp "s4 N1 running" | tee -a "$EV/s4-update.log"

$D logs Log=launch | tee -a "$EV/s4-update.log"

# The next start removes every app\* except current and previous

sleep 5; $D run start-app.ps1 'Path=%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Harness.lnk'
$D state | tee "$EV/s4-cleanup.log"
```

The broken builds come from the fake HTTPS CDN (B5.13) only. They are never published, not even to staging. Each is
strictly newer than N1, because the updater takes only a newer version:

```bash
Z1=${N1##*.}; XY=${N1%.*}
N2=$XY.$((Z1 + 1)); N3=$XY.$((Z1 + 2)); N4=$XY.$((Z1 + 3))
GOOD=$E2E_WORK/zips/harness-desktop-$N1-windows-arm64.zip
$D variant no-exe "$GOOD" "$N2" | tee "$EV/s4-broken.log"
$D variant no-start "$GOOD" "$N3" | tee -a "$EV/s4-broken.log"
$D variant no-exe "$GOOD" "$N4" | tee -a "$EV/s4-broken.log"
$D truncated "$E2E_WORK/zips/harness-desktop-$N4-windows-arm64.zip" | tee -a "$EV/s4-broken.log"
$D cdn-ca | tee "$EV/s4-cdn.log"
$D cdn-stage "arm64=$E2E_WORK/zips/truncated/harness-desktop-$N4-windows-arm64.zip@$E2E_WORK/zips/harness-desktop-$N4-windows-arm64.zip" | tee -a "$EV/s4-cdn.log"
$D cdn-serve | tee -a "$EV/s4-cdn.log"
$D cdn-on | tee -a "$EV/s4-cdn.log"
```

Each broken build is offered in turn, each time by restarting the app (as above), checking for the offer, then
`Update`:

1. **N4, a download cut short.** Pass: the app log says the download did not match its size or sha256; `current`
   stays N1; nothing is extracted (no `app\<N4>`, no `*.staging`). Evidence: `s4-truncated.log`,
   `s4-truncated.png`.
2. **N2, no executable.**

   ```bash
   $D cdn-stage "arm64=$E2E_WORK/zips/harness-desktop-$N2-windows-arm64.zip" | tee "$EV/s4-no-exe.log"
   ```

   Then restart, offer and `Update`. Pass, either way:
   - the updater refuses the build before the swap (its sentence is in the app log, and `current` stays N1);
   - or the launcher, finding no `harness-desktop.exe` in `app\<N2>`, switches `current` back to N1, writes the
     reason to `launch.log`, and N1's window comes up.

   The person never sees a broken app. Record which of the two happened.
3. **N3, an app that exits at once.**

   ```bash
   $D cdn-stage "arm64=$E2E_WORK/zips/harness-desktop-$N3-windows-arm64.zip" | tee "$EV/s4-no-start.log"
   ```

   Then restart, offer and `Update`. The updated app exits before its first frame. Start it again the way a person
   would, through the shortcut, until a window shows or three starts have been made:

   ```bash
   for i in 1 2 3; do
     $D run start-app.ps1 'Path=%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Harness.lnk' WaitSec=20 | tee -a "$EV/s4-no-start.log"
     $D state | grep -E "current:|previous:|app\\\\$N3" | tee -a "$EV/s4-no-start.log"
     $D state | grep -q "current: '$N1'" && break
   done
   $D logs Log=launch | tee -a "$EV/s4-no-start.log"
   ```

   Pass: `current` names N3 for at most two starts. Then the launcher switches to N1 and logs why
   (`two starts … without .started`). `app\<N3>` has no `.started`, and N1's window comes up.

Then:

```bash
$D cdn-off | tee "$EV/s4-cdn-off.log"          # hosts byte-identical, the CA gone
$D cdn-stop | tee -a "$EV/s4-cdn-off.log"
$D sh "e2e\\driver.cmd screen $CID" | tee "$EV/s4-after.log"
$D sh 'e2e\driver.cmd list' | tee -a "$EV/s4-after.log"
$D procs | tee -a "$EV/s4-after.log"
```

Pass, scenario 4:
- **N → N1:**
  - the offer showed `Update`, and after the click N1's window came up;
  - `current: '<N1>'`, `previous: '<N>'`, and `app\<N1>: … .started written …`;
  - About (Harness ▸ About Harness) shows N1;
  - record the time from `s4 Update clicked` to `s4 N1 running`.

```markdown
# Windows desktop: end-to-end results

Date: <date>. Branch `feat/windows-desktop` at `<sha>` (fixes `<sha>`, … made during the run). Builds `<N>` and
`<N1>` from the staging release mode ([run <R1>](<url>), [run <R2>](<url>)), downloaded from
`https://cdn.autonomous.ai/harness/staging/desktop/<ver>/`. The CLI the app installed is staging's `<cli version>`.
The broken `<N2>` (no executable), `<N3>` (exits before its first frame) and `<N4>` (download cut short) were made
from N1's zip and served from the Mac's fake HTTPS CDN (B5.13). They were never published. This is Task C5.2 of the
plan; the spec's section is
[§4.4](../superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-windows-desktop-design.md#44-end-to-end-on-the-windows-11-arm64-vm).

**How it was driven.** The UTM VM: <edition, build, CPUs, computer name>. A new standard user, `hxe2e`, reached
over SSH by key, signed in at the VM's desktop by Winlogon autologon for one boot (B5.14's test-only exception),
restored at once. Every check in the desktop session ran as a one-shot interactive scheduled task, through a
windowless launcher (`desktop/scripts/windows-e2e/session-run.ps1`, `hxrun.exe`), so the tooling itself never put a
console on the screen it checked. Controls were found by Windows UI Automation (`uia.ps1`), and screenshots were
taken in the session. The PTY driver (`cli/scripts/windows-pty-e2e`, through `driver.cmd`) read terminals on the
user's daemon on 18473. Nothing on the Mac ran the Mac's Harness CLI or touched its `~/.harness` or daemon; the
Mac half was the owner's.

**Who checked what.** **Script**: unattended. **UIA**: driven by UI Automation and seen in a screenshot.
**Person**: the owner, at the VM's screen or the Mac. Each row below says which.

**Evidence.** [`desktop/scripts/windows-e2e/evidence/`](../../desktop/scripts/windows-e2e/evidence/), one log or
screenshot per step: `preflight`, `users`, `session`, `s1-*` … `s6-*`, `mac-half`, `cleanup`. Ids are in their short
form. No email, token, sign-in code or QR code is in them; screenshots were masked or left out (listed under Known
limits).

**Time (Mac clock, +07).** Implementation (fixes during the run) <minutes>. Validation <start–end>, of which waiting
<minutes> (CI builds of N and N1, the power cycle, update polls). Writing this document <minutes>. No merge or

## Safety rules

- The run used a throwaway standard user, `hx…`, never an administrator. `cleanup.ps1` refuses any other name.
- `C:\work\e2e` was never opened. Its daemon was not running before or after (`preflight`, `cleanup`).
- Port 18473 was checked free before the run. Another user's daemon there would have stopped the run: it is not
  this run's to stop or use.
- Nothing was read from or copied out of the admin profile. No engine settings of any profile but `hxe2e`'s were
  written.
- HKLM Winlogon was the one machine-wide change outside the fake CDN, and it was test only:
  - it was saved first and set for one boot;
  - it was restored exactly as soon as the desktop was up (`restored exactly: True`);
  - the script refuses to run when a real autologon (a stored DefaultPassword) exists.
- The hosts file and the fake CDN's CA were in place for scenario 4 only, through B's `vm-cdn.ps1`. Afterwards the
  hosts file was byte-identical and the CA was gone.
- No broken build was published. Staging got only the two good builds.
- Nothing on the Mac ran the Mac's Harness CLI, app or daemon, or read its `~/.harness`. The sign-in was the owner's,
  on the VM. The machine it registered was deleted from the VM's own CLI.
- Evidence: passwords, zips and keys stayed in the session scratchpad; logs were redacted (`e2e_tools.py redact`);
  every screenshot was reviewed and masked before commit.
```

### Task C5.3: macOS and Linux unchanged, the TEMPORARY trigger removed, the PR's record

**Files:**
- Modify: `.github/workflows/windows-desktop.yml` (remove the TEMPORARY `push:` trigger and C4.7's TEMPORARY subject
  path, nothing else)
- Test: `cli/src/scripts/windowsWorkflows.spec.ts` (one new case)
- No other repository file. The suite comparison and the PR text use the scratchpad and `gh`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - C5.1's `e2e_tools.py compare-runs <base receipt> <head receipt>`;
  - `scripts/test-desktop.py` (`make desktop-test`), which writes `.harness/validation/<time>-desktop-<pid>/receipt.json`
    and prints `<status>: <receipt path>`;
  - C1.4's TEMPORARY block, in B's three-line form (`windows.yml`):

    ```yaml
      # TEMPORARY: remove before merging (workflow_dispatch needs the file on main)
      push:
        branches: [feat/windows-desktop]
    ```

  - C4.7's TEMPORARY subject path: the `mode` job's lines that end in `# TEMPORARY`, and the
    `(inputs.release || startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'ci(windows): desktop staging '))` term of the
    `concurrency` block, twice.

- Produces: the workflow with `workflow_dispatch` only (C4.7 adds no `workflow_call`), its release mode chosen by the
  dispatch inputs alone; the PR body's Validation section.

Order. Remove the trigger first, because it is the last change to the head. Push once. While PR CI runs on that
head, run the macOS comparison and the diff check. Then read CI, and record everything in the PR. Once the trigger is
gone, the workflow cannot be dispatched from the branch until merge (it needs the file on `main`), so this task
starts only after C5.2's Windows runs are done.

- [ ] **Step 3: Remove the trigger**

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib, re
p = pathlib.Path('.github/workflows/windows-desktop.yml')
s = p.read_text()
# C1.4's push trigger, three lines.
new = re.sub(r'\n[ \t]*# TEMPORARY[^\n]*\n[ \t]*push:\n[ \t]*branches: \[feat/windows-desktop\]\n', '\n', s)
assert new != s, 'the TEMPORARY push trigger is not in its three-line form: remove it by hand, and nothing else'
# C4.7's subject path: every line of the mode job that ends in `# TEMPORARY`.
lines = new.split('\n')
kept = [line for line in lines if not line.rstrip().endswith('# TEMPORARY')]
assert len(lines) - len(kept) == 6, f'expected six TEMPORARY lines in the mode job, found {len(lines) - len(kept)}'
new = '\n'.join(kept)
# ... and its term in the concurrency block, twice.
term = "(inputs.release || startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'ci(windows): desktop staging '))"
assert new.count(term) == 2, 'the concurrency block is not as C4.7 wrote it: edit it by hand'
new = new.replace('!' + term, '!inputs.release').replace(term, 'inputs.release')
# The mode job's comment about the subject path.
comment = (
    "  # section 3.6). On workflow_dispatch the inputs decide. The lines marked TEMPORARY go with the push trigger before\n"
    "  # merging: until this file is on main it cannot be dispatched, so a push whose head commit's subject is\n"
    "  # `ci(windows): desktop staging release <version>` runs the release mode and publishes, and\n"
    "  # `ci(windows): desktop staging dry run <version>` runs it as a dry run.\n"
)
assert new.count(comment) == 1, "the mode job's comment is not as C4.7 wrote it: edit it by hand"
new = new.replace(comment, "  # section 3.6). The dispatch inputs decide.\n")
p.write_text(new)
PY
git diff -- .github/workflows/windows-desktop.yml
actionlint .github/workflows/windows-desktop.yml
grep -n 'TEMPORARY' .github/workflows/*.yml || echo 'no TEMPORARY trigger left'
```

Expected:
- the diff removes the three trigger lines and the mode job's six `# TEMPORARY` lines, shortens its comment, and turns

- `actionlint` prints nothing;
- the last line is `no TEMPORARY trigger left`.

- [ ] **Step 7: The full desktop suite on macOS, head and base, side by side**

The base runs in its own worktree, never by stashing (repo rule). The two suites run at the same time on half the
workers each, within the machine's capacity:

```bash
git worktree add --detach "$SCR/c5-base" "$BASE"
(cd "$SCR/c5-base/desktop" && flutter pub get >/dev/null)
(cd desktop && flutter pub get >/dev/null)
W=$(( $(sysctl -n hw.ncpu) * 3 / 8 )); [ "$W" -ge 1 ] || W=1
$D stamp "C5.3 suites start" | tee -a "$SCR/c5-times.log"
( make -C "$SCR/c5-base" desktop-test ARGS="--workers $W --timeout 2400" > "$SCR/c5-base.out" 2>&1; echo "exit $?" >> "$SCR/c5-base.out" ) &
( make desktop-test ARGS="--workers $W --timeout 2400" > "$SCR/c5-head.out" 2>&1; echo "exit $?" >> "$SCR/c5-head.out" ) &
wait
$D stamp "C5.3 suites end" | tee -a "$SCR/c5-times.log"
BASE_RECEIPT=$(grep -Eo '/[^ ]+/receipt\.json' "$SCR/c5-base.out" | tail -1)
HEAD_RECEIPT=$(grep -Eo '/[^ ]+/receipt\.json' "$SCR/c5-head.out" | tail -1)
tail -3 "$SCR/c5-base.out" "$SCR/c5-head.out"
python3 -I desktop/scripts/windows-e2e/e2e_tools.py compare-runs "$BASE_RECEIPT" "$HEAD_RECEIPT" | tee "$SCR/c5-compare.txt"
```

Expected:
- both runs end with `failed: …/receipt.json` (the base has known failures, about 26 on 2026-09-25, and that set
  changes week to week) or `passed: …`;
- `c5-compare.txt` ends `verdict: no regressions`;
- its `removed tests` are only the moved menu-bar tests: each `test/linux_menu_bar_test.dart :: <name>` has a
  matching `new tests` line in C3's `in_window_menu_bar_test.dart`, which pins Linux's output.

If it says `REGRESSIONS`:
1. Run each newly failing file alone, on both trees:
   `make desktop-test ARGS="test/<file>_test.dart"`, and `make -C "$SCR/c5-base" desktop-test ARGS="…"`.
2. A test that passes alone on head and also flips on base is flaky. It is recorded as such in the PR, with both runs.
3. A test that fails on head and passes on base is a regression. The task whose file it is fixes it, with its own
   commit. Then that file is compared again, and the full suite is not rerun.

A test file the runner lists as an unverified file is a failure too: look for `"type":"error"` in its log (memory:
the runner can list a real failure that way). Then remove the worktree:

```bash
git worktree remove --force "$SCR/c5-base"
```

### Phase C5 rulings

- **The desktop session** comes from HKLM Winlogon autologon for one boot, restored as soon as the desktop is up. Every in-session check runs as an interactive scheduled task. This is the one test-only HKLM change, as in B5.14.
- **`winlogon.ps1 -Enable` refuses** when a `DefaultPassword` is already stored.
- **In-session tools run through `hxrun.exe`**, a GUI program, so the no-flash check is not blinded by its own console.
- **18473 must be free on the VM**, or the run stops and asks. The daemon there would not be this run's, and must not be stopped or used. The app would follow the test user's recorded port (C2.3), but B's PTY driver and this run's checks assume 18473.
- **The sign-in is the owner's**, in the app on the VM. B's `approve-qr.mts` is not used, because it reads the Mac's real `~/.harness`.
- **Staging releases (reconciliation).** N and N1 are published through C4.7's TEMPORARY subject path (`ci(windows): desktop staging release <version>`), one empty commit each, while the PR is a draft. Broken builds go only through the fake CDN, never staging.
- **Broken builds** are made by editing N1's zip: the version folder renamed, `current` rewritten, and the exe or `data\app.so` dropped. A cut copy served under the full zip's sha256 and size is the truncated-zip case.
- **The Mac-side helpers** are Python standard library, tested with `python3 -m unittest`, run locally and recorded in the PR.
- **`compare-runs`** counts a new failing test as a regression and lists a removed test without failing, since the menu-bar rename moves tests between files.
- **The uninstall check** expects every `desktop-app*` folder gone (the app writes `desktop-app-v2`), and the rest of `.harness` kept.
- **Screenshots** showing an email, a name, a QR code or a sign-in code are masked (`screenshot.ps1 -Mask`) or left out: the repository is public.
- **C5.3 removes** the TEMPORARY push trigger and C4.7's subject path, and nothing else in the workflow. Its test pins both.
